name: ABSA, the pressure equipment safety authority — Quality Management System Certificate of Authorization Permit for Integrity Assessment Organizations (AB-515)
authority: ABSA, the pressure equipment safety authority (originally incorporated as the Alberta Boilers Safety Association; a Delegated Administrative Organization under the Boilers Delegated Administration Regulation, Alta. Reg. 32/2002, administering the Safety Codes Act)
appliesTo: Any person or organization providing in-service pressure equipment integrity assessment services in Alberta and certifying the results, plus firms constructing, repairing or altering boilers, pressure vessels, pressure piping and fittings, or servicing pressure relief valves. Owner-users may be directed in writing to hold their own permit. Organizations located outside Canada are not required to hold an ABSA permit but must satisfy ASME and National Board stamping requirements instead.
summary: ABSA requires an inspection firm performing in-service integrity assessments to hold a Quality Management System Certificate of Authorization Permit and to document its system against AB-515. The written description must address scope, organization, impartiality, confidentiality, competence, measuring and test equipment, integrity assessment procedures, plans and work plans, reporting, repairs and alterations, internal audits, and control of NDE. Authorized scope is fixed on form AB-515(a), and work outside it is prohibited until a revised AB-515(a) is accepted. Individuals who certify equipment for continued operation must personally hold an Alberta In-Service Pressure Equipment Inspector Certificate of Competency. AB-515 renamed these firms Integrity Assessment Organizations, formerly Inspection Companies.
personnelCertification: Two separate credentials apply, and only one can be outsourced. NDT technicians work under employer-based certification: AB-515 §4.14 states an NDE organization conforming to ISO 9712, SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 (ACCP/ASNT) is desired, requires NDE procedures approved and signed by a Level III, and explicitly accepts a Level III who is 'contract or employee'. An outsourced Level III can therefore own the written practice and sign procedures. The in-service inspector credential cannot be handled that way: the person who certifies pressure equipment for continued operation must personally hold an ABSA Certificate of Competency issued under AB-526.
requiredDocuments: Form AB-29 Application for Certificate of Authorization Permit
Written description of the Quality Management System (the AB-515 manual)
Form AB-515(a) Integrity Assessment Organization Authorized Scope of Activities
Form AB-515(b) Integrity Assessment Organization QMS Written Description Checklist
Statement of Authority and Responsibility signed by a principal company official
Independence, impartiality and integrity policy, with conflict-of-interest clauses in employee and subcontractor contracts
NDE procedures reviewed and signed by a Level III, plus the NDE contractor's written practice for qualifying and certifying examiners
Personnel competency assessment records and copies of Alberta In-Service Inspector Certificates of Competency
Calibration records for measuring and test equipment, including subcontractor-owned equipment
Form AB-40 Repair/Alteration Report where repairs are inspected and certified
auditProcess: Information meeting with ABSA covering the Safety Codes Act, CSA B51, the applicable ASME code of construction and the AB-515 requirements. Optional for out-of-province applicants and not required for renewals.
Submit form AB-29, a draft written description of the QMS, form AB-515(a), the AB-515(b) checklist and the non-refundable application fee of $1,253.50 (ABSA Fee Schedule effective 2025-11-01).
ABSA reviews the written description and accepts it as the basis for review. Review is charged at the hourly rate of $163.50 with a minimum of four hours.
Applicant arranges a live project demonstrating the activities applied for and agrees an audit date with ABSA.
An ABSA auditor attends the work site, witnesses the work being performed and audits against the firm's own written description, assisted by the firm's management.
On a successful audit ABSA issues the Certificate of Authorization Permit; issuance fee $163.50. The normal term of a permit is three years.
ABSA conducts surveillance audit(s) within the certification term; a recommendation to continue validity of the permit is based on an acceptable audit.
renewal: The normal term of a Certificate of Authorization Permit is three years. ABSA conducts surveillance audit(s) within the term and continued validity depends on an acceptable audit. Renewal requires review and updating of the manual and submission of a new application for re-certification, approximately six months before expiry. In-Service Inspector Certificates of Competency run on a separate five-year cycle: form AB-98 plus the renewal fee of $188.90 must be submitted at least 21 days before expiry, with at least 15 weeks of in-service inspection experience in the last five years, a minimum of 80 hours of technical training (of which up to 12 hours may be in-house) and a re-certification examination.
commonFindings: Work performed outside the scope listed on form AB-515(a). AB-515 prohibits undertaking activity outside the accepted scope until a revised AB-515(a) covering the new scope is accepted by ABSA.
NDE procedures in use that have not been reviewed and signed by a Level III, which AB-515 §4.14 identifies as a control the organization is expected to verify.
No documented verification that subcontracted NDE personnel actually hold the qualification and certification the work order specified.
Impartiality and conflict-of-interest measures missing from employee and subcontractor contracts, which AB-515 §4.7.2 requires those contracts to incorporate.
Specifying integrity assessment or NDE activity in excess of what AB-506 requires, which AB-515 §4.7.2 gives as an example of compromised independence of judgement.

The manual fails to state which records are the client's property. AB-515 requires it to be clear that inspection reports, work plans and integrity assessment records created for the owner belong to the owner and must be returned on request.
Calibration status of measuring and test equipment used by subcontracted NDE companies not tracked by the certificate holder.

Personnel certifying pressure equipment with a lapsed Alberta In-Service Inspector Certificate of Competency; AB-526 states a certificate is no longer valid once expired and a person must not certify any item without a valid one.
sources: ABSA AB-515 Quality Management System Requirements for Integrity Assessment Organizations, Edition 3 Revision 0, issued 2022-09-19 (next scheduled revision 2027); ABSA AB-526 In-Service Pressure Equipment Inspector Certification Requirements, Edition 3 Revision 3, issued 2025-01-17; ABSA AB-512 Owner-User Pressure Equipment Integrity Management Requirements, Edition 4 Revision 0, issued 2025-10-14; Pressure Equipment Safety Regulation, Alta. Reg. 49/2006 as amended by AR 195/2015, ss. 11-13 and 41-44; ABSA Fee Schedule for Delegated Functions effective 2025-11-01; ABSA QMS-CAP FAQs. All verified against absa.ca and the Alberta King's Printer on 2026-08-21.

name: Technical Standards and Safety Authority — Boilers and Pressure Vessels Certificate of Authorization and Certificate of Competency regime, O. Reg. 220/01
authority: Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA), Boilers and Pressure Vessels Safety Division, administering the Technical Standards and Safety Act, 2000 and O. Reg. 220/01
appliesTo: Businesses that install, repair or alter boilers, pressure vessels, fittings and associated pressure piping in Ontario, which must hold a Certificate of Authorization from TSSA or another Canadian jurisdiction. Also owners seeking accreditation of an owner/user self-inspection repair program, piping contractors electing the alternate piping inspection process, and individuals working as boiler and pressure vessel inspectors for an Authorized Inspection Agency.
summary: Ontario splits the requirement in two. A firm needs a Certificate of Authorization, obtained by submitting a written Quality Program Manual, undergoing a TSSA audit and providing a demonstration item showing adequate controls for the activities claimed; deficiencies must be closed before the certificate issues. The audit team includes a Quality Assessment Specialist plus an Authorized Inspector or Authorized Inspector Supervisor. Separately, individuals inspecting for an Authorized Inspection Agency need a personal Certificate of Competency, which requires a National Board examination, a TSSA examination and an in-service commission. Ontario is unusual in tying inspection personnel to employment by the certificate holder rather than allowing a contracted inspector.
personnelCertification: For NDE technicians Ontario recognises both routes: TSSA states that non-destructive examination of alterations by qualified personnel according to CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or ASNT SNT-TC-1A may be required, so an employer written practice is accepted alongside central CGSB certification. The owner/user self-inspection checklist nonetheless requires the QC Manual to address CAN/CGSB-48.9712 to meet Canadian jurisdictional requirements. The constraint is on inspection personnel, not NDT: under Advisory BPV-001-23 a qualified person performing alternate piping inspections must be an employee of the Certificate of Authorization holder, which limits a purely contracted arrangement.
requiredDocuments: Quality Program Manual covering the activities claimed, with an organization chart showing the inspector-to-supervisor reporting hierarchy

Completed owner/user self-inspection checklist cross-referencing each requirement to a QC Manual paragraph, submitted with one controlled copy of the manual at least one month before the implementation review
Demonstration item or repair job package showing all elements of the program, including non-destructive examination and heat treatment
NDE procedures and evidence that NDE personnel are qualified in accordance with the applicable code section and CAN/CGSB-48.9712
Registered welding procedures (WPS/PQR) and welder performance qualification records reviewed annually
Records of API 510 and/or API 570 certification, National Board In-Service, Authorized Inspector or Repair course completion, and TSSA Regulatory Requirements training Module 1
Certificate of Inspection records for each device and evidence of design registration (CRN) for all equipment
Quality program supplement where the alternate pressure piping inspection process is added to an existing Certificate of Authorization
Calibration records for NDE equipment, and retained UT reports and RT films per the applicable code
auditProcess: Determine the activities to be authorized and prepare a written Quality Program Manual addressing the CSA B51 and National Board Inspection Code control requirements for that scope.
Submit the completed checklist with one controlled copy of the QC Manual to TSSA head office at least one month before the scheduled implementation review date.
TSSA reviews the manual and schedules an implementation review; the audit team comprises at minimum a Quality Assessment Specialist plus an Authorized Inspector or Authorized Inspector Supervisor.
Demonstrate implementation through a repair job package or demonstration item covering every element of the program, including NDE and heat treatment.
Close out all deficiencies identified during the audit; TSSA does not issue the Certificate of Authorization until they are addressed.

TSSA issues the Certificate of Authorization stating the authorized scope; individual inspectors separately obtain a Certificate of Competency after the National Board and TSSA examinations and an in-service commission.
renewal: Certificates of Competency for boiler and pressure vessel inspectors renew annually and expire on March 1 each year; TSSA sends renewal invoices roughly 60 days before expiration and a late renewal fee applies after the deadline. Renewal requires a valid and current National Board In-Service Commission card verified against the listed employer. A certificate not renewed within 12 months of expiry must go through reinstatement. Certificates of Inspection for equipment run on 12, 24 or 36 month cycles depending on equipment classification.
commonFindings: Qualified personnel performing alternate piping inspections who are contractors rather than employees, contrary to clause 2.1 of Advisory BPV-001-23 which requires them to be an employee of the Certificate of Authorization holder.
QC Manual does not address the qualification and certification of NDT personnel to CAN/CGSB-48.9712, which the owner/user self-inspection checklist lists as the Canadian jurisdictional requirement.
Inspector scope mismatch: personnel certified only to API 570 signing off on vessel work, where API 570 alone supports piping only.
Work performed outside the authorized scope stated on the Certificate of Authorization, or the alternate piping process used without first applying to add it to the scope.
No quality program supplement added to the existing manual when the alternate piping inspection program was adopted.
Missing TSSA Regulatory Requirements training Module 1 completion records for personnel signing Alternate Piping Data Forms.
Boilers or pressure vessels in service without a Canadian Registration Number, which cannot be remedied retroactively by registering equipment already purchased.
UT reports and RT films not retained for the period the applicable code requires, and NDE equipment calibration records incomplete.
sources: TSSA Advisory BPV-001-23, Alternate Process for Pressure Piping Inspection in Ontario, dated 2023-04-17 and effective 2023-05-01, referencing CSA B51-19 clause 4.10.2.1 as modified by Code Adoption Document BPV-20-01 R1; TSSA Accreditation of Owner/User Self-Inspection Repair Program, Guide for Review Teams, June 2007 Rev. 4; TSSA Accredited Inspection Agencies Acceptable to TSSA, 2008-05-08 Rev. 8; TSSA Certification: Boilers and Pressure Vessels, Types of Inspections, and Boiler & Pressure Vessel Owners pages; Technical Standards and Safety Act, 2000 and O. Reg. 220/01. Verified on tssa.org on 2026-08-21.

name: Technical Safety BC — Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Refrigeration contractor licensing and design registration under the Safety Standards Act
authority: Technical Safety BC, formerly the British Columbia Safety Authority, administering the Safety Standards Act, S.B.C. 2003, c. 39 and the Power Engineers, Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Refrigeration Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 104/2004
appliesTo: Contractors performing boiler, pressure vessel and refrigeration work in British Columbia, who must hold a BPVR contractor licence in the applicable class. Also manufacturers registering vessel, fitting and piping designs for use in BC, owners holding operating permits, and pressure welders holding certificates of qualification. Applies to design, construction, installation and operation of boilers, pressure vessels, pressure piping systems and fittings throughout the province.
summary: Note on naming: there is no body called the BC Safety Authority today; it was renamed Technical Safety BC and that is the current legal and operating name. TSBC licenses BPVR contractors across eight classes (A, Au, Ap, B, MA, PW, REF and SRV). Every class must submit a quality control program and designate a quality control manager with contact details, demonstrate working knowledge of that program, and may be required to show adequate equipment and facilities. Class B and REF applicants became subject to a QCP manual submission requirement from January 1, 2026. Design registration runs through the Design Registration Portal, and BC participates in the national CRN Reconciliation Agreement.
personnelCertification: British Columbia does not prescribe a specific NDT personnel certification scheme in B.C. Reg. 104/2004; section 64(c) simply requires non-destructive tests as required by a safety officer. Certification requirements reach the province through the adopted code, CSA B51:24, which references CAN/CGSB-48.9712, so central NRCan certification is the expected route in practice. I could not verify a published TSBC statement accepting an SNT-TC-1A employer written practice as an equivalent, so a firm relying on employer-based certification should confirm this with TSBC before bidding. Safety officers themselves must hold a valid National Board Commission as a boiler and pressure vessel inspector.
requiredDocuments: BPVR contractor licence application for the applicable class (A, Au, Ap, B, MA, PW, REF or SRV)
Quality control program manual covering the scope of the licence class
Designation of a quality control manager with name and contact information
For Class REF, the named refrigeration mechanic with a copy of their trade qualification and phone number
Design submissions through the Design Registration Portal, with professional engineering proof of design
British Columbia Statutory Declaration Form, or a statutory declaration from another province, for fitting registrations
Valid QMS certificate verifying the manufacturer's quality control program meets Annex F of CSA B51
Proof of initial registration from the originating regulatory authority for fittings first registered in another province
Pressure welder certificates of qualification (classes A, IT and R) for welding personnel
auditProcess: Select the correct contractor licence class and obtain the codes adopted by Ministerial Order M225-2024 for that scope.
Prepare the quality control program and designate a quality control manager, then submit the licence application with the non-refundable application fee.
Technical Safety BC reviews the quality control program; review is billed on an hourly basis depending on the complexity and quality of the submission.
Demonstrate knowledge of the quality control program, and where required show adequate equipment and facilities for the work.
Technical Safety BC issues the contractor licence for the authorized class; design registrations are handled separately through the Design Registration Portal.
Renew annually, with renewal available up to six months before the expiration date.
renewal: BPVR contractor licences require annual renewal, and contractors may renew up to six months before the expiration date. Manufacturers' quality control programs supporting fitting registrations must be recertified at a maximum interval of five years, and a fitting registration is only valid while a current certification of the manufacturer's quality control program is on record with Technical Safety BC.
commonFindings: Quality control program submitted without a designated quality control manager or without current contact information for that person.
Class B or REF licence held without the quality control program manual required from January 1, 2026.
Fitting registration lapsed because the manufacturer's quality control program certification on record with TSBC expired; registrations are only valid while a current certification is on file.
Fitting submissions missing the British Columbia Statutory Declaration Form or an equivalent declaration from another province.
Manufacturer's QC program does not meet Annex F of CSA B51, which the fittings checklist requires the QMS certificate to verify.
Design applications submitted outside the Design Registration Portal, which are rejected, and incomplete applications attracting additional fees.
Work carried out against superseded code editions after Ministerial Order M225-2024 took effect on December 31, 2024.
Class REF licence application without the named refrigeration mechanic and a copy of their trade qualification.
sources: Power Engineers, Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Refrigeration Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 104/2004 (ss. 60, 64, 65, 84, 86) under the Safety Standards Act, S.B.C. 2003, c. 39, via bclaws.gov.bc.ca; Technical Safety BC Information Bulletin, Adoption of Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Refrigeration Codes, bulletin dated 2024-07-18, effective 2024-12-31 under Ministerial Order M225-2024, adopting CSA B51:24, CSA B52-23, ANSI/NB-23 (2023), API 510 Eleventh Edition, API 570 Fifth Edition and NFPA 85 (2023); Technical Safety BC Boilers, Pressure Vessels & Refrigeration Licences and Pressure Fittings Design Registration Checklist pages. Verified on technicalsafetybc.ca on 2026-08-21.

name: Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan — Quality Management System of Inspections and Licensed Pressure Equipment Inspector regime
authority: Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan (TSASK), administering The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act and The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Regulations, with oversight from the Saskatchewan Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Board
appliesTo: Owners and insurers of pressure equipment in Saskatchewan who want to set inspection intervals by risk rather than fixed regulatory intervals, and the inspection companies that serve them. TSASK states that an inspection company providing inspection services of pressure equipment for an approved owner or insurer under a QMS must itself apply for registration with TSASK. Also applies to contractors constructing, installing, altering or repairing pressure equipment.
summary: Saskatchewan's Quality Management System of Inspections is voluntary but commercially decisive: it is what lets a company lengthen inspection intervals, remove start-up delays on newly installed equipment and extend PSV service intervals. Three authorization classes exist under Regulation 83(1) — Class A covering periodic inspections, repairs and alterations and acceptance inspections of new piping including boilers, Class B the same without boilers, and Class C for insurers inspecting equipment they insure. Every inspection carried out under an approved QMS must be done by a Licensed Pressure Equipment Inspector whose licence authorizes that inspection, and the holder must designate and employ one. Separately, contractors need a Certificate of Authorization built on a quality control manual.
personnelCertification: Saskatchewan is the strictest of the western provinces on this point. The TSASK quality control program guide states that personnel performing NDE must be qualified and certified in accordance with CGSB, with their qualifications maintained by the certificate holder, and requires annual vision and colour differentiation testing. That is central third-party certification through the NRCan NDT Certification Body to CAN/CGSB-48.9712, not an employer written practice, so an SNT-TC-1A Level II will not satisfy an auditor on its own. Inspection personnel need a TSASK Licensed Pressure Equipment Inspector licence, and a Designated Pressure Equipment Inspector also needs a TSASK Certificate of Qualification.
requiredDocuments: Application for a Quality Program Review
One controlled copy of the QMS manual covering design, construction, installation, operation, alteration, repairs, inspections and decommissioning information

Quality control manual per guide IP-2008-07-04, with title page, Certificate of Authorization facsimile, statement of authority, organization charts, and sections on drawings and designs, material control, examination and inspection, nonconformity, welding, NDE, heat treatment, calibration, record retention and sample forms
CGSB certification records for NDE personnel, plus annual vision and colour differentiation test results
Licensed Pressure Equipment Inspector licences and the Certificate of Qualification for the Designated Pressure Equipment Inspector
Welding procedure specifications and PQRs conforming to ASME Section IX, registered with the jurisdiction before use
Pressure Equipment Status Report and the QMS Inspection Reporting spreadsheet
Letter of Implementation and the semi-annual May and November inspection reports
Pressure Equipment Inventory Updates and written notification to the Chief Inspector of any change of designated inspector
Design submissions through the Design Submission Portal, with forms TSK-1003 and TSK-1009 as applicable
auditProcess: Submit the Application for a Quality Program Review together with one controlled copy of the QMS manual to TSASK.
TSASK conducts the manual review phase against the applicable requirements and the Chief Inspector approves the manual.
Complete the implementation audit within six months of approval; if the audit is not completed within six months a new application and payment are required.

TSASK issues the Certificate of Authorization, which must then be reproduced in facsimile inside the manual showing the current physical address of the managing facility and the scope of work from the title page.

Submit the Letter of Implementation, then maintain the four mandatory reporting streams: May and November inspection reports, pressure equipment inventory updates, and Chief Inspector notifications of designated inspector changes.
Request the renewal application at least 120 days before the certificate expiry date, and apply for an interim extension if the renewal audit will not complete before expiry.
renewal: Renewal applications must be requested at least 120 days before the certificate expiry date. Applications submitted closer to expiration may require an interim extension application to maintain compliance while the renewal audit is under way. A separate timing rule applies at first certification: the implementation audit must be completed within six months of manual approval or a new application and payment are required. TSASK did not publish a fixed certificate term in the material reviewed, so confirm the term on the certificate itself.
commonFindings: NDE personnel holding only employer-issued SNT-TC-1A certification, where the TSASK quality control program guide requires certification in accordance with CGSB.
Missing annual vision and colour differentiation test records for NDE personnel.

Inspections carried out under the approved QMS by a person whose Licensed Pressure Equipment Inspector licence does not authorize that class of inspection, for example Class 2 covering only pressure vessels and associated piping being used on boiler work.
Designated Pressure Equipment Inspector acting without the TSASK Certificate of Qualification required in addition to the LPEI licence.
Implementation audit not completed within six months of manual approval, voiding the application.
Certificate of Authorization facsimile in the manual showing an out-of-date physical address or a scope that does not match the title page.
Welding procedures not registered with the jurisdiction before use, or welder qualification attempted on production welds rather than a registered WPS test.
Renewal requested inside the 120-day window, leaving the certificate to lapse while the renewal audit is scheduled.
Inspection company serving an approved owner or insurer QMS without having registered with TSASK in its own right.
sources: TSASK Saskatchewan Quality Management System of Inspections, document IP-2011-01-01, including the Class A/B/C authorizations under Saskatchewan Regulation 83(1); TSASK Guide for Quality Control Program Requirements, document IP-2008-07-04, revision September 2017; TSASK Quality Management Systems, Pressure Equipment Inspector licensing and Design Registration pages; The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act and The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Regulations. Verified on tsask.ca on 2026-08-21.

name: Inspection and Technical Services Manitoba — pressure equipment Certificate of Authorization and inspection certificate regime
authority: Inspection and Technical Services (ITS), a branch of Manitoba Labour and Immigration — a government department, not a delegated or arm's-length safety authority
appliesTo: Any organization or individual that intends to construct, install, alter or repair pressure equipment in Manitoba, or to conduct pressure welding performance tests, and every owner operating a boiler, pressure vessel or refrigeration plant in the province. Repairs and alterations may only be performed by a holder of a current and valid Certificate of Authorization that includes the appropriate scope, with prior ITS approval before work begins.
summary: Manitoba is the province where a US firm is most likely to assume a third-party route exists and find none. Inspection and Technical Services performs the periodic inspections itself and issues the inspection certificate; the published ITS material does not describe an owner-user self-inspection or accredited third-party inspection agency programme of the kind Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario and Quebec operate. What a firm can hold is a Certificate of Authorization for construction, installation, alteration, repair or pressure welding performance testing, obtained by registering a written quality control manual with ITS and passing an implementation audit. Since June 8, 2020 ITS has applied a graded interval system rather than fixed annual and biennial inspections.
personnelCertification: The ITS publications reviewed do not name an NDT personnel certification scheme, so neither central CGSB certification nor an SNT-TC-1A employer written practice is affirmatively endorsed in Manitoba's own material. Certification requirements reach the province through the adopted code rather than through a provincial rule, and CSA B51 references CAN/CGSB-48.9712. What Manitoba does make explicit is a jurisdictional personal credential for welding: all welders and brazers working under a registered quality control programme must hold valid current Manitoba Welder Licences. Confirm the NDE expectation with ITS in writing before relying on employer-based certification.
requiredDocuments: Written quality control manual appropriate to the scope of work, registered with Inspection and Technical Services
Registered welding and brazing procedures
Valid current Manitoba Welder Licences for all welders and brazers
Certificate of Authorization stating the authorized scope of work
ITS ES Form 01 Repair & Alteration Report, submitted for repairs and alterations
Prior ITS approval for each repair or alteration before work begins
Design registration submissions for pressure equipment used in Manitoba
Inspection certificates carrying the Manitoba Object Number for each unit in service
auditProcess: Develop and implement a written quality control manual appropriate for the intended scope of work and meeting the applicable codes and standards.
Register the quality control manual with Inspection and Technical Services, submitting electronically per bulletin ITS 20-003 to QASupport@gov.mb.ca.
Complete the implementation audit conducted by ITS.
ITS issues the Certificate of Authorization detailing the authorized scope of work, valid for a period not to exceed three years.
Carry out all work in accordance with the registered manual, ensuring welders and brazers hold valid current Manitoba Welder Licences.
Review and update the manual and resubmit it before the expiry date to renew the certificate.
renewal: The Certificate of Authorization is valid for a period not to exceed three years and must be renewed prior to the expiry date by submitting an updated manual. Equipment inspection certificates carry their own expiry dates and the next inspection must occur before that date. Since June 8, 2020 inspection intervals have been graded: equipment is first assigned a grade 1 interval and only becomes eligible for the longer grade 2 interval after a minimum of two in-service inspections under grade 1, depending on condition and deficiencies found.
commonFindings: Repair or alteration work started before obtaining prior approval from ITS, which is required in every case.
Repairs performed under a Certificate of Authorization whose authorized scope does not actually include alteration and repair.
Welders or brazers working without a valid current Manitoba Welder Licence, which the registered quality control programme requires.
Certificate of Authorization allowed to lapse because the updated manual was not resubmitted before the three-year expiry.
Repair and alteration work not documented on ITS ES Form 01, or submitted without the unit location and Manitoba Unit number in the submission.
Equipment operated without a valid inspection certificate, which The Steam and Pressure Plants Act prohibits.
Assuming a grade 2 interval applies before the equipment has had the minimum two in-service inspections under grade 1.
Alterations made without design registration, including non-physical changes such as re-rating MAWP or design temperature, which Manitoba classifies as alterations.
sources: Manitoba Inspection and Technical Services Quality Control Program, Pressure Equipment Inspections, Repair and Alterations and Boiler & Pressure Vessel pages on gov.mb.ca; ITS Bulletin 22-004 Pressure Equipment Graded Inspections, describing the interval grading system implemented 2020-06-08; ITS Bulletin 20-003 Electronic Submissions Guide; The Steam and Pressure Plants Act and The Steam and Pressure Plants Regulation (Man. Reg. 108/87 R), and The Power Engineers Act. Note a genuine inconsistency in the source material: ITS pages variously cite The Technical Safety Act and The Steam and Pressure Plants Act as the governing statute, and the operative citation should be confirmed with ITS. Verified 2026-08-21.

name: Régie du bâtiment du Québec — Règlement sur les installations sous pression and the personne reconnue recognition regime
authority: Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ), Bureau d'expertise et d'homologation en équipements sous pression, administering the Building Act and the Règlement sur les installations sous pression, CQLR c. B-1.1, r. 6.1. Individual inspection certificates are issued separately by the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.
appliesTo: Inspection and insurance organizations that want to perform periodic inspections of pressure installations in Québec, which must be recognized by the RBQ as a personne reconnue. Also owner-users (exploitants-utilisateurs) responsible for having their installations inspected, manufacturers registering designs, and any individual who inspects the fabrication of pressure installations or installs, repairs or modifies them.
summary: Québec has two gates and a language requirement, which is why it defeats firms that cleared Ontario. First, the organization must be recognized: an inspection or insurance company obtains recognition as a personne reconnue by meeting the conditions in article 83 of the Règlement sur les installations sous pression and supplying the information and documents listed in article 84. Recognition is valid three years and renewal requires a fresh application, not a light-touch extension. Only the RBQ itself or a personne reconnue may perform the periodic external and internal inspections, and the personne reconnue issues the periodic inspection certificate to the owner-user. Second, the individual doing the work needs a provincial occupational certificate.
personnelCertification: The individual credential is the barrier. Québec requires a Certificat en inspection d'installations sous pression (IISP), a mandatory occupational certificate issued by the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale, for anyone who inspects the fabrication of pressure installations or installs, repairs or modifies them; working without it or an apprentice card is an offence carrying fines. It requires a minimum 1,000 hours of supervised apprenticeship and a written examination. National Board Inspector Commission holders get a shortened exam. Neither the regulation nor the RBQ application guide names an NDT personnel certification scheme, so confirm whether an SNT-TC-1A written practice is accepted before relying on it.
requiredDocuments: Application for recognition as a personne reconnue, with the information and documents specified in article 84 of the Règlement sur les installations sous pression
Evidence of compliance with the conditions in article 83 of the same regulation
Certificat en inspection d'installations sous pression (IISP) for each individual performing inspections, or a valid apprentice card
Periodic inspection certificates issued to the owner-user following each inspection

The owner-user registry: compliance certificates from permitted installers, all inspection and verification results, the manufacturer's operation and maintenance manual, and the complete maintenance, repair, replacement and modification history
Maintenance supervisor contact details and owner-user identification within the registry
Design plans and specifications submitted to the RBQ for Canadian Registration Number assignment
Quality control programme documentation for manufacturing certification, where applicable
auditProcess: Establish that the work requires recognition: periodic external and internal inspections must be carried out by the RBQ or by a personne reconnue on all pressure equipment except those excluded by article 71.
Apply to the RBQ for recognition, demonstrating the conditions of article 83 and supplying the documents required by article 84, via pcq-isp@rbq.gouv.qc.ca.

Ensure each individual inspector holds the Certificat en inspection d'installations sous pression, obtained through a minimum 1,000 hours of supervised apprenticeship and the written examination administered for the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.
RBQ grants recognition, valid for three years, and lists the organization publicly among the persons recognized to conduct periodic inspections.
Perform inspections at the frequencies set out in Table 1 of article 78 and issue the periodic inspection certificate to the owner-user for compliant equipment.
Submit a new application to renew recognition before the three-year term expires.
renewal: Recognition as a personne reconnue is valid for three years, and renewal requires a new application to the RBQ rather than a simple extension. The individual Certificat en inspection d'installations sous pression has a four-year validity, with apprentice cards renewed annually. Equipment inspection frequency is not a single interval but is set by equipment type in Table 1 of article 78 of the Règlement sur les installations sous pression. Note that a regulatory modification was published on 2026-07-15, so confirm current article numbering against the consolidated regulation.
commonFindings: Performing periodic inspections in Québec without RBQ recognition, where only the RBQ or a personne reconnue may carry them out.
Recognition lapsed because a renewal was treated as automatic; renewal requires a new application before the three-year term ends.
Inspectors working without the Certificat en inspection d'installations sous pression or a valid apprentice card, which is an offence subject to fines.
Owner-user registry incomplete: missing installer compliance certificates, the manufacturer's operation and maintenance manual, or the full modification history.
Periodic inspection certificate not issued to the owner-user after a compliant inspection.
Inspection intervals taken from a general rule rather than from Table 1 of article 78 for the specific equipment type.

Equipment returned to service after a period of inactivity without the evaluation and inspection by a personne reconnue that article 81 requires, which may call for thickness measurements and non-destructive testing.
Reports and certificates issued only in English where the francization requirements applicable to the work have not been addressed.
sources: Règlement sur les installations sous pression, CQLR c. B-1.1, r. 6.1, articles 71, 78 (Table 1), 81, 83 and 84; RBQ Personne reconnue and Respecter ses obligations pages, and La RBQ et les installations sous pression, which notes a regulatory modification published 2026-07-15; RBQ Guide d'application du Règlement sur les installations sous pression, produced by the Bureau d'expertise et d'homologation en équipements sous pression, which references CSA B51 édition 2014 and NQ 3650-900 édition 2013; Québec.ca, Certificat en inspection d'installations sous pression (IISP), issued by the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale. Verified 2026-08-21.

name: Canadian Registration Number (CRN) design registration under CSA B51
authority: Each provincial and territorial pressure equipment regulator issues its own CRN — ABSA in Alberta, TSSA in Ontario, Technical Safety BC, TSASK in Saskatchewan, ITS in Manitoba, the RBQ in Québec and the equivalent authorities elsewhere. There is no single national issuing body; CSA Group publishes the code, CSA B51, but registers nothing.
appliesTo: Manufacturers, fabricators and EPCs supplying boilers, pressure vessels, fittings and pressure piping into Canada, and the owners who buy them. Every pressure-retaining design needs a CRN in each jurisdiction where the equipment will be installed and operated. Inspection firms encounter it from the other side: equipment found in service without a CRN is a finding the owner cannot cure retroactively by registering a vessel already purchased.
summary: CRN is design registration, not certification of a company or a person, and it is the one Canadian requirement with no US equivalent. A design is submitted with proof of design to one province, receives a CRN, and is then extended to the others. The number itself encodes where: CSA B51 article 4.3 defines the format as a letter, four digits, a decimal point, then up to ten digits and three letters, and the digits after the decimal identify jurisdictions — 1 British Columbia, 2 Alberta, 3 Saskatchewan, 4 Manitoba, 5 Ontario, 6 Québec, 7 New Brunswick, 8 Nova Scotia, 9 Prince Edward Island, 0 Newfoundland, Y Yukon, T Northwest Territories, U Nunavut. C denotes all of Canada. Designs must be proven to an ASME code; EN and PED designs are not accepted.
personnelCertification: CRN registration assesses a design and the manufacturer's quality programme, not individual NDT personnel, so there is no Level III signature and no certification scheme choice at this stage. The relevant control is organizational: fitting registrations require a notarized statutory declaration plus evidence of a valid quality control programme acceptable to the regulatory authority, and Technical Safety BC requires a QMS certificate verifying the programme meets Annex F of CSA B51, recertified at a maximum interval of five years. NDE personnel qualification enters later, through the code of construction and through each province's in-service inspection regime.
requiredDocuments: Design drawings showing materials, welds and code details, with a professional engineer's stamp where required
Proof of design: code calculations, finite element analysis or proof test results, referenced to an ASME code
Manufacturer's Data Report (for example ASME Form U-1A) for vessels
Current quality control certificate — ASME Certificate of Authorization with the applicable code stamp, or an ISO certificate — covering welding where applicable
Notarized statutory declaration for fitting registrations, documenting drawing numbers, design proof methods, QC certification and the CRN marking
Evidence that the manufacturer's quality control programme meets Annex F of CSA B51
Proof of initial registration from the originating jurisdiction when extending an existing CRN to another province
For piping systems: P&IDs, line lists, the CRN inventory for component fittings, and the installation address
auditProcess: Determine the equipment category — vessel, fitting (categories A through H) or piping — and which jurisdictions the equipment will be installed in.
Prepare the design package proven to an ASME code, with the professional engineering stamp and a current quality control certificate.

Submit through the chosen jurisdiction's portal — ABSA's CRN Portal, the TSSA Client Portal, Technical Safety BC's Design Registration Portal or design.tsask.ca — and pay the applicable fee or deposit.

The jurisdiction performs the design survey and assigns the CRN. Under the Reconciliation Agreement in force since January 1, 2020, one design review is accepted by the other participating jurisdictions.
Extend the registration to additional provinces, which add their provincial digit to the CRN as acceptance; jurisdictions outside the Agreement may require their own design review.

Track fitting registration expiry: registrations must be resubmitted for validation not more than ten years after the date of acceptance by the regulatory authority in the original registering province.
renewal: Vessel design registrations do not carry a fixed expiry and remain valid until the design changes or a code change invalidates them. Fitting registrations do expire: under CSA B51 they must be resubmitted for validation not more than ten years after the date of acceptance by the regulatory authority in the original registering province, and the clock runs from that first province, not from the date a later province added its digit. In British Columbia a fitting registration is only valid while a current certification of the manufacturer's quality control programme is on record, recertified at a maximum interval of five years.
commonFindings: Assuming a CRN obtained in one province covers the whole country. The Reconciliation Agreement's participating jurisdictions are British Columbia, Manitoba, Northwest Territories, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, Québec, Saskatchewan and Yukon — Alberta, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador and Nunavut are not among the listed signatories, so registration there may still require a separate design review.
Submitting a design proven to EN or PED rather than to an ASME code, which is not accepted in Canada.
Fitting registration expired because the ten-year clock was counted from the most recent province's acceptance rather than from the original registering province's date.
Equipment installed and in service without a CRN; owners are told they must not buy a non-registered unit and then try to get it registered afterwards.
Fitting submission missing the notarized statutory declaration or the evidence of a valid quality control programme acceptable to the regulatory authority.
Manufacturer's quality control certificate does not cover welding where the fabrication scope includes it.
Piping system submissions missing the fitting CRN inventory for the components used in the system, or the installation address.
Applications submitted outside the required design registration portal, which are rejected, or incomplete applications attracting additional review fees.
sources: CSA B51:24, Boiler, pressure vessel, and pressure piping code, confirmed as the current edition via CSA Group and the Standards Council of Canada; CRN format per CSA B51 article 4.3 and fitting registration per clause 4.2. Reconciliation Agreement for the Canadian Registration Number (CRN) for Pressure Equipment (2018), in force 2020-01-01, signatories British Columbia, Manitoba, Northwest Territories, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, Québec, Saskatchewan and Yukon, per the Canadian Free Trade Agreement Regulatory Reconciliation and Cooperation Table (rct-tccr.ca) and Technical Safety BC. Fee data: TSSA National Service initial deposit CAD $1,200 including a $500 administrative fee plus taxes; ABSA Fee Schedule effective 2025-11-01, design survey for a simple vessel under 3 m³ $170.90 and fitting registration $163.50 per size, type and pressure. Verified 2026-08-21.

name: ASNT Recommended Practice No. SNT-TC-1A, Personnel Qualification and Certification in Nondestructive Testing
authority: American Society for Nondestructive Testing (ASNT) publishes it. Nobody enforces SNT-TC-1A directly — it becomes binding when a code, customer or regulator invokes it (ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII, AWS D1.1, the API inspection codes, prime purchase orders). ASNT Certification Services LLC will audit and accredit a firm's programme against it through the Employer-Based Certification (EBC) Accreditation Program.
appliesTo: Any US inspection service provider whose customer, code or purchase order invokes SNT-TC-1A: weld and fabrication NDT under ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII, structural work under AWS D1.1, refinery, piping and tank work under the API inspection codes, and pipeline construction where 49 CFR 192.243 requires NDT performed to written procedures by trained, qualified persons. It binds the firm's qualification programme, not the individual technician.
summary: SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice, not law. It gives an employer the framework for qualifying and certifying its own NDT personnel. For an inspection service provider the deliverable is a Written Practice covering training, examination, experience, vision and recertification for every method and level the firm sells, reviewed and approved by the employer's NDT Level III and retained on file for audit. Customers then audit the firm against its own Written Practice rather than against the standard directly. The 2024 edition adds the ASNT 9712 Program to the recognised examination routes, restricts eye drops used to improve vision, tells employers to assess whether externally referenced examinations meet their requirements, and expects written-examination proctors to be trained.
personnelCertification: Employer-based. The employer — not ASNT, not a third party — issues the certificate, and ASNT is explicit that where the person holds no third-party certification the credential is revoked on termination of employment. Because SNT-TC-1A states that in no case shall a certification examination be administered by oneself or by a subordinate, and because the Written Practice must be approved by an NDT Level III, a firm with no Level III on staff routinely engages an outside agency Level III. That contracted Level III can write and approve the Written Practice, build and grade examinations and recommend certification; the employer still signs and issues the certificate.
requiredDocuments: Written Practice for the control and administration of NDT personnel training, examination and certification, approved by the employer's NDT Level III and retained on file
NDT Level III qualification records — ASNT NDT Level III certificates, or the outside-agency Level III agreement plus that person's credentials
Training records showing classroom hours per method and level against the SNT-TC-1A training table, with content traceable to ANSI/ASNT CP-105 topical outlines
Documented on-the-job experience with dates, method, and supervisor attestation
General, specific and practical examination records, graded answer sheets, and the Level III-approved examination question bank
Vision examination records — near-vision acuity and colour contrast differentiation
Individual certification and recertification records stating method, level, technique and effective dates
Evidence that outside training or examination services used by the employer were assessed against the Written Practice
Calibration records for equipment the examinations and inspections depend on (light meters, gauges, reference standards)
auditProcess: Eligibility check and application to ASNT's Employer-Based Certification (EBC) Accreditation Program, submitting the signed application and payment, the Written Practice, the full list of locations seeking accreditation, the roster of NDT-certified technicians and backup certification documentation
Desktop audit: a qualified auditor reviews the Written Practice against SNT-TC-1A; the firm has 30 days to respond to nonconformances and a further 30 days to implement corrections

Compliance audit, conducted remotely, of actual certification packages against the firm's own Written Practice; 30 days to respond and 60 days to implement corrective action (an on-site audit is available at additional travel cost)
Panel review by a three-person independent panel confirming all accreditation requirements are satisfied
Accreditation decision — certificate valid three years and listing on the ASNT EBC registry
Renewal through the same audit sequence; ASNT notifies at least 90 days before expiry, and some registrations carry one-year terms with annual surveillance
renewal: Recertification is periodic and the interval is fixed by the employer's own Written Practice, not by ASNT. ASNT describes a recommended maximum interval of five years between renewals for NDT personnel. Recertification requires evidence of continued competence — re-examination or documented continuing activity — plus current vision records. Accreditation of the programme itself under the ASNT EBC route runs three years, with some registrations on one-year terms requiring annual surveillance.
commonFindings: Written Practice is a copy of the standard rather than a description of how the firm actually trains, examines and certifies
Examination question bank not approved by the NDT Level III, or reused without control
Certification examination administered by the candidate, or by someone the candidate supervises
On-the-job experience recorded without traceable dates, methods or supervisor attestation
Certificates issued without stating method, technique, level and scope limits
Vision examination records expired or missing, with no mechanism that stops the technician working
Outside training provider or outside examination service used with no employer assessment against the Written Practice
Level III oversight not evidenced — auditors write the finding against the Level III as well as the technician
Firm audits itself against a different edition of SNT-TC-1A than the one its purchase order names
sources: ASNT Recommended Practice No. SNT-TC-1A (2024), with Addendum — ASNT product listing (source.asnt.org) and ASNT standards page (asnt.org/standards-publications/standards); the addendum took effect May 2025 and ASNT recommends use with ANSI/ASNT CP-105 (2024). ASNT 'Ten Key Shalls of SNT-TC-1A' and 'What to Do in an Audit' (asnt.org blog). ASNT Employer-Based Certification Accreditation Program, certification.asnt.org — audit stages, three-year validity and published audit fees (single site and multi-site up to 150 technicians US$5,300; 151–500 technicians US$6,150; 500+ by quote), checked August 2026. 49 CFR 192.243(a)–(b) quoted from the govinfo CFR text. ASME Section V Article 1 T-120 and Section VIII Div. 1 UW-54 taken from secondary technical summaries, not read from the code; treat the clause designations as indicative. Vision examination frequency deliberately not stated as a number here — it was not verified against the 2024 text.

name: ANSI/ASNT CP-189, ASNT Standard for Qualification and Certification of Nondestructive Testing Personnel
authority: American Society for Nondestructive Testing (ASNT), approved as an American National Standard by ANSI. Enforced by the contract that invokes it — US Navy and defence supply chains, government and utility procurement — and auditable through ASNT's Employer-Based Certification Accreditation Program, which accredits programmes against SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, or both. The dependent credential, ASNT NDT Level III, is issued by ASNT Certification Services LLC.
appliesTo: Inspection service providers on contracts that call for CP-189 rather than SNT-TC-1A: US Navy and other defence and government work, parts of the nuclear and utility supply chain, and buyers who want the firm's qualification programme to be a requirement rather than a recommendation. It also matters to any firm claiming ASTM E543 conformance, which accepts CP-189 as a personnel-qualification basis.
summary: CP-189 is an American National Standard and it states requirements where SNT-TC-1A offers recommendations — it was written because employers implemented SNT-TC-1A inconsistently. It sets minimum education, training, experience and examination requirements for Level I, II and III nondestructive testing and predictive maintenance personnel, and adds requirements for NDT instructors. The 2024 edition adds requirements for computed radiography, digital radiography and computed tomography image interpreters, requires employers to assess whether externally referenced examinations meet their requirements, restricts eye drops used to improve vision, and requires trained proctors for written examinations. The commercially decisive provision is that Level III personnel must hold ASNT NDT Level III certification.
personnelCertification: Employer-based, with a central-certification prerequisite at the top. Levels I and II are certified by the employer against the firm's written certification procedure. The Level III running that programme must additionally hold ASNT NDT Level III certification in the method — a credential from ASNT Certification Services, earned through a computer-based Basic examination plus at least one Method examination, and ANAB-accredited to ISO/IEC 17024. This is precisely why CP-189 work is outsourced: the firm engages a contracted Level III who already holds the ASNT method certificates, and that person signs the procedure, sets and grades examinations and recommends certification while the employer issues the certificates.
requiredDocuments: Written certification procedure meeting CP-189 — the CP-189 equivalent of a Written Practice
Current ASNT NDT Level III certificates for the Level III of record, one for every method the firm certifies
NDT instructor qualification records
Training records mapped to the ANSI/ASNT CP-105 topical outlines
Experience records by method, level and technique, with evidence of supervision
Written, specific and practical examination records, including evidence that proctors administering written examinations were trained
Vision examination records — near-vision acuity and colour contrast
CR, DR and CT image interpreter qualification records where the firm offers digital radiography
Individual certification and recertification files carrying the certifying signature and the certified scope
auditProcess: Clause-by-clause gap analysis of the firm's certification procedure against the CP-189 edition named in the contract — CP-189 is a 'shall' document, so each deviation is a finding rather than a discussion
Verify the Level III of record holds current ASNT NDT Level III certification in every method the firm certifies, and that no certification was signed after a lapse date
Verify instructor qualifications and that delivered training content maps to the ANSI/ASNT CP-105 topical outlines
Review examination control — question banks, practical specimens, proctor training, and that nobody examined a subordinate or themselves
Pull individual certification files and trace each back through training hours, experience, examination results and vision records
Close nonconformances, then take either the customer's second-party approval or ASNT EBC accreditation against CP-189, which is issued for three years
methodsInScope: Predictive maintenance disciplines (CP-189 covers PdM as well as NDT personnel)
renewal: CP-189 makes recertification a requirement rather than a recommendation, with the interval fixed in the firm's certification procedure. The dependent credential has a firm published number: the ASNT NDT Level III certificate the CP-189 Level III must hold is renewed every five years, either by accumulating a minimum of 25 recertification points across the 60-month cycle while maintaining at least 36 months (756 days) per method of active Level III work, or by retaking and passing the examinations before the expiry date. ASNT publishes renewal-by-points fees from US$440 (member, single method) and examination recertification fees of US$525–545 per method for members.
commonFindings: Level III of record holds ASNT NDT Level III in some but not all of the methods the firm certifies under CP-189
Certification procedure written in SNT-TC-1A's permissive language and therefore failing CP-189's mandatory requirements
Instructor qualifications not documented for in-house training delivery
Training content not traceable to the CP-105 topical outlines CP-189 relies on
CR or DR image interpreters not qualified after the firm migrated from film to digital radiography
Proctor training for written examinations not evidenced
ASNT NDT Level III certificate lapsed mid-contract, invalidating every certification signed after the expiry date
Contract names one CP-189 edition and the firm self-audits against another
sources: ANSI/ASNT CP-189 (2024) — ASNT product listing (source.asnt.org) and ASNT standards page (asnt.org/standards-publications/standards), which describes CP-189 as establishing minimum requirements for employer-based NDT personnel certification including the requirement for ASNT NDT Level III certification of Level III personnel; 2024 changes (image interpreter requirements, proctor training, eye drop restriction, employer assessment of referenced exams) taken from ASNT's own edition summaries. Prior editions confirmed: 2006, 2016, 2020, 2024. ANSI/ASNT CP-105 (2024) topical outlines from the same ASNT standards page. ASNT NDT Level III recertification requirements and fees from certification.asnt.org/recertification/asnt-ndt-level-iii, checked August 2026. ASNT NDT Level III ANAB accreditation to ISO/IEC 17024 from ASNT Certification Services newsroom. ASTM E543 acceptance of CP-189 from A2LA R212 (10 Sept 2025) and the ASTM E543 scope. Recertification intervals for Levels I and II under CP-189 deliberately not given as a number — not verified against the 2024 text.

name: ASNT 9712 Certification Program, operating to ANSI/ASNT CP-9712 (ISO 9712:2021):2023 — the replacement for the ASNT Central Certification Program (ACCP)
authority: ASNT Certification Services LLC, the entity that manages and operates ASNT's certification programmes. The scheme document is ANSI/ASNT CP-9712 (ISO 9712:2021):2023, the ANSI-approved identical adoption of ISO 9712:2021. Accreditation status differs by programme: ASNT's separate ASNT NDT Level III programme is ANAB-accredited to ISO/IEC 17024, while ASNT has stated it is still pursuing ANAB accreditation for the ASNT 9712 programme.
appliesTo: Individual technicians and Level IIIs at US inspection service providers whose clients require third-party, ISO 9712-style certification rather than an employer certificate — international EPC contracts, export fabrication, offshore and marine scopes, and buyers who will not accept employer-signed credentials. It also applies to any firm still carrying legacy ACCP certificates, which are inside a closing transition window.
summary: The programme named in most older specifications no longer exists under that name. ASNT retired the ASNT Central Certification Program (ACCP) and replaced it with the ASNT 9712 Certification Program, launched by ASNT Certification Services LLC in March 2023 and built on ANSI/ASNT CP-9712 (ISO 9712:2021):2023, the ANSI-approved identical adoption of ISO 9712:2021. For an inspection service provider this is a personnel credential, not a company accreditation: it certifies the individual, travels with the technician, and cannot be signed for by a contracted Level III. ASNT's implementation choices inside the ISO framework include an 80% pass mark on practical examinations, mandatory flaw detection, psychometric validation of practical assessments, and acceptance of employer-based training certificates as qualifying documentation.
personnelCertification: Central, third-party certification. ASNT Certification Services LLC issues the certificate against the ASNT 9712 scheme; the employer cannot issue it, and an outsourced Level III cannot sign for the firm — the value here sits with the individual, not the programme. What the employer still supplies is verified experience and training documentation: ASNT explicitly accepts employer-based NDT programme training certificates as qualifying evidence, with technical training remaining valid for a maximum of ten years from completion. This is the single clearest break from SNT-TC-1A and CP-189, and it changes what an outsourced Level III can and cannot do for a bid.
requiredDocuments: ASNT 9712 application naming method, level and the practical technique coverage sought (single technique, or all techniques for the method)
Employer-signed verification of industrial NDT experience, expressed in days per method
Training certificates evidencing the required days of training, dated inside the ten-year validity window
Level II certificate or equivalent evidence where applying for Level III by the Level II route
Vision examination evidence — near vision acuity and colour vision
Existing ACCP certificate and its expiry date, where transitioning from the retired programme
Structured credit-point documentation assembled across the five-year cycle, for renewal
Records of the employer's job-specific training and the resulting authorisation to work on the employer's products
auditProcess: Apply to ASNT Certification Services for the method and level, selecting single-technique or all-technique practical coverage

Eligibility review against ASNT's published training and experience requirements — at Level II, 5 days training and 60 days experience for MT, PT and VT; 15 days and 180 days for RT; 18 days and 180 days for UT. At Level III with a Level II certificate and higher education, 180 days for MT, PT and VT and 270 days for RT and UT, plus 3–5 days of Level III training
Sit the computer-based written elements — General, Specific and Instruction Preparation at Level II; Basic, Basic Supplemental, Method and Procedure Preparation at Level III
Sit the hands-on practical examination(s) at an approved centre, against ASNT's 80% practical pass mark with mandatory flaw detection
Certification decision and certificate issued by ASNT Certification Services; the employer separately provides job-specific training and authorises the person for its own products
Renew at five years through the structured credit-point system, or transition a legacy ACCP certificate by applying and passing all required examinations before the ACCP certificate expires
methodsInScope: VT (direct, remote — announced by ASNT as coming, not yet released)
industries: Aerospace supply chain (as a supplement to, not a substitute for, NAS 410)
renewal: Certificates run five years and are renewed through a structured credit-point system rather than automatic re-examination; technical training supporting the initial certification stays valid for a maximum of ten years. ACCP transition dates are fixed and published: ASNT stopped accepting first-time ACCP applications on 15 May 2023 and stopped renewing existing ACCP certificants on 30 August 2023, with a transition period running to September 2028 when the ACCP programme sunsets. A 2026 ASNT article describes the last active ACCP certifications expiring in 2029. A restricted ACCP Level II VT route for AWS CWI/SCWI holders was extended by 24 months beginning 1 July 2023 by agreement between ASNT and AWS.
commonFindings: Firm assumes its employer-issued SNT-TC-1A certificates satisfy a client's ISO 9712 requirement — they do not, because ASNT 9712 certifies the person against a third-party scheme
Training certificates older than the ten-year validity window submitted as qualifying documentation
Experience verification supplied as hours or a job title rather than supervised days per method
Practical examination failed on flaw detection, which is mandatory under ASNT's implementation of the scheme
ACCP holder lets the certificate expire before applying to transition, losing the transition route entirely
Renewal credit-point evidence not accumulated across the five-year cycle and assembled at the last minute
Firm treats ASNT NDT Level III as equivalent to an ISO 9712 Level 3 certificate — different schemes, different examination structure, different accreditation status
Bid documents and quality manuals still cite 'ACCP' by name years after ASNT closed it to new applicants
sources: ASNT newsroom, 'Important Update to ACCP and CWI/SCWI Certification Program' (asnt.org) — verbatim dates: new applications stopped 15 May 2023, renewals stopped 30 August 2023, transition to September 2028, 24-month CWI/SCWI extension from 1 July 2023. ASNT Materials Evaluation, 'Understanding ASNT 9712: How It Relates to ISO 9712 and What Sets It Apart' (asnt.org/me/26/8) — identical adoption, 80% practical pass mark, mandatory flaw detection, psychometric validation, acceptance of employer-based training certificates, ACCP retirement with last certifications expiring 2029, and the statement that ASNT is pursuing ANAB ISO/IEC 17024 accreditation for ASNT 9712. ASNT 9712 Level II and Level III certification pages, certification.asnt.org — training days, experience days, exam structure, five-year validity, ten-year training validity, and published fees (Level II single technique US$1,270 member / US$1,345 non-member; multi-technique bundles US$1,620–1,970 member; Level III packages roughly US$1,190–1,820 member depending on method and whether the candidate already holds ASNT NDT Level III; individual exam components US$120–655). ANSI/ASNT CP-9712 (2023) listed on asnt.org/standards-publications/standards as the US adoption of ISO 9712:2021. All checked August 2026.

name: NAS 410, Certification and Qualification of Nondestructive Test Personnel, with its harmonised European counterpart EN 4179, Aerospace series — Qualification and approval of personnel for non-destructive testing
jurisdiction: United States (NAS 410); Europe (EN 4179), treated as technically equivalent
authority: Aerospace Industries Association (AIA) publishes NAS 410, distributed through Accuris. EN 4179 is prepared by ASD-STAN and published through CEN. Enforcement is by the airframe and engine primes through purchase-order flow-down, by the Performance Review Institute (PRI) through Nadcap audits to AC7114, and by aviation regulators — the FAA treats personnel qualified under EN 4179 as technically equivalent to NAS 410. National Aerospace NDT Boards (NANDTBs) operate in countries that have established them.
appliesTo: NDT providers and in-house NDT functions serving aerospace manufacturing, maintenance, repair and overhaul — engine and airframe shops, casting and forging suppliers, and independent NDT houses on aerospace approved-supplier lists. Primes flow the requirement down through purchase orders, and Nadcap audits it under AC7114. Firms selling into both US and European aerospace supply chains have to satisfy the NAS 410 and EN 4179 halves consistently.
summary: NAS 410 sets minimum requirements for qualifying and certifying Level 1, Level 2, Level 3 and Senior Level 3 personnel performing NDT, NDI or NDE in the aerospace manufacturing, service, maintenance and overhaul industries. Revision 6 was released by AIA and Accuris on 1 December 2025 and introduces a new Appendix D creating an additional pathway to Level 3 qualification, under which Level 2 personnel complete designated NDT activities that earn points toward qualification. EN 4179 is technically equivalent as published; the 2026 edition superseded EN 4179:2021 and carries annexes on the Level 3 recertification credit system, Level 1-limited personnel, and NANDTB requirements. Personnel certified to earlier revisions need not recertify until their current certification expires.
personnelCertification: Employer-based, with a named accountable individual. The employer shall identify in writing a Responsible Level 3 to act on its behalf in matters regarding the NDT qualification and certification process; that person shall be certified as a Level 3 in one or more NDT methods and shall have thorough knowledge of the written instructions, codes, specifications and standards the employer uses. NAS 410 does not require an ASNT NDT Level III certificate, though an employer's written practice may accept one as evidence of the General examination. Contracting the Responsible Level 3 role to an outside agency is common and workable — but only the employer certifies personnel, and in Europe a NANDTB may need to approve the Level 3.
requiredDocuments: Written practice for the training, qualification and certification of NDT personnel, approved by the Responsible Level 3
Written designation of the Responsible Level 3, plus that person's Level 3 certification records and evidence of knowledge of the employer's codes and specifications
Individual qualification files: training, experience, General, Specific and Practical examination results, and vision test records
Documented determination by the Responsible Level 3 — or by a NANDTB where one applies — of the adequacy and equivalency of experience carried in from a prior employer or programme
NDT procedures and work instructions for each method and technique, approved by the Responsible Level 3
Customer and procurement requirement flow-down records showing which prime specifications apply to which work
Internal NDT audit records, plus evidence that corrective actions from the previous Nadcap audit remain implemented
Equipment calibration, system performance check and process control records, including calibration requirements flowed down to subcontractors
The completed AC7114 self-audit package, including all applicable job audits, sent to the auditor before the audit
auditProcess: Apply for Nadcap accreditation through PRI's eAuditNet / EANSM platform and select the AC7114 checklists matching the methods and techniques actually performed
Complete the self-audit against those checklists including all applicable job audits, and send the required package to the auditor 30 days before the audit

On-site audit covering scope and general information, customer and procurement requirements, internal NDT audits, personnel proficiency and certification records, examinations and vision testing, Level 3 responsibilities and inspection status control — plus live job audits on real parts
Auditor uploads nonconformance reports; the supplier responds with root cause and corrective action, reviewed by PRI staff engineers
The Nadcap NDT Task Group votes to accredit, fail, or issue merit
First reaccreditation audit within twelve months of the initial audit; subsequent reaccreditation intervals extend to 18 or 24 months under the Supplier Merit Program based on audit performance
renewal: Personnel certification expiry is set by the employer's written practice; NAS 410 states that personnel certified to previous revisions of NAS 410 or EN 4179 need not recertify to the requirements of the new revision until their current certification expires. The company-level cycle is separate and defined by Nadcap: the first reaccreditation audit falls within twelve months of the initial audit, after which the Supplier Merit Program can extend the interval to 18 or 24 months depending on audit performance.
commonFindings: Self-audit not performed, or performed without all applicable job audits — consistently among the most-cited AC7114 nonconformances
Required pre-audit package not sent to the auditor 30 days before the audit
Corrective actions from the previous Nadcap audit no longer implemented at the following audit
Calibration requirements not flowed down to subcontracted calibration or subcontracted NDT services
Written procedure and observed practice disagree during a job audit — the technique the operator ran is not the technique the procedure specifies
Equivalency of experience carried in from a prior employer or programme not evaluated and documented by the Responsible Level 3 or the NANDTB
Written practice not approved, or not re-approved, by the current Responsible Level 3 after a personnel change
Process timing steps missed during a job audit — PRI's published lists cite eddy current step-one timing among the recurring job-audit nonconformances
US firm holding only a NAS 410 Level 3 finds it insufficient for a European customer who requires a NANDTB-approved Level 3
sources: AIA press release, 'AIA and Accuris Release NAS410 Revision 6, Advancing Aerospace Safety and Workforce Development' (aia-aerospace.org) — release date 1 December 2025, Appendix D points-based Level 2 to Level 3 pathway, Accuris as sole source for AIA subscription content. NAS 410 Rev 5 (2020) scope and the four levels (Level 1, 2, 3, Senior Level 3) from standard catalogue records. NAS 410 paragraph 4.5 'Responsible Level 3' wording quoted from ndt.net technical forum discussion citing the standard text; treat the paragraph number as indicative and confirm against Rev 6. EN 4179:2021 (BS/DS editions) and EN 4179:2026, listed by BSI and DIN distributors as the current edition published 2026, superseding EN 4179:2021 — verified through distributor catalogue listings rather than the CEN portal. FAA/EASA harmonisation and technical equivalence of EN 4179 and NAS 410 from published NDT qualification literature and the FAA's NDT memorandum for production approval holders. Nadcap AC7114 audit content, top nonconformances and the Supplier Merit Program 12/18/24-month intervals from PRI (p-r-i.org) course outlines and Nadcap programme material, plus Quality Magazine's Nadcap NDT audit perspective. Checked August 2026.

name: ISO 9712, Non-destructive testing — Qualification and certification of NDT personnel
jurisdiction: International, adopted nationally across the Americas
authority: ISO Technical Committee ISO/TC 135, Non-destructive testing, Subcommittee SC 7, Personnel qualification, in collaboration with CEN/TC 138 under the Vienna Agreement. Operationally the authority is the certification body running the scheme, which must operate to ISO/IEC 17024. In the Americas: ASNT Certification Services LLC (ASNT 9712 / ANSI/ASNT CP-9712) in the United States; Natural Resources Canada's National NDT Certification Body (NDTCB) under CAN/CGSB-48.9712 in Canada; ABENDI's SNQC-END, accredited by Inmetro, in Brazil.
appliesTo: Inspection service providers bidding work where the client specification names ISO 9712, EN ISO 9712 or a national identical adoption instead of an employer-based scheme — international EPCs, offshore and marine, export fabrication, and Canadian and Brazilian work where the national scheme is effectively mandatory. Because it certifies individuals, it constrains who can be put on a crew, not what the firm's paperwork says.
summary: ISO 9712 specifies requirements for the qualification and certification of personnel who perform industrial non-destructive testing. The fifth edition, ISO 9712:2021, was published in December 2021 and cancels and replaces ISO 9712:2012, which it technically revised — clarifying responsibilities for the certification body, authorized qualification body, examination centre and employer, revising training and industrial experience durations, modifying visual acuity testing, adding requirements for renewal candidates, and revising the structured credit system for Level 3 recertification. Its Scope notes that it specifies requirements for what are in effect third-party conformity assessment schemes. For a service provider this changes the shape of a bid: certificates belong to certification bodies and to individuals, not to the company.
personnelCertification: Central, third-party — the opposite pole from SNT-TC-1A. The certificate is issued by a certification body, which under the standard's own normative reference to ISO/IEC 17024 must be a properly constituted certification body, and that body retains authority over granting, maintaining, recertification, scope extension, suspension and withdrawal. Canada's NDTCB states plainly that it does not delegate those decisions. An outsourced Level III cannot sign for the firm here.
