What the employer keeps is real but different: verifying eligibility, delivering job-specific training on its own products, equipment, procedures and codes, and issuing the resulting operating authorization that lets a certified person work.
requiredDocuments: Application to the certification body or authorized qualification body naming method, level and industrial or product sector (Annex A)
Documented training from a source the certification body recognises, meeting the durations in Clause 7.2
Employer-attested industrial NDT experience performed under supervision in the method and sector (Clause 7.3)
Vision evidence meeting Clause 7.4 — near vision acuity and colour vision, with ISO 18490 as the normative reference for evaluating visual acuity
Examination results for the general, specific, practical and NDT instruction writing elements at Levels 1 and 2, or the basic and main method elements at Level 3 (Clause 8)
The certificate issued by the certification body, showing scope and expiry (Clause 9.2)
The employer's written operating authorization, issued after job-specific training on the employer's products and procedures
Renewal and recertification file, including Annex C structured credit system records where that route is used
auditProcess: Select a certification body accredited to ISO/IEC 17024 for the ISO 9712 scheme — or the national identical adoption the client actually names, since adoptions are not automatically interchangeable
Submit application and eligibility evidence: training duration, supervised industrial experience by sector, and vision (Clause 7)

Sit the examinations at an examination centre approved by the certification body — general, specific, practical and instruction writing elements at Levels 1 and 2; basic and main method elements at Level 3 (Clause 8)
Certification decision taken by the certification body alone (Clause 9); the certification body owns the certificate and controls suspension and withdrawal
Employer delivers job-specific training and issues the operating authorization before the person works on the employer's products
Renew under Clause 10 before expiry; recertify under Clause 11, using the Annex C structured credit system where the scheme allows it for renewal at Levels 1, 2 and 3 and for Level 3 recertification
methodsInScope: LT — leak testing (hydraulic pressure tests excluded)
VT — visual testing (direct unaided visual tests excluded)
renewal: Certificates carry a defined validity period, with renewal handled under Clause 10 and recertification under Clause 11. European Accreditation states that ISO 9712 certificates expire at the end of a maximum period of validity of five years, that renewal may be applied for up to 12 months after the expiry date, and that an application for recertification made more than 12 months after expiry requires a complete examination. Where the standard allows latitude, the certification body has the final decision, so the operative numbers come from the scheme rules, not from a universal figure. In the Americas: ASNT 9712 certificates run five years; Canada operates CAN/CGSB-48.9712-2022 (ISO 9712:2021, IDT) with its own Rules of Implementation; Brazil's SNQC-END operates under ABENDI's NA-001.
commonFindings: Bidding an ISO 9712 scope with employer-based SNT-TC-1A certificates and assuming they will be accepted
Certificate sector under Annex A does not match the work — a sector-limited certificate used across pre-service and in-service scopes
Certificate lapsed and the renewal window missed, converting a renewal into a complete re-examination
No employer operating authorization on file, so a validly certified technician still cannot be shown as authorised for the client's product
Vision evidence required of certificate holders under Clause 7.4 not maintained by the employer between examinations

Assuming reciprocity between national adoptions — NRCan states that adopting ISO 9712:2021 as CAN/CGSB-48.9712-2022 synchronises the published standards but does not by itself provide full harmonisation or mutual recognition of other certification schemes
Practical examination technique on the certificate narrower than the technique the job actually requires
Certification body chosen whose ISO/IEC 17024 accreditation does not cover the ISO 9712 scheme, or does not cover the specific method
sources: ISO 9712:2021 itself, fifth edition, 2021-12, read from the ISO-published preview: title page, Foreword (ISO/TC 135/SC 7 with CEN/TC 138 under the Vienna Agreement; fifth edition cancels and replaces the fourth edition ISO 9712:2012; the listed technical changes), Introduction, Clause 1 Scope with its ten methods and NOTE 3 on third-party conformity assessment, Clause 2 normative references (ISO/IEC 17024:2012 and ISO 18490:2015), Clause 3 definitions including 3.11 employer, 3.13 examination centre and 3.20 job-specific training leading to operating authorizations, and the full table of contents (Clauses 5–13, Annexes A–G). Validity period, renewal window and the 12-month recertification rule from European Accreditation's published FAQ on ISO 9712. Canada: Natural Resources Canada NDT certification pages — CAN/CGSB-48.9712-2022 (ISO 9712:2021, IDT), Rules of Implementation, the statement that adoption does not provide full harmonisation or mutual recognition by default, and NDTCB's statement that it retains and does not delegate certification decisions; also NRCan's 2026 notice that CGSB publishing changes do not interrupt NDTCB services. Brazil: ABENDI SNQC-END, accredited by Inmetro as a personnel certification body (OPC-02) to ABNT NBR ISO/IEC 17024 on the criteria of ABNT NBR ISO 9712, operating norm NA-001. United States: ANSI/ASNT CP-9712 (ISO 9712:2021):2023 per asnt.org. Note on the normative reference: ISO 9712:2021 cites ISO/IEC 17024:2012 as a dated reference, while ISO/IEC 17024:2026 was published on 1 April 2026 — ANAB has published transition milestones of 1 October 2027 for certification body self-attestation, assessments from October 2027 to September 2028, and 31 March 2029 as the final deadline. Checked August 2026.

name: ISO/IEC 17020, Conformity assessment — Requirements for bodies performing inspection
jurisdiction: International, applied through national accreditation bodies
authority: Developed by the ISO Committee on Conformity Assessment (CASCO) in collaboration with CEN/CLC/JTC 1. Enforced by accreditation bodies — in the United States by ANAB (which runs a dedicated NDE inspection body programme), A2LA (which covers NDT under both ISO/IEC 17020 and ISO/IEC 17025), IAS and PJLA. Since 1 January 2026 those bodies operate under the Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated (Global ACI) MRA, which replaced the separate ILAC MRA and IAF MLA when ILAC and IAF were wound up.
appliesTo: NDT and inspection service providers that issue statements of conformity rather than raw measurements — in-service inspection, third-party witness and shop surveillance, field and rope-access crews, and firms bidding public or regulated work that requires accredited inspection. It fits providers whose product is a judgement about an item, and it is the standard clients name when they want the provider's independence proven rather than asserted.
summary: ISO/IEC 17020 contains requirements for the competence and impartiality of bodies performing inspection and for the consistent operation of their inspection activities. The third edition, ISO/IEC 17020:2026, was published in March 2026 and cancels and replaces the 2012 second edition. The headline change for an inspection firm is that the categorisation of independence collapses from types A, B and C to type A and type non-A, with the independence requirements sitting in normative Annex A and impartiality requirements applying equally to both types. The edition also adds definitions of item and client, adds a subclause on control of data and information and on actions to address risks and opportunities, incorporates the common CASCO elements, and replaces some prescriptive requirements with performance-based ones.
personnelCertification: ISO/IEC 17020 names no personnel certification scheme. Clause 6.1 requires the body to define competence criteria and to select, train, authorise and monitor personnel against them; the inspection scheme or the client's specification decides what evidence counts, and Clause 3.3 notes that an inspection scheme can specify independence requirements. In most industrial NDT work an employer-based SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 programme satisfies clause 6.1, which means an outsourced Level III can hold the technical authority — writing competence criteria, approving procedures, signing qualifications. Where the scheme itself demands ISO 9712 certificates, clause 6.1 inherits that requirement and the outsourced Level III can no longer substitute for it.
requiredDocuments: Management system documentation under Clause 8 — policies and responsibilities, documented information, records control
Independence declaration and type A / type non-A justification against normative Annex A, supported by the actual ownership and commercial relationships
Impartiality risk register with evidence of ongoing monitoring of activities and of personnel relationships (4.1.3), and top management commitment to impartiality (4.1.5)
Legally enforceable confidentiality commitments extending to employees, contractors, committee members and anyone acting on the body's behalf (4.2.1, 4.2.4)
Legal entity evidence and arrangements covering liabilities arising from operations (5.2)
Personnel competence criteria, authorisation records, training and ongoing monitoring records (6.1)
Facilities and equipment records including calibration and traceability (6.2), and control of externally provided products and services including subcontracted NDT (6.3)
Inspection methods and procedures, inspection records, and inspection reports or inspection certificates (7.2, 7.4, 7.6)
Contract review records and control of data and information (7.1, 7.5)
Appeals and complaints registers, internal audit records, management review records and corrective action records (7.7, 7.8, 8.5, 8.6, 8.7)
auditProcess: Gap analysis against ISO/IEC 17020 and the accreditation body's own requirement documents, then application with a proposed scope — A2LA asks inspection bodies to provide a proposed draft scope of accreditation, and asks laboratories to complete its F215 NDT scope selection list
Document review of the management system by the assessor, with clarifications and required changes identified and documented before the on-site visit
On-site assessment covering the management system plus witnessed inspections — the assessor observes real inspections against the written procedures, in the field as well as at the base location
Nonconformity response and corrective action inside the accreditation body's window, with root cause and objective evidence of implementation

Accreditation decision and issue of the scope of accreditation, with methods broken down to the most descriptive definition supportable and, where appropriate, referenced by code section and paragraph
Surveillance and reassessment on the accreditation body's cycle, plus transition to ISO/IEC 17020:2026 within the three-year window that accreditation bodies date from the March 2026 publication
methodsInScope: LT — bubble, pressure change, halogen diode, mass spectrometer
industries: Construction and structural steel special inspection
renewal: ISO/IEC 17020 sets no accreditation interval of its own — the accreditation body's cycle governs, with surveillance assessments between reassessments. What is fixed is the edition deadline. Accreditation bodies have announced a three-year transition from the publication of ISO/IEC 17020:2026, with UKAS and ANAB citing 27 March 2029 as the point after which only accreditation to the 2026 edition is recognised. Existing ISO/IEC 17020:2012-based accreditations remain valid until then, and the main work is re-justifying independence under the type A / type non-A model and evidencing ongoing impartiality risk monitoring.
commonFindings: Independence type asserted without an Annex A justification that matches actual ownership, group companies and commercial relationships — the type A / type non-A change makes previously comfortable type B and C claims worth re-arguing
Impartiality threats identified once at implementation and never monitored on an ongoing basis, including the relationships of personnel (4.1.3)
Inspector remuneration linked to inspection outcomes or pass rates, which 4.1.7 treats as a direct nonconformity

Confidentiality commitments not legally enforceable, or not extended to contractors and personnel of external bodies (4.2.4), or the client not informed in advance of information the body intends to make public (4.2.1)
Witnessed inspection deviates from the written procedure — what the technician actually does and what the controlled document says disagree
Competence criteria stated only as a certification level with no evidence of authorisation and ongoing monitoring of each inspector (6.1)
Subcontracted NDT or subcontracted calibration not controlled as an externally provided service (6.3)
Appeals and complaints handled by the same person who made the original conformity decision, or not recorded at all (7.7, 7.8)
Inspection reports missing required identification, dates or traceability to the item inspected and the method actually used (7.6)
sources: ISO/IEC 17020:2026 itself, read from the ISO-published preview: title page (third edition, 2026-03), Foreword (prepared by CASCO with CEN/CLC/JTC 1; cancels and replaces the second edition ISO/IEC 17020:2012; the listed main changes including type A / type non-A, the new item and client definitions, the new subclause on control of data and information and on actions to address risks and opportunities, the CASCO common elements, risk-based thinking and greater flexibility), Introduction (type A and type non-A reflect the level of independence; impartiality requirements apply equally to both), Clause 1 Scope, Clause 2 normative reference to ISO/IEC 17000:2020, Clause 3 definitions 3.1–3.8, Clause 4.1 and 4.2 verbatim, and the full table of contents including normative Annex A on independence requirements. Publication date: the standard's own title page gives 2026-03; European Accreditation states 31 March 2026 while ANAB's blog and UKAS's technical bulletin work from 27 March 2026 — the month is certain, the day is not, so treat 'March 2026' as the verified figure. Transition: three years from publication per an ILAC General Assembly resolution, with UKAS and ANAB citing 27 March 2029. Global ACI: ILAC's and IAF's own sites confirm Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated was registered as an Incorporated Society on 6 December 2024 and functions as a complete entity from 1 January 2026, with the ILAC MRA Mark transferred and the IAF MLA Mark licensed to it. A2LA R212, Specific Requirements — Nondestructive Testing Laboratory Accreditation Program, publication date 10 September 2025, read in full: general criteria are ISO/IEC 17025 for testing laboratories and ISO/IEC 17020 for inspection bodies; the nine technologies in scope; scope breakdown conventions. ANAB's NDE inspection body programme page (anab.ansi.org/accreditation/nde). IAS inspection agency accreditation to ISO/IEC 17020 (iasonline.org). Checked August 2026.

name: ISO/IEC 17025, General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories
jurisdiction: International, applied through national accreditation bodies
authority: Developed under ISO's Committee on Conformity Assessment (CASCO). Enforced by accreditation bodies — in the United States principally A2LA, ANAB and PJLA — which since 1 January 2026 operate under the Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated (Global ACI) MRA that replaced the ILAC MRA and IAF MLA. A2LA's NDT programme is governed by its R212 specific requirements document, with the P102 metrological traceability policy and the F215 scope selection list.
appliesTo: NDT service providers that report measured test results rather than conformity judgements — fixed laboratories, mobile and field crews reporting thickness, hardness and flaw data, and firms calibrating their own NDT instruments and reference standards. It is also the route for providers whose customers want method-by-method proof of competence and traceable calibration instead of a company-level quality certificate, and for firms that need a scope of accreditation to name specific ASME, AWS or AISC provisions.
summary: ISO/IEC 17025:2017, the third edition, sets general requirements for the competence, impartiality and consistent operation of laboratories. It is structured as general requirements covering impartiality and confidentiality, then structural, resource, process and management system requirements, with Clause 8 offering Option A — a set of built-in management system requirements — or Option B, an ISO 9001-conforming system. For an NDT provider the practical consequence is that accreditation is granted method by method: the scope of accreditation names each technique rather than asserting general competence. A2LA accredits NDT under ISO/IEC 17025 for testing laboratories and ISO/IEC 17020 for inspection bodies, with an optional additional assessment to ASTM E543 or ASTM E1212.
personnelCertification: ISO/IEC 17025 requires competence but prescribes no certification scheme. Clause 6.2 requires documented competence requirements plus procedures and records for selecting, training, supervising, authorising and monitoring personnel — and clause 6.2.5 is a recurring deficiency in published A2LA assessment data. An employer-based SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 programme satisfies it, so an outsourced Level III can own the competence criteria, approve the NDT procedures and authorise technicians, and a laboratory can be accredited without a single third-party-certified individual. That changes only where a method on the scope, or the customer's specification, calls for ISO 9712 certification instead.
requiredDocuments: Management system documentation under Clause 8, Option A or Option B, including control of management system documents and control of records
Scope of accreditation request — for NDT under A2LA, the F215 Scope of Accreditation Selection List, broken down technique by technique
Completed ASTM E1359 self-assessment checklist, submitted to the assessor before the assessment, where the laboratory elects to be assessed to ASTM E543
Test methods and NDT procedures with evidence of selection, verification and validation (7.2)

Equipment records and calibration certificates meeting the accreditation body's traceability policy — under A2LA P102 this specifically covers MT ammeters, timers, gauss meters and white/black light meters; RT density film strips; PT pressure gauges, white/black light meters and temperature gauges; VT white light meters; leak test pressure gauges and gas sensing units
Metrological traceability records and reference standards (6.5), and records for externally provided products and services (6.6)
Personnel competence, training, authorisation and monitoring records (6.2)
Proficiency testing plan and results summary — A2LA's F104 — required for initial, renewal, surveillance assessments and annual reviews
Technical records and test reports meeting Clause 7.8, including the date of issue
Internal audit records (8.8) and management review inputs and outputs (8.9)
auditProcess: Apply with preferred assessment dates and the proposed scope; A2LA typically assigns an assessor within about 60 days
Document review by the assessor and scheduling of the on-site assessment; submit the ASTM E1359 checklist first if electing ASTM E543 assessment
On-site assessment of the management system plus technical witnessing of each method and technique on the requested scope, including field work where the scope covers it
Deficiency response and corrective action — A2LA works to a 30-day response window, with root cause and objective evidence

Accreditation decision and issue of the scope of accreditation, listing each technique and, where appropriate, the governing code section (A2LA's own examples include ASME Section V Article 6, AWS D1.1 inspection provisions, and AISC 360 Chapter N)

Ongoing cycle: renewal and surveillance assessments open seven months before the expiry or anniversary date with initial documents due six months prior; annual reviews open four months prior with documents due three months prior; proficiency testing documentation is required at all of them
methodsInScope: RT — X-ray (digital and/or film), gamma (digital and/or film)
MT — prod, yoke and bench, visible or fluorescent, wet or dry
UT — contact straight beam, contact angle beam, immersion straight beam, immersion angle beam, immersion phased array
LT — pressure drop, gas detection, gas concentration, flow rate
renewal: ISO/IEC 17025 sets no accreditation interval of its own; the accreditation body's cycle governs. A2LA opens renewal assessments seven months before the expiry date with initial documents due six months prior, opens surveillance assessments on the same lead times against the anniversary date, and opens annual reviews four months before with documents due three months before — and proficiency testing documentation is required at initial, renewal, surveillance and annual review alike. Unlike ISO/IEC 17020 and ISO/IEC 17024, which were both reissued in 2026, ISO/IEC 17025:2017 remains the current edition, so there is no edition transition to plan for.
commonFindings: Equipment and reference measurement standards without calibration records meeting the accreditation body's traceability policy — A2LA reports that around 38% of its nonconformances fall under clause 6.4
Externally provided products and services not evaluated or controlled — A2LA reports around 21% of nonconformances under clause 6.6, concentrated in 6.6.2
Management review outputs missing the records required by clause 8.9.3
Date of issue omitted from test reports, against clause 7.8.2.1 j)
Personnel competence procedures and records incomplete under clause 6.2.5 — selection, training, supervision, authorisation and ongoing monitoring, not just a certificate on file
Scope claimed more broadly than the techniques actually witnessed, since ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation is granted method by method rather than as a general competence statement
ASTM E1359 self-assessment checklist not submitted to the assessor before the assessment where ASTM E543 assessment was elected
Proficiency testing plan absent, or not covering every normally scheduled assessment and annual review
NDT equipment outside the A2LA P102 list checked or standardised in a way the method being used does not actually specify
sources: ISO/IEC 17025:2017, third edition, read from the ISO-published redline preview: title page and the full table of contents showing the restructure into Clause 4 general requirements (4.1 impartiality, 4.2 confidentiality), Clause 5 structural, Clause 6 resource (6.1 general, 6.2 personnel, 6.3 facilities and environmental conditions, 6.4 equipment, 6.5 metrological traceability, 6.6 externally provided products and services), Clause 7 process (7.1 to 7.11), Clause 8 management system with Options A and B, and Annexes A and B. Currency confirmed: no 2026 revision of ISO/IEC 17025 exists, unlike ISO/IEC 17020:2026 and ISO/IEC 17024:2026. A2LA R212, Specific Requirements — Nondestructive Testing Laboratory Accreditation Program, publication date 10 September 2025, read in full — general criteria (ISO/IEC 17025 for testing laboratories, ISO/IEC 17020 for inspection bodies), the ASTM E543 / E1212 option, the mandatory ASTM E1359 self-assessment checklist submitted before the assessment, the P102 equipment calibration list quoted method by method, the F215 scope selection list, and the scope breakdown conventions with A2LA's own code-section examples. A2LA ISO/IEC 17025:2017 FAQ (a2la.org) — process steps, ~60-day assessor assignment, 30-day corrective action window, and the 7-month/6-month renewal and surveillance and 4-month/3-month annual review lead times, plus the F104 proficiency testing requirement. Deficiency statistics attributed to A2LA assessor data as reported by Ideagen and in published A2LA top-10 deficiency material — treat the percentages as A2LA-reported, not audited by us. ASTM E543-26, Standard Specification for Agencies Performing Nondestructive Testing, confirmed on the ASTM store as the current designation, last updated 21 January 2026 (A2LA's R212 still cites the older title 'Standard Practice for Evaluating Agencies Performing Nondestructive Testing'). Checked August 2026.

name: Natural Resources Canada National Non-Destructive Testing Certification Body (NRCan NDTCB)
authority: Natural Resources Canada (NRCan), Government of Canada — NDTCB, based at 183 Longwood Road South, Hamilton, Ontario
appliesTo: Any firm supplying NDT technicians for regulated work in Canada under CSA B51, CSA Z662, CSA W178.1, the CSA N285 nuclear series or a provincial pressure-equipment authority. The body certifies individuals, not companies, but the employer signs the experience attestation, holds the certificates on file and issues the written authorisation to operate, so the firm carries the compliance burden and the audit exposure.
summary: NRCan NDTCB is the federal body that issues Canadian NDT certificates to CAN/CGSB-48.9712. Its formal name is the Natural Resources Canada National Non-Destructive Testing Certification Body; practitioners still say "CGSB certification", but CGSB only publishes the standard, and since November 2024 CWB Group has been a second certification body issuing to it. For an inspection service provider this is the gate to regulated Canadian work: technicians must hold a current certificate in the correct method, level and sector before deployment. The firm keeps the certificates, vision records and written authorisation to operate on file and produces them for clients and regulators. Employers, supervisors and a CGSB-certified Level 2 or 3 sponsor attest experience on the application. Certification is personal — it leaves with the technician.
personnelCertification: Central, third-party certification only — there is no SNT-TC-1A style employer written practice in this scheme. An outsourced ASNT Level III cannot certify anyone in Canada and cannot sign as the certifying authority for a Canadian firm's personnel. What an outsourced Level 3 can do is hold a personal CAN/CGSB-48.9712 Level 3 in the method and sector, receive written authorisation to operate from the client firm, and on that basis write and approve NDT procedures, act as technical authority, and co-sign experience attestations as the required CGSB-certified sponsor. The distinguishing point is that the certificate must be his own, issued by NRCan NDTCB or CWB Group.
requiredDocuments: Application form for Non-destructive Testing Certification, with experience attested by employer, supervisor and referee on pages 3 and 4
Vision Test Report Form and Vision Attestation Form
Photograph Verification Form and Identification Verification Form
Code of Conduct acknowledgement
Recognized Training Organization (RTO) course completion certificates for each method and level claimed
Electronic Written Examination Authorization (EWEA) and examination admittance and registration forms
Two professional passport photographs, 5 cm x 7 cm, taken within the previous 12 months, plus verified government-issued ID for first-time applicants
Renewal Application Form with evidence of continued satisfactory work activity
Structured credit system evidence, for certifications due for renewal on or after 15 April 2026
auditProcess: Submit the application package with attested experience, RTO training certificates, vision report, photographs and fees; NRCan NDTCB states new applications are processed within ten working days.
NDTCB verifies eligibility and issues examination admittance and registration forms, including electronic written examination authorisation.
Complete the required training at a Recognized Training Organization for each method and level.
Sit the computer-based written examinations at an Authorized Examination Centre — paper multiple-choice examinations were phased out on 28 July 2023 — and the practical examination.

Results are released within fifteen working days. All examination attempts must be completed within two years of the first attempt, with a further two years allowed to finish outstanding experience hours.
Certificate issued, valid for up to five years (60 months or less), expiring in the holder's birth month; the holder appears in the public directory of certified personnel.
Renew before expiry, or recertify by examination at the alternate cycle.
methodsInScope: Exposure Device Operator written examination (qualifying body on behalf of the CNSC)
renewal: Certificates are valid for up to five years (60 months or less) and expire in the holder's birth month. Renewal requires evidence of continued satisfactory work activity plus a vision test — near and distance acuity results are valid one year, colour vision and grey-scale perception five years. Applications were due one month before expiry for certificates expiring up to 15 March 2026, and four months before expiry from 15 April 2026, when a structured credit system also becomes the proof of continued competence, with one attempt permitted per method. Late renewal is possible up to twelve months after expiry with a CAD 150 additional fee. Recertification, which adds examination, applies at the alternate cycle; CWB Group, certifying to the same standard, states recertification every ten years from initial certification. Published NRCan fees (page last modified 17 July 2026, non-refundable and non-transferable): application CAD 525 for all methods and levels; written registration CAD 90 per paper at Level 1, CAD 115 at Level 2, CAD 140 at Level 3; online written examination CAD 125 per paper; practical registration CAD 110–625; practical examination fees paid to the authorized examination centre CAD 320–1,520.
commonFindings: Technician deployed on work outside the sector or method endorsement printed on his certificate
Certificate expired in the holder's birth month while the firm's personnel matrix still showed it current
Renewal submitted late against the four-month deadline that applies from 15 April 2026, so the certificate lapsed
Near or distance vision record on file older than twelve months
Experience attestation not co-signed by a CGSB-certified Level 2 or 3 sponsor
ASNT SNT-TC-1A card presented as evidence of Canadian certification for CGSB-scope work
No employer-issued written authorisation to operate for the method the technician is performing
Training certificate from an organisation that is not on the NRCan Recognized Training Organization list
sources: Verified August 2026 against NRCan NDTCB pages: "National Non-Destructive Testing Certification Body"; "Apply for NDT Certification"; "Details about the Initial NDT Certification Process"; "Renewing Your NDT Certification"; "Fees for NDT Certification and Examination" (page last modified 17 July 2026); "NDT Certification Body: FAQs" (confirming the NDTCB is the qualifying body for the CNSC exposure device operator written examination); "Standards Framework for the NDT Certification Program"; and "Rules of Implementation for CAN/CGSB-48.9712" (effective 31 March 2024). Also NRCan NDTCB controlled document 8.2.1-083, version 02, issued 24 March 2026; IAS accreditation certificate PCB-115 to ISO/IEC 17024:2012, scope effective 2 August 2019 (current accreditor should be re-confirmed before relying on it); CWB Group "Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) Personnel Certification" and "Making sense of NDT personnel certification in Canada", read 2026.

name: CAN/CGSB-48.9712, Non-destructive testing — Qualification and certification of NDT personnel (ISO 9712, IDT)
authority: Canadian General Standards Board (CGSB), Public Services and Procurement Canada, publishes the standard; certification to it is delivered by NRCan NDTCB and by CWB Group
appliesTo: Every Canadian code and regulator that names NDT personnel qualification points here: CSA B51, CSA Z662, CSA W178.1, the CSA N285 nuclear series and the provincial pressure-equipment authorities. It binds the individual technician, and through him the firm that deploys him. An inspection provider cannot staff regulated Canadian work with technicians holding only employer-issued certificates.
summary: CAN/CGSB-48.9712 is the Canadian adoption, identical, of ISO 9712. The current edition is CAN/CGSB-48.9712-2022, adopting ISO 9712:2021, published October 2022, applied through the NDTCB Rules of Implementation effective 31 March 2024. It sets three levels, defines methods and sectors, fixes minimum training and industrial experience, and requires examination by a certification body independent of the employer. For an inspection service provider the operative consequences are narrow and testable: certificates must be current and in the right method, level and sector; the employer must issue written authorisation to operate; and NDT procedures must be approved by someone who personally holds Level 3 in that method. The standard is what auditors compare the personnel matrix against.
personnelCertification: Central certification, explicitly not employer-based. CWB Group states it plainly: certification is delivered through independent third-party bodies, and "This differs from second-party certification systems, such as employer-based programs like SNT-TC-1A." Two bodies issue to this standard — NRCan NDTCB, and since November 2024 CWB Group, which is accredited by the Standards Council of Canada to ISO/IEC 17024 and can also renew and recertify certificates originally issued by NRCan. An outsourced Level III adds value here only if he personally holds CAN/CGSB-48.9712 Level 3 in the relevant method and sector; the employer then authorises him in writing to operate, and he can own the procedures.
requiredDocuments: Controlled copy of CAN/CGSB-48.9712-2022 (ISO 9712:2021, IDT)
Rules of Implementation for CAN/CGSB-48.9712, effective 31 March 2024
Personnel certification matrix listing method, level, sector and expiry date for every technician
Employer's written authorisation to operate, issued per technician and per method
Vision test records — near and distance acuity annually, colour and grey-scale perception every five years
Recognized Training Organization course records evidencing the published training hours
Documented industrial experience logs with employer, supervisor and referee attestations co-signed by a CGSB-certified Level 2 or 3 sponsor
NDT procedures signed and approved by a Level 3 certified in that method
auditProcess: Establish eligibility for the method, level and sector sought, and meet the vision requirement.
Complete the published training hours at a Recognized Training Organization; NRCan publishes Level 3 training as ET 42 hours, RT 35 hours, UT 35 hours, MT 28 hours and PT 21 hours.

Accumulate documented industrial experience: volumetric methods (ET, RT, UT) 45 days / 315 hours at Level 1 and 135 days / 945 hours at Level 2; surface methods (MT, PT, VT) 60 days / 420 hours at Level 2; Level 3 routes run from 180 days / 1,260 hours upward. One day means at least seven hours, which may be accumulated.

Have experience attested by employer, supervisor and referee and co-signed by a CGSB-certified Level 2 or 3 sponsor. Levels 1 and 2 may sit examinations before accruing experience; Level 3 candidates must hold 40% of the required experience first. Accelerated Experience Programs are capped at five days per method, level and sector and at 50% of the required experience.
Pass the examinations set by the certification body — written papers and a practical examination for the method and level.
Certificate is issued and the holder is published in the certification body's public directory, in support of clause 9.3 of the standard.
The employer issues written authorisation to operate before the technician works to the certificate.
renewal: Five-year validity. Renewal at the end of each period on evidence of continued satisfactory work activity and current vision; recertification, which adds examination, at the alternate cycle — CWB Group states renewal every five years and recertification every ten years from initial certification. The standard's own future is in transition: the Government of Canada announced in Budget 2025 that CGSB operations wind down effective 1 April 2026. NRCan NDTCB confirmed on 24 March 2026 that its certification services continue without interruption and that CGSB is developing a transition plan for maintenance of the standard. CAN/CGSB-48.9712 was due for periodic maintenance review by 31 October 2027; SCC approved a two-year extension running from the date ISO publishes a confirmation or a new edition of ISO 9712, whose systematic review is scheduled to start in October 2026.
commonFindings: Technician holds the right method and level but the wrong sector endorsement for the work being performed
Procedure approved by an ASNT Level III where the governing code calls for CAN/CGSB-48.9712 Level 3
No written authorisation to operate on file, with the certificate itself being treated as permission to work
Experience log not co-signed by a CGSB-certified Level 2 or 3 sponsor
Accelerated Experience Program credit claimed beyond five days per method, level and sector, or beyond 50% of required experience
Level 3 candidate examined without the required 40% of experience already accrued
Vision records expired — near and distance acuity are valid for only one year
Firm working to an uncontrolled or superseded copy of the standard and the Rules of Implementation
sources: Verified August 2026 against: CAN/CGSB-48.9712-2022 (ISO 9712:2021, IDT), published October 2022, per CGSB, SCC and distributor listings; NRCan NDTCB "Rules of Implementation for CAN/CGSB-48.9712", effective 31 March 2024, for the Canadian latitude, experience percentages, sponsor co-signature and Accelerated Experience Program caps; NRCan NDTCB "Qualifying Work Experience for NDT Certification" for the day and hour tables, and "Training Requirements and Prerequisites for NDT Certification" for Level 3 training hours; NRCan NDTCB document 8.2.1-083 version 02, issued 24 March 2026, for the CGSB wind-down and the SCC-approved maintenance extension; CWB Group "Making sense of NDT personnel certification in Canada" and "Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) Personnel Certification", read 2026; CSA W178.2-18 clause 1.6, which directs NDT method certification to this standard.

name: CSA B51, Boiler, pressure vessel, and pressure piping code
jurisdiction: Canada — national standard adopted province by province
authority: CSA Group publishes the code; it is enforced by each provincial and territorial pressure equipment safety authority, including ABSA (Alberta), Technical Safety BC, TSSA (Ontario) and Manitoba Inspection and Technical Services
appliesTo: Inspection providers working on boilers, pressure vessels, pressure piping and fittings anywhere in Canada — new construction inspection, in-service integrity assessment, NDE subcontracting and design registration support. CSA B51 is adopted, with jurisdiction-specific exceptions, by every province and territory through its pressure equipment safety authority, so a firm's obligations are set by the edition its jurisdiction has adopted, not by the newest published edition.
summary: CSA B51 is Canada's boiler, pressure vessel and pressure piping code. CSA B51:24 is the twentieth edition, though several jurisdictions still enforce B51:19 (R2024). The code does not certify inspection companies itself; it sets the technical and quality-programme requirements that provincial regulators then enforce through permits. For an inspection service provider the load-bearing items are the requirement that non-destructive personnel associated with the quality control system be certified to CAN/CGSB-48.9712/ISO 9712 or another standard acceptable to the regulatory authority, and the new B51:24 annexes covering quality programmes for new construction inspection, quality programmes for design examination services, audit programmes, and pressure equipment integrity management programmes.
personnelCertification: Mixed, and the mix is the commercial opening. B51 points NDE personnel at CAN/CGSB-48.9712/ISO 9712 "or other standards acceptable to the regulatory authority" — the wording ABSA quotes from Clause 4.11. On the ASME new-construction side an employer written practice to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 governs, so an outsourced Level III can own and sign that written practice. On the in-service side, Alberta's AB-506 permits SNT-TC-1A Level II where the owner accepts it, but requires CGSB Level 2 for ultrasonic shear wave. Confirm the clause number against your adopted edition: B51:24 renumbered material when Part 3 was folded in.
requiredDocuments: The adopted edition of CSA B51 for each jurisdiction worked in — B51:24 or B51:19 (R2024)
Quality programme manual meeting the applicable B51:24 annex — Annex N for performing new construction inspection, Annex O for organizations providing design examination services
Written NDE procedures for each method in use, addressing ASME Section V and available to the Inspector
NDE personnel certification records including dates and results of qualifications, available to the owner, the Inspector and the regulator
Declaration of Conformity form (Figure D.6 in B51:24, which replaced the Statutory Declaration)
Canadian Registration Number (CRN) application form (Figure D.9 in B51:24) and supporting registration documentation
Provincial Certificate of Authorization Permit and the written authorized scope
Audit programme documentation consistent with Annex P
Integrity management programme documentation consistent with Annex Q where in-service work is performed
auditProcess: Identify the adopted edition and jurisdictional exceptions. British Columbia adopted B51:24 on 31 December 2024 under the Power Engineers, Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Refrigeration Safety Regulation but is not immediately enforcing impact-testing clauses 6.2.6.1, 6.2.6.2, 6.3.7.1 and 6.3.7.2. Manitoba adopted it on 1 January 2025 except clauses 5.2.7.3 c), 6.2.6 and 6.3.7.

Write the quality programme to the relevant B51:24 annex and to the regulator's own document set — in Alberta, AB-515 for integrity assessment organizations, with AB-515b as the self-assessment checklist.
Apply to the provincial authority for a Certificate of Authorization Permit stating the scope of work and the industry sector.
Desk review of the quality manual, procedures, personnel certifications and equipment calibration records.
On-site and in-field survey covering an actual inspection or examination, with interviews of the in-service inspector and the NDE examiners.
Close out non-conformances, then receive the permit limited to the authorized scope.
Maintain through periodic re-audit and permit re-issue on the interval and terms the jurisdiction sets.
renewal: The code itself is on a roughly five-year revision cycle — B51:24 followed B51:19 — and what governs is the date the jurisdiction adopts it, not the publication date, so a firm can legitimately be working to two different editions in two provinces at the same time. Permits issued under it, such as Alberta's Certificate of Authorization Permit for an integrity assessment organization, are renewed on the interval each provincial authority sets in the permit terms; confirm that interval with the issuing authority rather than assuming a national figure.
commonFindings: NDE examiner certification records not produced on request to the owner, the Inspector or the regulator, which AB-506 requires the examiner's employer to maintain and make available
No documented NDE procedure for a method in use, or a procedure that does not address ASME Section V
Ultrasonic shear-wave examination performed by an examiner without CGSB Level 2 in the method
Work performed outside the authorized scope shown on the Certificate of Authorization Permit
Quality manual still written to a superseded edition after the jurisdiction adopted B51:24
Statutory Declaration still in use where B51:24 requires the Declaration of Conformity
Independence requirement breached — the organization assessing the equipment is also its supplier, installer or maintainer
Corrosion or condition monitoring locations not reviewed and accepted by the Inspector
sources: Verified August 2026 against: CSA B51:24, twentieth edition, and CSA B51:19 (R2024), per CSA Group and ANSI listings; Technical Safety BC Information Bulletin IB-BP 2024-02 for the 31 December 2024 British Columbia adoption under the PEBPVRSR and the deferred impact-testing clauses; Manitoba Inspection and Technical Services adoption directive ITS-25-002 for the 1 January 2025 adoption, the excepted clauses, and the B51:24 key-changes list including new Annexes M, N, O, P, Q, R, S and T and the Declaration of Conformity (Figure D.6) and CRN application form (Figure D.9); ABSA AB-506, Inspection and Servicing Requirements for In-Service Pressure Equipment, Edition 4 Revision 0, issued 21 October 2025, sections 7, 8 and 14 read in full; ABSA conference presentation "An ABSA Overview of Code and Regulatory Requirements for NDE", NDT in Canada 2015, which quotes CSA B51 Clause 4.11 verbatim.

name: CSA W178.1, Certification of welding inspection organizations
authority: CSA Group publishes the standard; it is administered and audited by the CWB Group (Canadian Welding Bureau), Milton, Ontario
appliesTo: Organizations supplying welding inspection, non-destructive inspection or mechanical testing services to Canadian industry, and their individual divisions, offices, laboratories and sections. Fabricators, EPCs and owners in structural, shipbuilding, offshore, pipeline and pressure equipment work routinely make W178.1 certification a bid condition, and several product standards and regulators call it up by name.
summary: CSA W178.1 certifies the inspection organization, not the individual. The seventh edition, W178.1:18, was published in May 2018 and reaffirmed as W178.1:18 (R2023). Certification is granted for a defined combination of inspection methods and product categories and is maintained by an annual third-party CWB audit. The organization must have a qualified welding inspection supervisor holding technical control over every welding method in scope, welding inspectors certified to CSA W178.2, NDT personnel certified to CAN/CGSB-48.9712, documented inspection procedures for each product category, controlled equipment maintenance and calibration, and controlled records. The standard is intended to be applied alongside a quality management system such as the CAN/CSA ISO 9000 family.
personnelCertification: Third-party throughout, and W178.1 adds a constraint that decides the commercial question. Clause 7.1, clarified in the 2018 edition after a formal request for interpretation, states that an individual shall only act as the qualified welding inspection supervisor for one welding inspection organization, or for one designated division, office, laboratory or section. A shared or outsourced supervisor across several certified firms is therefore not available. Clause 7.2.2 does permit named delegates meeting defined minimum knowledge and experience. An outsourced Level III's realistic role here is procedure authorship and approval, internal audit and technical support — not holding the supervisor post at more than one client.
requiredDocuments: CWB Form 350, Application for Certification to CSA Standard W178.1
CWB Form 333, company details and requested scope of operations
CWB Form 351, record of welding inspectors, test equipment operators and welding inspection supervisor delegates
CWB Form 352, record of test equipment
CWB Form 355, welding inspection supervisor responsibility declaration
Documented welding inspection procedures for each product category in the scope of certification (Clause 9)
Equipment maintenance and calibration records (Clause 10)
Welding inspection personnel records and inspection records (Clause 11)
CSA W178.2 certificates for visual welding inspectors and CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certificates for NDT personnel
auditProcess: Define the scope: which inspection methods and which product categories the certificate is to cover.
Appoint a welding inspection supervisor certified to CSA W178.2 Level 3, dedicated to this organization or designated section under Clause 7.1, and name any delegates under Clause 7.2.2.
Submit Form 350 with Forms 333, 351, 352 and 355 and the supporting quality documentation; a multi-site organization may designate a single Certification Contact under Clause 5.3.
CWB reviews the submission against Clause 5 (obtaining certification), Clause 7 (personnel), Clause 8 (methods), Clause 9 (procedures), Clause 10 (equipment) and Clause 11 (records).
CWB conducts the certification audit, verifying that inspection procedures exist for every product category in scope and that calibration and records controls function in practice.
Non-conformances are closed and the certificate is issued for the defined methods and product categories.
Certification is maintained by an annual third-party CWB audit under Clause 6.
industries: Structural steel — buildings, bridges, industrial structures
Machinery, cranes, rail and road vehicles
Mobile drilling units and steel fixed offshore structures
Pressure vessels, boilers and heat exchangers
renewal: Certification is maintained by an annual third-party audit conducted by the CWB Group under Clause 6; there is no multi-year gap between surveillance visits. The standard itself was published in May 2018 as the seventh edition, superseding editions of 2014, 2008, 2002, 1996, 1990 and 1973, and was reaffirmed in 2023 as W178.1:18 (R2023). CWB quoted the standard document at CAD 180.00 at the time it published its July 2018 change summary; CWB certification, application and audit fees are quoted separately and are not published on the public certification page.
commonFindings: The named welding inspection supervisor also appears as supervisor at another certified organization or section, contrary to Clause 7.1
Delegates used without documentation of the minimum knowledge and experience Clause 7.2.2 requires
Final written inspection reports issued without the review and sign-off Clause 7.2.6 requires
No documented inspection procedure for one of the product categories listed on the certificate
Equipment calibration overdue or calibration records incomplete against Clause 10
NDT performed in a method that appears in the firm's marketing but sits outside the certified scope
NDT technician holds ASNT certification only, where CAN/CGSB-48.9712 is required
Welding inspection personnel and inspection records not retained and controlled as Clause 11 requires
sources: Verified August 2026 against: CSA W178.1:18 (R2023), seventh edition, published May 2018, per CSA Group and ANSI Webstore listings; CWB Group technical bulletin "CSA W178.1-18 Certification of Welding Inspection Organizations — Overview of Changes in the 2018 Edition", dated July 2018, read in full, which sets out the eleven-clause structure and describes the Clause 5.3 Certification Contact and the Clause 7.1, 7.2.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.6 and 7.2.8 changes and quotes their operative wording; CWB Group "Inspection Company Certification" page, read 2026, for scope statement, Forms 333, 350, 351, 352 and 355, the inspection and testing methods, the product categories, and the annual third-party audit.

name: CSA W178.2, Certification of welding inspectors
authority: CSA Group publishes the standard; Clause 4.1 assigns administration to the Canadian Welding Bureau (CWB), which assesses candidates, issues certificates and maintains the public directory
appliesTo: Individual welding inspectors, and the inspection organizations that must staff a CSA W178.1 certificate or satisfy a fabricator's or owner's contract. Anyone signing visual welding inspection reports in Canada under a code that calls up W178.2 needs a current certificate at the level matching the duties performed, plus an open-book endorsement on the specific product code being inspected.
summary: CSA W178.2-18, published May 2018, certifies welding inspectors at three levels. Under Clause 4 the CWB administers the standard, assesses candidates, issues certificates and makes a public directory of certified inspectors available. The standard defines the technical duties at each level, sets experience and training prerequisites, prescribes the examinations including an open-book examination on at least one product code, sets a near-vision requirement, and fixes a three-year certificate validity with a six-year recertification cycle. Clause 1.6 draws the boundary that matters most to an NDT firm: W178.2 does not address certification of individuals performing radiographic, ultrasonic, eddy current, magnetic particle or liquid penetrant examinations.
personnelCertification: Central and third-party — the CWB is the sole administrator and assessor, and an employer-issued welding inspector certificate carries no standing under this standard. Clause 8.2.7 lets the CWB grant equivalent certification to the holder of a valid welding inspector certificate issued by another jurisdiction who has met requirements equivalent to Clauses 8.1 and 8.2, but that is a CWB decision, not an employer's. Clause 6 f) of the code of ethics requires an inspector to sign only for work he has inspected or has personal knowledge of through direct technical control, which sets a hard limit on how far any remote or outsourced signatory can go.
requiredDocuments: CWB Form 301, Welding Inspector Application Guide for CSA Standard W178.2
CWB Form 455, near vision acuity record
CWB Form 457, proof of continuing involvement in welding examination or testing
Documented welding and inspection experience covering the acceptable areas listed in Clause 8.1.2
Evidence of recognized courses, or of a CWB-recognized Welding Engineering Technology or Welding Engineering programme
Record of the code and standard endorsements held under Clause 8.2.6 and Annex B
CWB Form 463, welding inspector stamp record
Evidence for the 40 hours of instruction claimed under Clause 10.5.1 b), with proof of attendance, session length, subjects covered and any examination result
auditProcess: Establish eligibility under Clause 8.1.1: one year of experience for Level 1, or six months plus recognized courses in welding fundamentals, quality control and welding inspection, or a CWB-recognized Welding Engineering Technology or Welding Engineering programme.

Progress by documented time in the duties: two further years at Level 1 for Level 2 (examinations may be written at 18 months), four further years at Level 2 for Level 3 (examinations at three and a half years). Direct entry needs five years of prior welding inspection experience for Level 2 or ten years for Level 3; two years of related teaching experience can support direct application at Level 2.
Meet the vision requirement of Clause 8.3 — Jaeger number 1 or Times Roman N4.5 or equivalent, letter height 1.6 mm, at not less than 30 cm, with one or both eyes, corrected or uncorrected.
Pass the examinations for the level sought, always including an open-book examination on the content of CSA W178.2 and an open-book examination on at least one product code or standard from Annex B.
CWB issues the certificate, valid for three years under Clauses 9.1 and 10.1, and lists the holder in the public directory.
Renew every three years under Clause 10.2 with Form 455 and evidence of continuing involvement; an inspector who does not renew before expiry is decertified under Clause 10.2.3.
Recertify at six years under Clause 10.5 by passing the practical visual examination, or by completing 40 hours of instruction acceptable to the CWB within three years of the recertification date.
industries: Structural steel — buildings, bridges, industrial structures
Machinery, cranes, rail and road vehicles
Offshore structures and mobile drilling units
Pressure vessels, boilers and heat exchangers
renewal: Certificates are valid for three years (Clauses 9.1 and 10.1). Renewal is required every three years from initial certification and needs evidence of satisfactory vision and of continuing involvement in welding examination or testing; an inspector who does not renew before the expiry date is decertified. Recertification is required every six years from initial certification and is satisfied either by an examination on the visual detection, identification and descriptive reporting of weld faults, dimensional faults, material deficiencies and structural discontinuities and their assessment against defined acceptance criteria, or by 40 hours of instruction acceptable to the CWB completed within three years of the recertification date, in subjects such as visual welding inspection, non-destructive examination of welds, quality assurance or quality control, and codes and standards. A decertified inspector must rewrite all qualifying examinations for the level sought.
commonFindings: Level 1 inspector working without the qualified supervision Clause 5.3 requires
Reports signed against a product code for which the inspector holds no open-book endorsement under Clause 8.2.6
Certificate lapsed because renewal was submitted after the expiry date, triggering decertification under Clause 10.2.3
Form 455 near vision acuity record missing or out of date
Form 457 evidence of continuing involvement not retained by the employer
40 hours of recertification instruction claimed but completed outside the three-year window in Clause 10.5.1 b)
Course with a built-in examination component claimed for recertification without evidence the examination was passed
W178.2 certificate offered as evidence of competence for UT or RT work, which Clause 1.6 explicitly excludes
sources: Verified August 2026 against the full text of CSA W178.2-18, Certification of welding inspectors, published May 2018 by CSA Group, ISBN 978-1-4883-1383-1, Standards Update Service list ID 2426105 — Clauses 1.1 to 1.8, 2 (reference publications, which cite CAN/CSA-W117.2-12 (R2017) and CAN/CGSB-48.9712-2014/ISO 9712:2012), 3, 4.1 to 4.4, 5, 6, 7.1 to 7.4.2, 8.1.1 to 8.3, 9.1, 9.2, 10.1 to 10.5.2 and Annexes A to C read directly. Supplemented by CWB Group "Visual Welding Inspector Certification" page, read 2026, for Forms 301, 455, 457, 463 and 1049 and the CWB Form 301E/2026-6 application guide.

name: Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission licensing and personnel certification for inspection service providers
authority: Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC), acting under the Nuclear Safety and Control Act and its regulations
appliesTo: Any inspection service provider that possesses, uses or transports sealed radioactive sources or exposure devices in Canada — in practice, every firm offering gamma radiography — and any firm supplying non-destructive examination services to a nuclear facility licensee. It binds the company through its licence and the technician through his CNSC certification; neither one substitutes for the other, and both are checked.
summary: The CNSC does not certify NDT methods. It licenses the company and certifies the person who operates an exposure device. An inspection provider doing industrial radiography needs a Nuclear Substances and Radiation Devices licence covering use type 812, a named Radiation Safety Officer with documented training including a source retrieval course, a radiation protection programme built on ALARA, dosimetry from a CNSC-licensed dosimetry service, an Emergency and Operating Procedures manual, sealed source leak-test and device maintenance records, and certified Exposure Device Operators. On nuclear plant pressure-retaining components the NDE method certification requirement comes from the CSA N285 series and points at CAN/CGSB-48.9712 rather than at any CNSC document.
personnelCertification: Two separate things, and firms conflate them. Exposure Device Operator certification is central: the CNSC certifies EDOs under the Nuclear Substances and Radiation Devices Regulations, and no person other than a certified EDO, or a trainee acting under the direct supervision and continuous observation of one, may operate an exposure device. No employer written practice substitutes. NDE method certification inside Canadian nuclear work runs to CAN/CGSB-48.9712 for radiographic, ultrasonic, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant and eddy current methods, with one documented carve-out: for ASME-stamped components, SNT-TC-1A qualification has been accepted where the authorized inspection agency and the licensee both agree.
requiredDocuments: Nuclear Substances and Radiation Devices licence covering use type 812 for industrial radiography
Completed "Request to Appoint a Radiation Safety Officer" form, with an RSO job description setting out roles, responsibilities, qualifications and authority
RSO training course certificate and, for use type 812, a source retrieval course training certificate
Emergency and Operating Procedures (EOP) manual
Radiation protection programme documentation demonstrating dose control and ALARA
Dosimetry records obtained from a CNSC-licensed dosimetry service
Sealed source leak testing records, and quarterly and annual exposure device maintenance records
Valid CNSC Exposure Device Operator certification cards for every operator, plus training logs for trainees
Transport package registration and packaging documentation, one registration per certificate number
auditProcess: Apply for the licence following REGDOC-1.6.1, Licence Application Guide: Nuclear Substances and Radiation Devices, selecting the use types the work requires.

Appoint and evidence the Radiation Safety Officer, including the job description, qualifications, RSO training certificate and the source retrieval course certificate required for industrial radiography.

Submit the radiation protection programme, the Emergency and Operating Procedures manual, operating procedures, safety and emergency equipment inventory, and personnel qualifications for specialised incident response.
CNSC reviews the application and issues the licence with conditions limiting activities, locations, nuclear substances and devices.

Certify the operators: candidates complete vocational and on-the-job training, then pass the written examination — the NRCan NDTCB is the qualifying body for the EDO written examination — and the practical examination.

Operate under continuing obligations: dosimetry through a licensed service, leak testing, quarterly and annual device maintenance records, and notification to the CNSC within 15 days of a change in the RSO or the RSO position.
CNSC compliance verification through desktop review and on-site inspection, followed by licence renewal on its stated term.
industries: Nuclear fuel cycle and waste management
Oil and gas construction and fabrication
renewal: Exposure Device Operator certification is renewed every five years. Renewal requires documentary evidence of successful completion of the EDO practical examination, and a written examination is additionally required after a significant interruption in work. Since 1 January 2017 only EDO cards issued on or after 1 February 2013 are recognised, and cards must not be expired. The CNSC expects the practical examination to be administered by a certified EDO who administers examinations at an NRCan Authorized Examination Centre, or who has held certification for at least five years, or who has been authorised by their licensed employer to conduct practical examinations. Company licences run for the term stated on the licence and are renewed by application; dose limits for nuclear energy workers under the Radiation Protection Regulations are 50 mSv in a one-year dosimetry period and 100 mSv over five consecutive years, with a licensed dosimetry service required where there is a reasonable probability of exceeding 5 mSv in a year.
commonFindings: An uncertified worker operating an exposure device, or a trainee not under direct supervision and continuous observation
Change of Radiation Safety Officer not reported to the CNSC within 15 days
Dosimetry obtained from a service not licensed by the CNSC where doses above 5 mSv per year are reasonably probable
Quarterly or annual exposure device maintenance records missing or incomplete
Sealed source leak test overdue against the licence condition
Emergency and Operating Procedures manual not current, or not available at the work site
RSO appointed without the source retrieval course certificate required for use type 812
EDO card issued before 1 February 2013 still being presented as valid
Transport packaging used without the corresponding package registration
sources: Verified August 2026 against CNSC published regulatory documents and pages: REGDOC-2.2.3, Personnel Certification, Volume I: Exposure Device Operators, Version 1.1, last modified 19 December 2022, made under the Nuclear Substances and Radiation Devices Regulations pursuant to the Nuclear Safety and Control Act, which references CSA PCP-09, Exposure Device Operator Personnel Certification Guide – Revision 1, published August 2021; REGDOC-1.6.1, Licence Application Guide: Nuclear Substances and Radiation Devices, Version 2.1 (Version 2 superseded Version 1 of October 2015), for use type 812 and the application content; REGDOC-2.5.7, Design, Testing and Performance of Exposure Devices, Version 1.1; REGDOC-2.7.1, Radiation Protection, and REGDOC-2.7.2, Dosimetry, Volumes I and II; Radiation Protection Regulations (SOR/2000-203) for dose limits and the licensed dosimetry service threshold; CNSC "Exposure device operators" and "Certified exposure device operators" pages. The NRCan NDTCB role as qualifying body for the EDO written examination is confirmed on the NRCan NDTCB FAQs page. The Canadian nuclear NDE certification position (CAN/CGSB-48.9712 required, SNT-TC-1A accepted for ASME-stamped components with AIA and licensee agreement) is taken from WNA CORDEL report 2014/003, "Certification of NDE Personnel — Harmonization of International Code Requirements", October 2014, and should be re-checked against the current CSA N285.0 and N285.4 editions (N285.4:23 is the eighth edition) before being relied on contractually.

name: CSA Z662, Oil and gas pipeline systems
authority: CSA Group publishes the standard; it is incorporated by reference into the Canada Energy Regulator's Onshore Pipeline Regulations and adopted by provincial energy regulators including the BC Energy Regulator, the Alberta Energy Regulator and TSSA in Ontario
appliesTo: NDT and inspection contractors on oil and gas pipeline construction, maintenance and integrity work in Canada, and the pipeline companies that hire them. Because CSA Z662 is incorporated by reference into the Canada Energy Regulator's Onshore Pipeline Regulations and adopted provincially, its inspection clauses carry the force of law for federally and provincially regulated pipelines alike.
summary: CSA Z662:23, the ninth edition, was released on 30 June 2023 and covers pipelines from design through construction, operation, maintenance, deactivation and abandonment, with a new clause for hydrogen and hydrogen-blend systems. For an inspection service provider the operative content sits in Clause 7: mandatory non-destructive inspection extents, documented and company-approved NDI procedures, standards of acceptability, production and retention of radiographs, and ultrasonic inspection of circumferential butt welds. Personnel qualification is pinned to CAN/CGSB-48.9712 — radiographers, with radiographic image interpretation at Level 2 or 3, and ultrasonic inspectors at Level 2 or 3. Since the 2019 edition a CGSB Level 3 must review and approve non-destructive inspection procedures.
personnelCertification: Central certification only. Clause 7.14.8.1 requires radiographers to be qualified as specified in CAN/CGSB-48.9712, with radiographic image interpretation at Level 2 or 3; Clause 7.15.6 requires ultrasonic inspectors to be qualified to Level 2 or 3; and confirmation of complete crack removal by liquid penetrant or wet magnetic particle inspection must be by inspectors qualified to the same standard. There is no employer written practice route. This is exactly where an outsourced Level III earns his place: the requirement introduced in Z662:19 and carried into Z662:23 that a CGSB Level 3 review and approve non-destructive inspection procedures is a signature a pipeline contractor can buy in.
requiredDocuments: Documented non-destructive inspection procedures, approved by the company and reviewed and approved by a CGSB Level 3

Documented visual inspection procedures covering extent and frequency of visual inspection, personnel qualification and visual acuity, maximum viewing distance and angle, lighting conditions, evaluation tools and reporting (Clause 7.10.2.1)
Visual inspection reports carrying weld identification, description, position and length of defects, date, and the signature of the qualified visual inspector (Clause 7.10.2.3)
Visual inspection records retained until the piping is abandoned (Clause 7.10.2.4) and radiographic records retained per Clause 7.14.9
Ultrasonic calibration and reference-level records — reference at 80% full screen height and recording at 40%, six decibels below reference, in the edition verified
CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certificates for radiographers, radiographic image interpreters and ultrasonic inspectors
Records demonstrating that welds selected for daily non-destructive inspection were reasonably representative of daily production
Search unit and equipment performance records against the referenced specification, with repair or replacement criteria established by the manufacturer or the inspection company
auditProcess: Confirm which edition governs. The Canada Energy Regulator incorporates the latest version of CSA Z662 by reference through section 4 and paragraph 4(1)(d) of the Onshore Pipeline Regulations, so a new edition takes effect on publication rather than on a separate adoption date.
Write the non-destructive inspection procedures and have them reviewed and approved by a CGSB Level 3, then approved by the pipeline company as Clause 7.10.4.1 requires.
Qualify personnel to CAN/CGSB-48.9712 in the correct method, with Level 2 or 3 for radiographic image interpretation (Clause 7.14.8.1) and for ultrasonic inspection (Clause 7.15.6).

Agree the inspection extent against Clause 7.10.3 — full-length inspection at uncased road and railway crossings, at water crossings and on pressure-retaining welds that will not be pressure tested in place, plus a daily percentage of other production welds; carbon dioxide pipelines and partial-penetration butt welds are treated separately.
Execute and record inspection to the approved procedures, evaluating results against Clause 7.11 or, at the company's option and where the conditions are met, Annex K.

Company surveillance or audit of the contractor, including the company's right under Clause 7.14.8.2 to examine radiographer qualifications and under Clause 7.15.6 to require ultrasonic inspectors to demonstrate competence.
renewal: CSA Z662 is revised on a roughly four-year cycle — 1994, 1996, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2011, 2015, 2019, 2023 — and Z662:23 is the ninth edition, released 30 June 2023. Because the Onshore Pipeline Regulations incorporate the latest version by reference, a new edition takes effect on publication rather than on an adoption date. The Canada Energy Regulator's Information Advisory IA 2023-001 told companies to review Z662:23 and take the steps needed to comply as soon as possible, and to demonstrate for pending applications how projects would meet the new requirements. There is no certificate to renew under this regime; what expires is the personnel certification behind it and the currency of the procedures written to it.
commonFindings: Non-destructive inspection procedure approved by an ASNT Level III rather than by a CGSB Level 3
Radiographic image interpretation performed by a Level 1 where Clause 7.14.8.1 requires Level 2 or 3
Visual inspection procedure silent on maximum viewing distance and angle, lighting conditions or evaluation tools, all of which Clause 7.10.2.1 requires it to address
Visual inspection reports missing the signature of the qualified visual inspector required by Clause 7.10.2.3
Daily non-destructive inspection selection not demonstrably representative of that day's production
Radiographic records not retained, or visual inspection records disposed of before the piping was abandoned
Ultrasonic reference and recording levels not set as the approved procedure requires
Contractor procedures still written to a superseded edition after Z662:23 came into force on 30 June 2023
sources: Verified August 2026 against: CSA Z662:23, ninth edition, released 30 June 2023, per CSA Group and ANSI Webstore listings, which record it as superseding the 2019, 2015, 2011, 2007, 2003, 1999, 1996 and 1994 editions; Canada Energy Regulator Information Advisory IA 2023-001, confirming the 30 June 2023 in-force date and incorporation by reference through section 4 and paragraph 4(1)(d) of the Onshore Pipeline Regulations; the CSA Z662:19 table of contents, confirming clause numbering for 7.10, 7.11, 7.14 (including 7.14.8 Radiographers and 7.14.9) and 7.15 (including 7.15.6 Qualification of ultrasonic inspectors); and the verbatim text of Clauses 7.10.2, 7.10.3, 7.10.4, 7.14.8 and 7.15.6 read from a CSA Z662-11 excerpt filed as exhibit 76 in South Dakota PUC docket HP14-001. Clause numbering was unchanged between those editions, but inspection percentages and ultrasonic reference levels should be confirmed against the edition in force. The requirement for a CGSB Level 3 to review and approve non-destructive inspection procedures is reported in the Z662:19 and Z662:23 change summaries published by standards distributors; it was not read from the clause text and should be confirmed against a purchased copy before it is relied on contractually.

name: Norma Regulamentadora nº 13 — Caldeiras, Vasos de Pressão, Tubulações e Tanques Metálicos de Armazenamento
authority: Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE), which publishes the Normas Regulamentadoras; enforced on site by Auditores-Fiscais do Trabalho
appliesTo: Every Brazilian employer operating boilers above 60 kPa operating pressure, pressure vessels whose P·V product exceeds 8 or which contain class A fluids, interconnecting piping carrying class A or B fluids, and metallic storage tanks over 3 m external diameter and 20,000 litres nominal capacity. Inspection service providers are bound indirectly but absolutely: the employer must be able to prove that every inspection, test and NDT report it buys satisfies NR-13.
summary: NR-13 places the legal duty on the employer, not the contractor, and that shapes how inspection service providers sell into Brazil. Every safety inspection must be executed under the technical responsibility of a Profissional Legalmente Habilitado (PLH) — item 13.3.3. Selection of examinations and tests, hydrostatic and pneumatic test procedures, interval extensions and the consolidated report all rest on that PLH's technical judgement, and the report must carry the PLH's legible name, signature and professional-council registration number. A provider supplying only NDT technicians cannot sign; it must employ a Brazil-registered engineer or work under the client's PLH. Metallic storage tanks entered scope on 4 July 2026, opening a substantial new inspection market.
personnelCertification: Two separate requirements, and confusing them is the classic and expensive mistake. The PLH is not an NDT Level III: item 13.3.2 defines it as a person legally competent to practise engineering in Brazil under the prevailing professional regulation, so an ASNT Level III without Brazilian engineering registration cannot sign an NR-13 inspection report. Certification of the PLH's competences is voluntary, through an Organismo de Certificação de Pessoas accredited by Cgcre/Inmetro, with recertification every sixty months (Annex III). For NDT technicians, Annex II requires contracted NDT labour to be certified under prevailing regulation, and Inmetro's SPIE requirements make that ABNT NBR NM ISO 9712 — central third-party certification, not an employer written practice.
requiredDocuments: Prontuário da caldeira / prontuário do vaso de pressão — manufacturer's data book, including construction code and edition, material specification, PMTA methodology, fabrication hydrostatic test records, safety-device data and category (items 13.4.1.5 a and 13.5.1.5 a)

Registro de Segurança — a numbered-page book, folder set or computerised system recording all occurrences affecting safety, interval changes, and initial, periodic and extraordinary inspections with the equipment's operational condition
Projeto de Instalação — boiler installation design, authored under the responsibility of a PLH (item 13.4.2.1)
Projeto de Alteração ou Reparo
Relatórios de Inspeção de Segurança — initial, periodic and extraordinary, with the prescribed minimum content
Certificados de inspeção e teste dos dispositivos de segurança
Manual de operação, kept current and in Portuguese, for every boiler (item 13.4.3.1)
Folhas de dados dos tanques — storage tank data sheets needed to plan and execute inspection (item 13.7.1.2 a)
Plano e programa de inspeção approved by the PLH, including any documented risk-based inspection methodology integrated into the PGR under NR-01
auditProcess: Classification — the employer confirms scope under item 13.2.1 and categorises each boiler as A (operating pressure at or above 1,960 kPa) or B (above 60 kPa and below 1,960 kPa) and each pressure vessel into categories I to V.

Initial safety inspection before the equipment enters service at its definitive installation location, comprising internal examination, external examination and a pressure test, under PLH technical responsibility; fabrication-stage hydrostatic testing evidenced by a report signed by a PLH.
Inspection programme and plan drawn up and approved by the PLH, defining the examinations and tests per applicable codes and the equipment's history.

Periodic safety inspections at the maximum intervals of item 13.4.4.4 (boilers) and Table 2 (pressure vessels), with outcomes and operational condition entered in the Registro de Segurança and signed by the PLH and, for boilers, the operator present.
Extraordinary inspection after accidental damage, significant repair or alteration, relocation, or extended idleness (over 12 months for vessels, over 24 months for tanks).

Enforcement — Auditores-Fiscais do Trabalho examine the documentation on site. NR-13 issues no certificate of any kind; the only certificate route is the voluntary SPIE scheme of Annex II, certified by an Inmetro-accredited OCP.
methodsInScope: Hydrostatic and pneumatic pressure testing (not NDT, but ordered by the same clauses)
industries: Pulp and paper (alkali recovery boilers are named explicitly)
renewal: Boilers, periodic internal and external examination (item 13.4.4.4): maximum 12 months for categories A and B; 18 months for alkali recovery boilers of any category; 24 months for category A provided safety valve opening pressures are tested at 12 months; 30 months for category B with a combustion management system meeting Annex IV.
