Establishments holding a certified SPIE may extend to 24 months (alkali recovery and category B), 30 months (category A) and 48 months (category A with a Safety Instrumented System meeting Annex IV). Pressure vessels follow Table 2 by category I to V — external examination at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 years and internal at 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10 years; with a certified SPIE, external at 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 years and internal at 6, 8, 10 and 12 years, with category V internal at technical criterion. A certified SPIE using a documented risk-based methodology may extend further, capped at 10 years for internal examination of category I vessels. Piping follows the internal interval of the most critical connected vessel or boiler and may be doubled on the PLH's technical justification, capped at 10 years. Boilers reaching 25 years of use undergo a broader integrity assessment at the following inspection. Postponement of up to six months is possible with a risk assessment coordinated by a PLH, and must be formally justified to the predominant workers' union.
commonFindings: Consolidated inspection report signed by an NDT Level III or a senior technician rather than by a PLH — the report content lists require the PLH's legible name, signature and professional-council registration number

Prontuário incomplete or missing the PMTA calculation memory; item 13.4.1.6 requires reconstitution under the technical responsibility of the manufacturer or a PLH, and functional characteristics, safety-device data and the PMTA calculation are non-negotiable
Registro de Segurança that does not record the equipment's operational condition, or lacks the boiler operator's signature alongside the PLH's at the time of inspection (item 13.4.1.8 b)
Contracted NDT technicians holding employer-issued or foreign certificates with no SNQC certificate for the method and industrial sector

Interval extension claimed under SPIE rules by an establishment that holds no SPIE certificate, or a risk-based extension applied without the documented methodology integrated into the PGR under NR-01 (item 13.5.4.5.2)
Inspection postponed without the formal justification communicated to the predominant workers' union required by item 13.3.1.1.1
Metallic storage tanks, in scope since 4 July 2026, with no data sheets, no inspection programme and no Registro de Segurança
Safety valve opening-pressure tests overdue against the 12-month cycle relied on to justify a 24-month interval for a category A boiler
sources: NR-13 consolidated text published by the Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego on gov.br (file nr-13-atualizada-2023-b.pdf), extracted and read directly. Current wording given by Portaria nº 1.846 of 1 July 2022 (DOU 4 July 2022) — cited within the norm's own publication table as Portaria MTP nº 1.846 and in the body text as Portaria MTb nº 1.846 — amended by Portaria MTP nº 4.219 of 20 December 2022 (DOU 22 December 2022), with rectifications dated 20 October 2022. Parent instrument Portaria MTb nº 3.214 of 8 June 1978 (DOU 6 July 1978). Storage-tank scope commencement of 4 July 2026 from the note to item 13.2.1 f citing art. 3 of Portaria MTP nº 1.846/22; piping scope commencement of 20 March 2018 from the note to item 13.6.2.1 citing art. 6. Verified 21 August 2026.

name: Sistema Nacional de Qualificação e Certificação de Pessoas em Ensaios Não Destrutivos (SNQC/END)
authority: ABENDI — Associação Brasileira de Ensaios Não Destrutivos e Inspeção, acting as an Organismo de Certificação de Pessoas (OPC) accredited by the Coordenação Geral de Acreditação (Cgcre) of Inmetro
appliesTo: Individual NDT practitioners rather than firms — but it binds firms hard, because Inmetro's SPIE requirements, Petrobras fabrication inspection specifications and most Brazilian industrial buyers all demand SNQC-certified technicians. Any inspection service provider staffing work in Brazil, including a foreign firm mobilising a crew for a turnaround, must field individually SNQC-certified people in the specific method, level and industrial sector concerned.
summary: SNQC is Brazil's national NDT personnel certification scheme. ABENDI began building it in the early 1980s, brought it into national operation at the end of that decade and has issued certificates since the early 1990s under its own scheme document NA-001, which implements ISO 9712. For a service provider this is a hiring and mobilisation constraint, not a company certification to buy: ABENDI certifies people, and a firm demonstrates capability by holding a clean file of its technicians' valid certificates. Certificates are granted per method, per level and per industrial sector, so a technician certified for the oil and petrochemical sector is not automatically covered for steel, aerospace or nuclear work.
personnelCertification: Central, third-party certification — the single most important fact for anyone selling outsourced Level III services into Brazil. ABENDI issues the certificate as an accredited personnel certification body operating to ABNT NBR ISO/IEC 17024; the employer certifies nobody, and an SNT-TC-1A written practice signed by a contracted Level III carries no standing in the scheme. An outsourced Level III can still write and approve procedures, train candidates and act as a firm's technical authority, but only if that individual personally holds a valid SNQC Level 3 in the relevant method and sector. Foreign ASNT or PCN credentials do not convert automatically; the individual sits SNQC examinations.
requiredDocuments: Certificado SNQC for each technician, stating the method, level, sublevel where applicable, and industrial sector
Formulário de solicitação de certificação — the application lodged with ABENDI for a specific method, level and sector
Comprovação de treinamento — training records evidencing hours per method and level
Comprovação de experiência industrial, attested by the employer for the method and level claimed
Atestado de acuidade visual — near-vision and colour-contrast examination records
Registros de exames de qualificação — general, specific and practical examination results, held by ABENDI
Procedimentos de END approved by a Level 3 holding SNQC certification in the method concerned
Evidence of recertification at the end of the certificate's validity period
auditProcess: Application to ABENDI naming the method, level and industrial sector, supported by training and experience evidence.
Eligibility screening — ABENDI verifies training hours, documented industrial experience and a current vision examination before admitting the candidate to examination.

Qualification examinations — general, specific and practical components. Level 3 candidates additionally sit a basic examination covering technical knowledge of materials science and process technology, knowledge of the SNQC scheme itself, and knowledge of NDT methods at Level 2.
Impartial analysis and decision by ABENDI personnel or a committee formally designated for the purpose and not involved in conducting the examinations.
Formalisation — ABENDI issues the certificate naming the NDT method, level and sublevel, and the industrial sector qualified for.
Surveillance through the validity period and recertification at its end.
methodsInScope: US — ultrasonic testing, with sublevels including thickness measurement, welds, forgings, laminates, phased array and TOFD
Subsea and underwater inspection methods, including ROV-deployed thickness and electrochemical potential measurement
renewal: ABENDI publishes that certification at any of the three levels is valid for sixty months, after which recertification is required. The scheme follows ISO 9712's structure, in which continued validity depends on maintaining satisfactory vision records and continuity of activity in the method. Do not quote a recertification route — examination versus a documented structured-credit path — to a client without reading the current NA-001 revision, which has been revised many times and had reached at least Rev 34; ABENDI announced in February 2023 that SNQC was being updated to align with the new ISO 9712 edition, the first in roughly ten years.
commonFindings: Technician holds a valid SNQC certificate for a different industrial sector than the work performed — steel-sector certification used on refinery pressure equipment is the classic case
Phased array or TOFD performed by a technician holding only a general ultrasonic certificate with no corresponding sublevel
NDT procedures approved by a Level III whose SNQC certification has lapsed, or who holds only ASNT credentials
Vision examination records stale, or missing the colour-contrast assessment
Mobilisation packs not reconciled against ABENDI's register, so expired certificates travel to site
Employer experience attestations that do not evidence the hours or the specific method claimed on the application
Level 1 technicians interpreting and signing results rather than working under Level 2 supervision
sources: ABENDI scheme document NA-001, 'Qualificação e Certificação de Pessoas em Ensaios Não Destrutivos', which implements ISO 9712 and governs SNQC/END; ABENDI's certification pages at www1.abendi.org.br/certificacao for methods, sublevels, levels and industrial sectors; ABENDI's article 'Nova edição da Norma ISO 9712', published 27 February 2023, for the SNQC realignment to the new ISO 9712 edition. ABENDI's accreditation by Inmetro as an Organismo de Certificação de Pessoas under ABNT NBR ISO/IEC 17024, and the sixty-month certificate validity, from ABENDI's published SNQC material. Limitation: the abendi.org.br host — which serves the NA-001 PDF and the SNQC history page — refused connections from this environment on 21 August 2026, so the current NA-001 revision number, the precise recertification route and ABENDI's OPC accreditation number were not read from the primary documents and are deliberately not stated here. Verified 21 August 2026.

name: Instituto Nacional de Metrologia, Qualidade e Tecnologia — Coordenação Geral de Acreditação (Cgcre)
authority: Inmetro, a federal body under the Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços; accreditation is performed by its Coordenação Geral de Acreditação (Cgcre), described by Inmetro as the only accreditation body recognised by the Brazilian government
appliesTo: Inspection bodies, testing and calibration laboratories, and certification bodies operating in Brazil. Two routes matter to an NDT service provider: accreditation as an Organismo de Inspeção Acreditado under ISO/IEC 17020, where Inmetro maintains a specific non-destructive testing scope; and, for an industrial end user's in-house inspection department, certification of a Serviço Próprio de Inspeção de Equipamentos (SPIE) under NR-13's Annex II, whose conformity assessment requirements Inmetro writes and owns.
summary: Cgcre is the gatekeeper for anything in Brazil entitled to be called accredited. It accredits inspection bodies against ABNT NBR ISO/IEC 17020, testing and calibration laboratories against ISO/IEC 17025, personnel certification bodies against ISO/IEC 17024, product certification bodies against ISO/IEC 17065 and validation/verification bodies against ISO/IEC 17029. For an inspection service provider, accreditation converts a technically competent crew into a report a regulator or a demanding client accepts without argument. Separately, Inmetro owns the SPIE conformity assessment requirements that NR-13 makes available to equipment owners, consolidated in Portaria Inmetro nº 62 of 31 March 2026 — the document that decides, in practice, what a Brazilian plant demands of its NDT subcontractors.
personnelCertification: Inmetro does not certify NDT people; it accredits the bodies that do, under ABNT NBR ISO/IEC 17024, which is how ABENDI's SNQC acquires its legal weight. In the SPIE requirements consolidated by Portaria Inmetro nº 62/2026, clause 5.1.3.11 a requires NDT inspectors to hold the qualification and certification of ABNT NBR NM ISO 9712, welding inspectors ABNT NBR 14842 and painting inspectors ABNT NBR 15218. Employer-issued certification is not accepted for those roles. Clause 5.1.3.12 is the only relief valve: for NDT methods not covered by national standards, an international qualification or documented formal training from the manufacturer or technology owner may be required instead.
requiredDocuments: Solicitação formal de certificação to the OCP, with a detailed description of the establishment, its location, general layout and the geographic distribution of operating units (SPIE clause 6.2)
Information on activities performed by third parties and outsourced installations capable of affecting the certification, including equipment connected to SPIE equipment
Types and quantities of equipment controlled, NR-13 classification, available human resources with their locations, functions and competences
Programa e plano de inspeção, with evidence of minimum compliance with the programme
Procedimentos escritos for the principal activities performed
Arquivo técnico — the maintained, current technical file needed to satisfy NR-13, with mechanisms to distribute information on request
Registros de qualificação e certificação for own and contracted personnel, including ABNT NBR NM ISO 9712 certificates for NDT inspectors
Lista atualizada da aparelhagem de inspeção with calibration records and traceability to nationally or internationally recognised standards
Registros de auditorias internas and the internal audit procedure covering auditor qualification, experience and independence
Relatório de inspeção consolidado signed by the PLH, with contracted NDT reports annexed, referenced and technically validated by that PLH
auditProcess: Formal application to an Organismo de Certificação de Produtos (OCP) established in Brazil and accredited by Inmetro, submitting the establishment description, equipment inventory and resource information.

Initial audit planning — the OCP builds the audit plan, verifies the inspection programme including any overdue items, and defines the sample; the workforce (efetivo) is verified and the checklist prepared.
On-site initial audit against the checklist, with the inspection programme assessed in full and the remaining requirements assessed by sampling.

Non-conformity treatment — Category A RGI deviations must be corrected during the audit period and the audit is interrupted if immediate action is impossible; up to three common Category A non-conformities are permitted subject to an OCP-approved action plan; corrective and preventive action within 90 days.

Critical analysis and decision by a Certification Commission constituted by the OCP with tripartite, equal representation of the Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego, the workers of the establishments and the establishments themselves.
Certificate of Conformity issued, valid 48 months from the date of issue.

Maintenance audits every 12 months from certificate issue, and recertification concluded before the certificate expires — planned like a maintenance audit but decided under the initial-evaluation rules.
methodsInScope: Non-intrusive inspection (INI) and risk-based inspection (IBR) methodologies, which require a specific-scope audit before use
renewal: SPIE certificates are valid for 48 months from issue (clause 6.2.5.3). Maintenance audits run every 12 months from the certificate date. That may be extended to 18 months only where all four conditions hold: certified for at least two certification cycles; no suspension in the last two cycles; no warning in the last cycle; and no Category A non-conformities in the last cycle. The extension takes effect only from the start of the cycle following the request and can be revoked at any time following a major accident, a warning or a suspension. Recertification must be concluded before the current certificate expires. Portaria Inmetro nº 62/2026 revokes Portarias Inmetro nº 537/2015, nº 582/2015, nº 177/2023 and nº 382/2023 twelve months after it takes effect; certificates already issued are updated to reference it at the next evaluation stage, and adoption of INI or a Safety Instrumented System by a certified SPIE requires a specific-scope audit.
commonFindings: Contracted NDT reports annexed to the consolidated inspection report but neither referenced nor technically validated by the responsible PLH, contrary to the SPIE reporting rule
No documented criteria for evaluating the performance of contracted inspection services, or no records of those evaluations (clause 9.2)
Inspection equipment list incomplete, or calibration not traceable to nationally or internationally recognised standards with no documented and periodically reviewed alternative basis (clause 10.5)
Repeated delays in executing the inspection plan detected across successive audit cycles
NDT technicians certified to a scheme other than ABNT NBR NM ISO 9712 with no justification under the clause 5.1.3.12 exception for methods lacking national standards
Non-intrusive or risk-based inspection used to define or postpone intervals before the specific-scope audit required by clause 6.7
Safety valve opening-pressure tests exceeding the 12-month maximum applied to each boiler
No dedicated PLH, or inspection staff lacking the exclusive dedication to inspection, integrity assessment and remaining-life activities that NR-13 Annex II requires
sources: Portaria Inmetro nº 62, de 31 de março de 2026, 'Aprova a Instrução Normativa Inmetro e os Requisitos de Avaliação da Conformidade para os Serviços Próprios de Inspeção de Equipamentos – Consolidado', Annexes I and II, extracted and read directly; it cites Consulta Pública nº 17 of 21 November 2024 (DOU 11 December 2024) and Processo SEI nº 0052600.011368/2022-51, and adopts Portaria Inmetro nº 200/2021 (Requisitos Gerais de Certificação de Produtos, RGCP) as its general certification rules. Cgcre's status as sole recognised accreditation body and the conformity assessment body types and standards from Inmetro's accreditation pages on gov.br. Limitation: the inspection-body scope acronyms — including OIA-END for non-destructive testing and OIA-OG for oil and gas fabrication — come from Inmetro's inspection body accreditation page, but the ftp.inmetro.gov.br and www4.inmetro.gov.br hosts were unreachable from this environment on 21 August 2026, so the scope list was not re-read against the primary page, no accreditation counts are stated, and the accreditation surveillance cycle for OIA is not asserted. Verified 21 August 2026.

name: Petrobras supplier registration (CADASTRO PETROBRAS) and fabrication inspection technical requirements
authority: Petróleos Brasileiros S.A. (Petrobras) as the contracting party; registration administered through the Canal Fornecedor and the Petronect portal, with technical requirements issued as Petrobras N-series standards and ET / I-ET specifications
appliesTo: Companies wanting to supply goods or services to Petrobras — fabrication shops, inspection contractors and NDT service providers among them. It also reaches down the chain: the general fabrication inspection specification applies to direct and indirect purchases whose final client is Petrobras, so a subcontractor two tiers down still inherits the personnel certification rules, and it applies to goods families carrying a Requisito de Qualificação Técnica in the Petrobras register.
summary: Petrobras publishes far more than most national oil companies, which makes this regime unusually researchable. Supplier registration is documented publicly on the Canal Fornecedor, and Petrobras technical specifications and N-series standards are downloadable from the public Petronect content area without a contract. The commercially decisive document for inspection providers is ET-0000.00-0000-972-P8L-001, 'Requisito Geral de Inspeção de Fabricação', which sets minimum fabrication inspection requirements for direct and indirect purchases destined for Petrobras. What Petrobras does not publish is the internal scoring, weighting and thresholds behind supplier evaluation, so nothing should be claimed about how a bid is actually ranked — a distinction worth making explicitly to any client who asks.
personnelCertification: Central certification, with one defined alternative route. Clause 7 of ET-0000.00-0000-972-P8L-001 requires fabrication inspection, welding, dimensional, non-destructive testing, painting and assembly activities to be performed by professionals certified by the Sistema Nacional de Qualificação e Certificação (SNQC), or by professionals meeting the qualification requirements of Petrobras document I-ET-0000.00-0000-970-PSQ-001; it further requires those professionals to be formally involved in every activity and attribution their certification norm assigns them. The specification's reference list names ABNT NBR NM ISO 9712, ABNT NBR 16278 for oil and gas sector fabrication inspection personnel, and ISO/IEC 17024. An employer written practice alone will not satisfy clause 7.
requiredDocuments: Cadastro submission on Petronect, with the questionnaire of general and commercial company information and the products and services offered
Certificado de registro cadastral, issued on successful registration and documented as a distinct component of the supplier programme
Requisito de Qualificação Técnica (RQT) evidence for each goods family being registered
Plano de Inspeção e Testes (PIT), prepared by the supplier to cover all production, installation and associated service processes of the supply
Termo de adequação do procedimento de inspeção por ensaios não destrutivos
Relatórios de ensaios não destrutivos foreseen in the PIT and in the specific inspection requirement
Certificados SNQC — or evidence of the I-ET-0000.00-0000-970-PSQ-001 route — for NDT, welding, dimensional, painting and fabrication inspectors
Relatório de Inspeção de Fabricação, prepared per Annex II of the specification
Documentation supporting the published evaluation dimensions: legal, economic-financial, technical, SMS/HSE and Due Diligence de Integridade
auditProcess: Register on Petronect and complete the Petrobras supplier questionnaire covering general and commercial company information and the products and services offered.
Petrobras evaluates the applicant across the dimensions it publishes: legal, economic-financial, technical, SMS/HSE and integrity (Due Diligence de Integridade).

Technical qualification per goods family against the applicable Requisito de Qualificação Técnica — the stage at which inspection capability, written procedures and certified personnel are actually examined.
Certificado de registro cadastral issued; Petrobras states that registered companies are evaluated more quickly in contracting processes.

On award, fabrication inspection runs against ET-0000.00-0000-972-P8L-001 plus the discipline-specific fabrication inspection requirement, with the PIT as the control document; the edition of every referenced standard is the one in force at the date of contract signature.
Release of fabrication stages — receiving, documentation, PIT preparation, testing and final inspection — by certified fabrication inspectors, with NDT reports as the PIT requires.
methodsInScope: UT — Petrobras N-1594 covers ultrasonic testing of welds
industries: Oil and gas exploration and production
renewal: Petrobras documents the certificado de registro cadastral as a component of the supplier programme and treats registration as something the supplier must keep current. Petrobras does not publish a single fixed validity for technical qualification applicable across all goods families, so no interval should be quoted to a client without checking the specific Requisito de Qualificação Técnica for that family. On the technical side the operative rule is edition control rather than renewal: the specification states that the edition or revision of applicable documents is the one in force at the date of contract signature. Personnel certificates renew on their own scheme's cycle — sixty months for SNQC.
commonFindings: NDT technicians presented with ASNT or other employer-based certificates where clause 7 requires SNQC certification, with no evidence of meeting the I-ET-0000.00-0000-970-PSQ-001 alternative
PIT that does not cover all production, installation and associated service processes of the supply, or that omits the additional inspection requirements defined for the goods family
NDT procedures used without the termo de adequação that the specification requires
Standard editions applied that are not those in force at the date of contract signature
Fabrication stages released by staff who are not certified fabrication inspectors for receiving, documentation, PIT preparation, testing and final inspection
NDT reports that cannot be traced back to the PIT line item they were meant to satisfy
Registration data left stale on Petronect, delaying or blocking participation in a contracting process
sources: Petrobras specification ET-0000.00-0000-972-P8L-001, 'Requisito Geral de Inspeção de Fabricação', Rev. B, dated 20 October 2016 (Rev. A 19 September 2016, Rev. 0 10 November 2015), downloaded from the public Petronect content area and extracted; sections 1 (Objetivo), 2 (Referências), 6 and 7 (Qualificação e Certificação de Pessoal) and 8 (Planejamento da Inspeção de Fabricação) read directly. Supplier registration process, the named evaluation dimensions (legal, economic-financial, technical, SMS, Due Diligence de Integridade), the certificado de registro cadastral, pre-qualification, the Regulamento de Licitações e Contratos and the Catálogo de Padronização from Petrobras's public Canal Fornecedor at canalfornecedor.petrobras.com.br. Petrobras N-1594, N-1595, N-1596, N-1597 and N-1598 titles taken from the specification's own reference list, not from those standards themselves — note in particular that N-1595 is the radiography standard, not a personnel standard. Limitation: I-ET-0000.00-0000-970-PSQ-001 is named in clause 7 but was not retrievable (404 on Petronect), so the alternative qualification route it defines is not characterised here. Verified 21 August 2026.

name: NOM-020-STPS-2011, Recipientes sujetos a presión, recipientes criogénicos y generadores de vapor o calderas — Funcionamiento — Condiciones de seguridad
authority: Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social (STPS); conformity assessed by unidades de inspección (statutory term until 2020: unidades de verificación) that are accredited by an accreditation entity and approved by STPS
appliesTo: Every workplace in Mexican national territory operating pressure vessels, cryogenic vessels, steam generators or boilers, with named exclusions including diving bells, hyperbaric chambers, fire extinguishers, portable compressed-gas cylinders, LPG vessels regulated by the energy ministry and rail tank cars. The commercial market for an inspection provider is Category II and III equipment, which carries mandatory periodic pressure testing or non-destructive examination.
summary: The current designation is confirmed: NOM-020-STPS-2011, published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación on 27 December 2011 and in force from 27 June 2012, superseding NOM-020-STPS-2002, with an authorised alternative procedure published 9 December 2014 and continued validity confirmed by systematic review on 15 August 2022. It is the engine of the Mexican NDT inspection market because it makes periodic non-destructive examination or pressure testing mandatory rather than discretionary for Category II and III equipment. The employer classifies each item into Category I, II or III from fluid hazard, relief-device set pressure and volume, maintains a per-equipment file, and either contracts an accredited inspection unit or — for Category III only — constitutes its own Type B unit.
personnelCertification: Clause 4.21 defines 'personal certificado' as a person with the technical capability and experience to perform, supervise, interpret and evaluate NDT results in accordance with NMX-B-482-1991, or the standards that replace it, or an equivalent. That replacement is NMX-B-482-CANACERO-2016, 'Industria siderúrgica — Capacitación, calificación y certificación de personal en ensayos no destructivos', issued by CANACERO and declared in force in the DOF on 20 October 2016. Crucially, NOM-020 names no accredited certification body for NDT personnel and its 'o equivalente' wording admits other recognised schemes, so an employer-based written practice supported by an outsourced Level III is defensible under the norm itself — unlike Brazil. Client contracts, notably Pemex, routinely override this.
requiredDocuments: Expediente del equipo — the per-equipment file, maintained for each item including Category I equipment
Classification record placing each item in Category I, II or III under clause 7, based on relief-device set pressure, volume and whether the fluid is hazardous
Registro de la última prueba de presión o exámenes no destructivos practicados a los equipos
Resumen cronológico de las pruebas de presión o exámenes no destructivos
Procedimientos for the pressure tests and non-destructive examinations, with the acceptance and rejection criteria applied to results
Records signed by personal certificado endorsing NDT results, and by an engineer with knowledge in the matter endorsing pressure tests (clause 13.2 f and i)
Dictamen de evaluación de la conformidad, or dictamen de evaluación de la conformidad con reporte de servicios where a Type C unit provided the services
Aviso a la Secretaría for Category III equipment, filed within sixty days of the dictamen, together with the STPS-assigned número de control
Registros de capacitación — theoretical and practical training records for workers who operate, maintain, repair and test the equipment (clause 17)
auditProcess: Classify each item into Category I, II or III per clause 7 and Table 1, using the set pressure of the relief device, the volume, and whether the fluid is hazardous.
Build and maintain the per-equipment file, operating and maintenance procedures, and train the workers involved.

Perform the pressure test or NDT on the statutory cycle — for new Category II and III equipment holding a manufacturing certificate or code stamp, the first before ten years from that certificate or stamp; for equipment without one, and for used equipment, before entering service.

Select the NDT scope — clause 13.5 requires, following a visual review, at least one volumetric examination combined with one surface or one flux-loss examination; results endorsed by name and signature of personal certificado.
For Category III equipment, perform the test or examination in the presence of a Type A, B or C unidad de inspección (clause 13.2 j).

The unidad de inspección issues the dictamen de evaluación de la conformidad, carrying its accreditation number, the dates of accreditation and STPS approval, the equipment data and the dictamen validity.

For Category III, file the aviso with STPS within sixty days of the dictamen; STPS assigns a número de control to each item and issues the official letter within five working days of receiving the notice.
methodsInScope: ET — electromagnetismo, corrientes de Eddy (surface option)
Leak testing by halogen detector, mass spectrometer or bubble chamber (flux-loss option)
VT — the visual review that precedes and drives method selection
Hydrostatic, pneumatic and hydrostatic-pneumatic pressure testing, plus alternative methods approved by STPS
renewal: For Category II and III equipment: the first pressure test or NDT is due before ten years from the manufacturing certificate or code stamp for new equipment that has one; equipment without that certificate or stamp, and all used equipment, is tested before entering service. Thereafter at least every five years, performed within the sixty calendar days before the end of each five-year period. The periodicity is determined by the employer's qualified personnel and may in no case exceed five years (clause 13.2 a). Dictámenes issued by a unidad de inspección are valid ten years for new equipment and five years for used equipment (clause 19.7). Boilers additionally require functional testing of safety shutdowns. Category III equipment requires a notice to STPS within sixty days of the dictamen.
commonFindings: Equipment misclassified into Category I or II to escape the Category III duties to have a unidad de inspección present and to notify STPS
Only a volumetric examination performed, with no accompanying surface or flux-loss examination as clause 13.5 requires
NDT results endorsed by a technician whose certification cannot be traced to NMX-B-482, its replacement, or a demonstrably equivalent scheme
Pressure test endorsed by an NDT technician rather than by an engineer with knowledge in the matter, contrary to clause 13.2 f and i
The five-year examination performed outside the sixty-day window before the end of the quinquennium
Aviso to STPS not filed within sixty days of the dictamen, leaving Category III equipment without a número de control
Chronological summary of pressure tests and non-destructive examinations missing from the equipment file
A dictamen relied on beyond its validity — five years for used equipment, not the ten that applies to new
sources: NOM-020-STPS-2011 as published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación, Segunda Sección, Tuesday 27 December 2011, retrieved from the STPS document repository at asinom.stps.gob.mx and extracted; clauses 3.7, 4.19 to 4.21, 4.32, 4.41 to 4.43, 7 and Table 1, 13.1 to 13.6, 16, 17, 19 and 20, and Reference Guide III read directly. Status as vigente, entry into force on 27 June 2012, the authorised alternative procedure of 9 December 2014, and the systematic review confirmation of 15 August 2022 from the Sistema Nacional de Infraestructura de la Calidad catalogue at platiica.economia.gob.mx. NMX-B-482-CANACERO-2016 — full title, vigente status, DOF declaratoria de vigencia of 20 October 2016, CANACERO as issuing Organismo Nacional de Normalización, cancellation of NMX-B-482-1991, and its recorded international grade of 'no equivalente' — from the same catalogue. Limitation: the text of NMX-B-482-CANACERO-2016 itself was not obtained, so its internal qualification model is not characterised here beyond its recorded grade. Verified 21 August 2026.

name: Entidad Mexicana de Acreditación, A.C.
authority: ema, operating as an Entidad de Acreditación under the Ley de Infraestructura de la Calidad; sectoral aprobación is granted separately by the regulating dependency — for pressure equipment under NOM-020, the Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social
appliesTo: Inspection bodies, testing and calibration laboratories, certification bodies and personnel certification bodies operating in Mexico. For an NDT or inspection service provider the route that matters is accreditation as a unidad de inspección under ISO/IEC 17020, in whichever of the three types — A, B or C — matches the firm's independence from the party whose equipment is being inspected.
summary: ema is the accreditation body that turns a Mexican inspection firm into one whose dictámenes a regulator will recognise. It accredits unidades de inspección against NMX-EC-17020-IMNC-2014, the Mexican adoption of ISO/IEC 17020:2012, applying ILAC P15 as guidance. Two things routinely trip up foreign firms. First, accreditation alone is not sufficient for regulated work: issuing a dictamen under a NOM also requires aprobación by the relevant dependency, and STPS publishes the directory of accredited and approved units. Second, since the Ley de Infraestructura de la Calidad took effect the statutory term changed from unidad de verificación to unidad de inspección — the activity is unchanged, and ema's own procedures still carry both names.
personnelCertification: ISO/IEC 17020 does not require an inspection body's inspectors to hold third-party certification. The body itself defines, documents and verifies competence criteria for each inspection activity, and ema evaluates that system — verifying personnel competence by demonstration during the on-site evaluation and by witnessing real inspections (testificación). That makes an employer-operated competence scheme backed by an outsourced Level III genuinely workable in Mexico, provided it is documented, applied and evidenced. Separately, ema accredits personnel certification bodies against NMX-EC-17024-IMNC, which is how centrally certified NDT personnel exist in Mexico at all. Where a NOM or a client contract names a personnel standard, that sits on top of, not instead of, the 17020 competence system.
requiredDocuments: Solicitud de acreditación filed through ema's SAEMA system, naming a representante autorizado who accepts the accreditation requirements on the body's behalf
Alcance de acreditación — the requested scope stating inspection activities, methods, and the NOMs or standards to be inspected against
Documented management system meeting NMX-EC-17020-IMNC-2014, including the impartiality and independence declaration that establishes Type A, B or C
Procedimientos técnicos de inspección for every method and activity in the requested scope
Registros de competencia del personal inspector — competence criteria per activity, authorisation records, training and ongoing monitoring
Registros de equipos y trazabilidad metrológica — calibration certificates and traceability evidence
Formatos de dictamen and reporting templates carrying the accreditation number and the required dates
A real inspection made available for ema to witness (testificación) before initial accreditation is granted
Solicitud de aprobación to the regulating dependency, such as STPS for NOM-020, once accredited
auditProcess: Recepción de la solicitud — application received and reviewed for completeness.
Inicio del proceso de evaluación and designación del grupo evaluador — a lead technical evaluator plus evaluators covering each area of the requested scope.
Evaluación documental of the management system and technical procedures against NMX-EC-17020-IMNC-2014 and the applicable ema application guide, general or by subject matter.
Evaluación en sitio — verifying personnel technical competence by demonstration, reviewing records, auditing metrological traceability of equipment, validating methods and observing real operation.

Testificación — ema observes the performance of the inspection process. For initial accreditation this must be carried out before accreditation is granted, and is normally done during the on-site evaluation.
Dictamen — the relevant evaluation committee or technical opinion commission decides to grant, deny, reduce, suspend or cancel the accreditation.
Aprobación by the regulating dependency where the scope covers a NOM, after which the unit appears in that dependency's directory and may issue dictámenes under that NOM.
methodsInScope: Witnessing of hydrostatic and pneumatic pressure testing
Note: ema scopes are written per NOM or per standard and per inspection activity, not per NDT method — the methods above are those an NOM-020 scope typically exercises
renewal: ema's procedure sets surveillance (vigilancia) at 12-month intervals, which may be conducted in the two months before or after the due date. The first surveillance evaluation is performed on site and preferably before 12 months from the accreditation date, with an outer limit of 18 months measured from that date for initial accreditations. Reevaluación must be carried out before the four-year cycle completes, counted from the last reevaluation decided by the relevant evaluation committee or technical opinion commission. Testificación must be repeated within no more than four years of the last witnessing. Renovación — a full re-evaluation against an expiry date — applies where a dependency requires the accreditation to carry one. Under Article 59 of the Ley de Infraestructura de la Calidad, accreditation or approval can be cancelled for issuing documents with false or erroneous information, repeatedly refusing requested services, express renunciation, serious breaches of obligations, or altering issued documents.
commonFindings: Type declared as A while the unit also inspects for a related party, breaching the independence conditions that type requires
Competence criteria for inspectors written generically rather than per inspection activity and method, with no authorisation records tying a named inspector to a specific scope
Metrological traceability gaps — calibration certificates without traceability to recognised standards, or equipment in use past its calibration date
Testificación allowed to lapse beyond four years from the last witnessed inspection
Dictamen templates missing the accreditation number, the date accreditation was granted, or the date of dependency approval that the NOM being assessed requires
Issuing dictámenes under a NOM for which the unit is accredited but not approved
Scope drift — inspecting against NOMs or standards outside the granted alcance
Surveillance evaluation slipped outside the two-month window either side of the 12-month due date
sources: ema, 'Manual de Procedimientos — Evaluación y Acreditación de Unidades de Verificación (Organismos de Inspección) con base en la norma NMX-EC-17020-IMNC-2014 / ISO/IEC 17020:2012', extracted and read directly, including its definitions of renovación (4.33), testificación (4.44) and vigilancia (4.46) and its surveillance, reevaluation and witnessing intervals; the procedure cites ILAC P15, 'Guía de aplicación de la ISO/IEC 17020 para unidades de Verificación'. Types A, B and C and the accredited-plus-approved requirement from ema's application guides for the same standard and from NOM-020-STPS-2011 clauses 4.41 to 4.43 and 19. Terminology change from unidad de verificación to unidad de inspección under the Ley de Infraestructura de la Calidad, published in the DOF on 1 July 2020; cancellation grounds from Article 59 of that law. Limitation: ema's own website returned HTTP 403 from this environment on 21 August 2026, so the public accredited-body directory at catalogo.consultaema.mx was not consulted and no counts or named accredited firms are stated. Verified 21 August 2026.

name: Pemex supplier and contractor registration and the Normas de Referencia / Estándares Técnicos technical requirements
authority: Petróleos Mexicanos (Pemex); technical standards issued by the Comité de Normalización de Petróleos Mexicanos y Organismos Subsidiarios
appliesTo: Companies bidding for or supplying goods and services to Pemex, including inspection and NDT contractors and the fabrication shops they serve. Registration in the padrón de proveedores y contratistas is documented as a precondition for participating in Pemex's open bidding, and the technical requirements flow down to subcontractors through the standards the contract cites.
summary: Pemex publishes more than most national oil companies. The padrón de proveedores y contratistas is a public registry described on pemex.com, and the Normas de Referencia (NRF) and the newer PEMEX-EST technical standards are published as downloadable PDFs on the same site, issued by the Comité de Normalización de Petróleos Mexicanos y Organismos Subsidiarios and applied as mandatory in Pemex acquisitions and service contracting. Registration information is transferred to SISCeP, Pemex's electronic contracting platform, and suppliers are told the registration is theirs to keep current — updated at least once a year. What Pemex does not publish is the internal evaluation scoring, weighting or any pre-approved vendor list for inspection services.
personnelCertification: This is where Pemex diverges sharply from baseline Mexican practice, and it is the argument that sells. NOM-020 accepts 'personal certificado' under NMX-B-482 or an equivalent, which leaves room for an employer written practice; published Pemex reference standards are stricter, requiring NDT personnel to be qualified and certified to ISO 9712 or to NMX-B-482-CANACERO-2016, with ISO 11484 cited as the applicable route for certain steel-product scopes, which follows a different qualification model. Level rules apply: Level 1 works only under direct Level 2 supervision, and interpretation of results is issued by Level 3, or by Level 2 with Level 3 approval. An outsourced Level III must personally hold certification under the scheme the contract cites.
requiredDocuments: Registro en el padrón de proveedores y contratistas, completed through the Registro de proveedores section of pemex.com
Acta constitutiva and its recent modifications, bearing the seal of the Registro Público de la Propiedad y de Comercio
Registro Federal de Contribuyentes with a current tax domicile
Latest annual and partial income tax declarations, except for recently incorporated companies
Catálogo of goods and services offered, as declared in the registration questionnaire
Procedimientos de ensayos no destructivos meeting the NRF or PEMEX-EST standard cited in the contract
Certificados de calificación y certificación del personal de END under ISO 9712, NMX-B-482-CANACERO-2016 or ISO 11484 as the cited standard requires
Records evidencing the level and supervision rules — who performed the examination, who supervised, and who interpreted and approved the result
Evidence of the annual update to the registration record
auditProcess: Register on pemex.com under Relación con proveedores / Registro de proveedores, completing the questionnaire of general and commercial information and the products and services offered.
Submit the corporate, tax and financial documents Pemex publishes for national suppliers.
The registration record is created and its information transferred to SISCeP, Pemex's electronic contracting system, enabling participation in open bidding.

Bid against the specific procurement, whose terms cite the applicable NRF or PEMEX-EST standards — these are publicly downloadable, so the technical requirements can and should be read before bidding.
On award, demonstrate personnel qualification and certification and procedure compliance against the cited standards throughout execution.
Keep the registration current — Pemex places the responsibility on the supplier and states it should be updated at least once a year.
methodsInScope: Tube and steel-product inspection scopes where ISO 11484 is the cited qualification route
industries: Oil and gas exploration and production
renewal: Pemex states that keeping the registration information current is the supplier's responsibility and that it should be updated at least once a year. Pemex does not publish a single uniform validity period for supplier registration across all categories, so no interval should be quoted to a client without checking the current registration rules on pemex.com. On the technical side the operative mechanism is revision control rather than renewal: NRFs are revised and reissued by the Comité de Normalización, with newer editions cancelling and replacing earlier ones, and PEMEX-EST standards have been issued alongside them since 2017-2018 — so the edition cited in the tender governs. Personnel certificates renew on their own scheme's cycle; ISO 9712-based certification is typically five years.
commonFindings: NDT personnel presented with employer-issued certificates where the cited NRF requires ISO 9712 or NMX-B-482-CANACERO-2016 certification
Level 1 technicians performing examinations without documented direct Level 2 supervision
Results interpreted and signed by a Level 2 without the Level 3 approval the cited standard requires
Working to a superseded edition of an NRF where the contract cites a later one, or to a later edition where the contract fixed an earlier
Registration record left un-updated beyond a year, disqualifying the supplier from a bid at the worst possible moment
Procedures not demonstrably aligned to the specific NRF or PEMEX-EST cited in the contract, only to a generic international code
Certification scope mismatch — certified in a method but not in the product form or technique the scope of work actually requires
sources: Pemex's public supplier pages on pemex.com — Relación con proveedores, Registro de proveedores, Requisitos for national suppliers, Proceso de registro, and the Padrón de proveedores y contratistas transparency page — together with Pemex's 'Guía rápida para el registro y evaluación de proveedores y contratistas', for the registration steps, required corporate and tax documents, the annual update duty and the transfer of registration data to SISCeP. Normas de Referencia and PEMEX-EST standards are published at public pemex.com URLs under procura/procedimientos-de-contratacion — examples confirmed to exist there include NRF-193-PEMEX-2014, NRF-065-PEMEX-2014, NRF-010-PEMEX-2014, PEMEX-EST-IC-274-2018 and PEMEX-EST-TD-142-2017 — and are issued by the Comité de Normalización de Petróleos Mexicanos y Organismos Subsidiarios. Important limitation, stated plainly: the pemex.com host refused connections from this environment on 21 August 2026, so the NDT personnel requirements attributed here to Pemex NRFs were read from secondary summaries of NRF-193-PEMEX-2014 rather than from the primary PDF. For that reason no NRF clause numbers are quoted anywhere in this entry, and the specific NRF or PEMEX-EST cited in a given tender should be downloaded and read before relying on the detail. Verified 21 August 2026.

name: IRAM-NM-ISO 9712 NDT Personnel Certification and Organismo Argentino de Acreditación (OAA) Accreditation
authority: Instituto Argentino de Normalización y Certificación (IRAM) as certification body; Organismo Argentino de Acreditación (OAA) as the sole national accreditation body; Ente Nacional Regulador del Gas (ENARGAS) as the sector regulator for gas transmission and distribution
appliesTo: Any inspection or NDT service provider working in Argentina on gas transmission and distribution pipelines regulated by ENARGAS, on refinery and petrochemical plant, on Vaca Muerta oilfield fabrication and gathering lines, on nuclear facilities, or on structural and pressure fabrication where the client cites IRAM standards. It also binds any firm seeking OAA accreditation as an inspection body under IRAM-ISO/IEC 17020.
summary: Argentina issues no single NDT licence. Two things bind a service provider. First, personnel: technicians are expected to hold certification to IRAM-NM-ISO 9712, the Argentine adoption of the Mercosur standard NM ISO 9712, issued by an accredited certification body rather than by their own employer. Second, where the work is regulated the regulator names that standard directly. ENARGAS NAG-100 Part E, Section 243, requires NDT of pipeline welds to be carried out by persons trained and certified at Level 2 or 3 to IRAM NM ISO 9712 or recognised equivalent international standards, and requires the written, qualified NDT procedures to be signed by an inspector competent to the same standard. A firm selling inspection as an accredited third party additionally pursues OAA accreditation under IRAM-ISO/IEC 17020.
personnelCertification: Central and third-party, not employer-based. IRAM operates an OAA-accredited scheme under IRAM-ISO/IEC 17024, accredited since 2004, certifying to IRAM-NM-ISO 9712; examinations are delivered by IRAM-authorised qualifying bodies (Organismos de Calificación Autorizados) including CNEA's OCA and UTN Facultad Regional Delta. INTI runs a separate OAA-accredited certification body for persons, scope reference OCH-003, using NM ISO 9712 and IRAM 710. An employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice does not on its own produce a certificate Argentina recognises for ENARGAS-regulated work. An outsourced Level III can still sign procedures under NAG-100's "normas equivalentes internacionales reconocidas" wording where he holds a centrally issued certificate such as ASNT NDT Level III.
requiredDocuments: Certificados de calificación IRAM-NM-ISO 9712, Nivel 1, 2 or 3, per method, showing issuing body and expiry date
Registro de agudeza visual: near vision and colour differentiation, dated within the last twelve months
Procedimientos escritos de END, calificados y documentados, signed by an inspector competent to IRAM NM ISO 9712, per NAG-100 Section 243 b)(1)
Registros de Calificación de Procedimientos (RCP/PQR) issued by an Ente Habilitado per IRAM/IAS U 500-138, or by a welding inspector certified per IRAM/IAS U 500-169
Certificados de Inspector de Soldadura per IRAM/IAS U 500-169 for the visual inspection required by NAG-100 Section 241

Registro de ensayos no destructivos: number of girth welds made, number tested, number rejected and location of rejections by kilometre post, engineering station or geographic feature, retained for the life of the pipeline (NAG-100 Section 243 f))
Manual de calidad y procedimientos conforming to IRAM-ISO/IEC 17020 where OAA accreditation is sought, including the impartiality analysis and type A/B/C declaration
Certificados de calibración for UT instruments, reference blocks, densitometers and field gauges
Autorización de la Autoridad Regulatoria Nuclear (ARN) for gamma radiography sources, operators and transport
auditProcess: Apply to OAA naming the scheme (IRAM-ISO/IEC 17020) and the requested scope by inspection activity, method and normative document
Documentary review of the quality manual, NDT procedures, personnel certification records and impartiality arrangements
On-site assessment at the declared premises plus witnessing of live inspections for each method claimed in the scope
Close non-conformities within the period OAA sets, with objective evidence rather than corrective-action promises
OAA decision and issue of the accreditation certificate with the approved scope annexed
Periodic surveillance evaluations during the term and reassessment before expiry, on the cycle set in OAA's accreditation rules
industries: Oil and gas transmission and distribution
renewal: IRAM-NM-ISO 9712 is the Argentine adoption of the Mercosur standard NM ISO 9712, whose April 2025 edition is an identical adoption of ISO 9712:2021 and whose previous edition, January 2014, adopted ISO 9712:2012. On that basis the ISO 9712 cycle applies: certificates run five years, are renewed once on evidence of continued visual acuity and uninterrupted activity, and require recertification at ten years. Confirm which edition IRAM has adopted before quoting an exam route. OAA accreditation is maintained by periodic surveillance and reassessment; OAA does not publish the interval on its public pages, so verify it in the current OAA rules rather than assuming a number.
commonFindings: NDT procedures on file are unsigned, or are signed by someone whose Level III certificate does not cover the method the procedure addresses, contrary to NAG-100 Section 243 b)(1)
Technicians hold only an employer-issued SNT-TC-1A card with no IRAM-NM-ISO 9712 certificate, and the auditor treats the whole method scope as uncovered for regulated pipeline work
Certificates expired but technicians still on the job roster; no system tracking the five-year expiry against crew assignment
Annual visual acuity records missing, or older than twelve months, for personnel on active assignment
The pipeline NDT register omits rejection locations by kilometre post or engineering station, so the life-of-asset record NAG-100 Section 243 f) requires is incomplete

Radiographic coverage percentages applied to the wrong location class: at least 10 per cent in Class 1, at least 15 per cent in Class 2, and 100 per cent where possible but not less than 90 per cent in Classes 3 and 4, at major or navigable river crossings, submarine sections and within rail and highway rights of way, with 100 per cent at tie-ins
Welding inspector competence claimed as "IRAM o equivalente" with no certificate to IRAM/IAS U 500-169 or a demonstrably equivalent international scheme on file
Accredited scope advertised more broadly than the scope OAA actually annexed to the certificate
sources: IRAM, NDT operators certification scheme page (accessed August 2026), stating IRAM-NM-ISO 9712, IRAM-ISO/IEC 17024 and OAA accreditation since 2004; CNEA Departamento de Ensayos No Destructivos y Estructurales OCA page (methods and levels: US, PM, CI, LP, RI levels 1-3, USPA levels 1-2) and INTI Organismo de Certificación pages citing IRAM-ISO/IEC 17024, NM ISO 9712 and IRAM 710, and OAA persons-certification scope reference OCH-003 (accessed August 2026); ENARGAS NAG-100 Año 1993, Adenda N.º 3 Año 2026, Parte E, Sections 221, 225, 227, 229, 241, 243 and 245, text read directly, approved by ENARGAS Resolución 62/2026 published in the Boletín Oficial on 10 February 2026 and effective 11 February 2026, which also repeals NAG-105; AMN/Mercosur catalogue record for NM ISO 9712, April 2025 edition, identical adoption of ISO 9712:2021, superseding the January 2014 edition; OAA public site (accessed August 2026), noting Decreto 1474/94 as the framework for the Sistema Nacional de Normas, Calidad y Certificación, and the replacement of ILAC and IAF by Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated (GLOBAC) from 1 January 2026.

name: Sistema Nacional de Acreditación del Instituto Nacional de Normalización (INN) and Chilean Mining-Sector Inspection Requirements
authority: Instituto Nacional de Normalización (INN), which is both the national standards body and the national accreditation body; Servicio Nacional de Geología y Minería (SERNAGEOMIN) for mine safety; the SEREMI de Salud for boilers, autoclaves and steam equipment; SICEP, administered by the Asociación de Industriales de Antofagasta, as the mining supplier register
appliesTo: NDT and inspection contractors serving Chilean copper, lithium and gold mines, concentrator plants, smelters, ports and the pulp, power and refining sectors. It binds any firm bidding into Codelco, BHP, Antofagasta Minerals and comparable operators, any firm inspecting boilers, autoclaves and steam equipment, and any firm claiming accredited inspection status inside Chile.
summary: Chile does not licence NDT companies. Access is controlled in two separate places instead. Accreditation: INN runs the Sistema Nacional de Acreditación and accredits inspection bodies against NCh-ISO 17020:2012 under its accreditation regulation INN-R401. Accreditation is voluntary in itself but becomes obligatory wherever a technical regulation incorporates it; applications go through INN's SDAC portal on forms F407-21-01 and FD-D06-04, and accreditations are granted for five years, renewable, with surveillance evaluations during the term. Commercial access: the mining majors screen contractors through SICEP, the Sistema de Calificación de Empresas Proveedoras, which rates financial capacity, operational and technical capability, legal and labour compliance and risk prevention. A firm can be technically excellent and still not be biddable without SICEP standing.
personnelCertification: Employer-based certification is accepted, and in practice is the norm. Chile has adopted ISO 9712 as NCh-ISO 9712, but the 2018 edition is shown as no longer current in INN's own catalogue, and INN's register of accredited personnel certification bodies does not list a Chilean body certifying NDT personnel to it, so there is no verified domestic route to an ISO 9712 certificate. Chilean technicians therefore hold employer certification written against ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or ISO 9712 certificates issued by foreign bodies. An outsourced ASNT Level III can write and sign the employer's written practice, approve procedures and certify Level I and II staff, which is how most Chilean NDT firms operate.
requiredDocuments: Práctica Escrita to ASNT SNT-TC-1A, signed and dated by the Level III, naming every method, level and technique and the education, training, experience and examination requirements for each
Certificados de calificación y certificación del personal by method and level, with general, specific and practical examination papers and grading records
Registros de agudeza visual (Jaeger N.º 1 or equivalent) and colour differentiation, dated within the last twelve months
Procedimientos de END approved by the Level III and traceable to ASME BPVC Section V, AWS D1.1, API or the client's own specification
Certificados de calibración de equipos plus verification records for reference blocks, transducers and gauges
Manual de gestión conforming to NCh-ISO 17020:2012, with the impartiality analysis and the type A, B or C declaration, where INN accreditation is sought
Formulario F407-21-01 (solicitud de evaluación) and the scope form FD-D06-04, submitted through SDAC, with fees per INN-R410
SICEP file: financial statements, technical and equipment inventory, legal and labour compliance certificates and the risk-prevention programme
Autorización sanitaria and radiation-protection authorisation from the SEREMI de Salud for industrial radiography sources and operators
auditProcess: Submit the application and proposed scope through INN's SDAC portal using forms F407-21-01 and FD-D06-04, and pay the fees set out in INN-R410
INN reviews the management documentation against NCh-ISO 17020:2012 and the inspection body criteria document DA-D22
On-site evaluation at the declared premises plus witnessing of live inspections for each activity and method in the requested scope
Correct non-conformities within the period INN sets and submit supporting evidence
INN decision and grant of accreditation for a five-year period, published with the approved scope
Surveillance evaluations during the term, and application for reaccreditation before the five years expire
renewal: INN accreditation is granted for five years and may be renewed for further five-year cycles, with surveillance evaluations during the term to verify continued conformity; INN does not publish a fixed surveillance month on its public pages, so confirm the schedule in INN-R401 rather than assuming one. SICEP standing is a periodically updated diagnosis rather than a fixed-term certificate and lapses if the file is not maintained. Boiler and autoclave inspection under the Ministry of Health regulation runs on a frequency tied to equipment category; establish the category before quoting an interval to a client.
commonFindings: The written practice is a generic template that was never tailored to the methods and techniques the company actually sells, and the Level III who signed it is no longer engaged
Level II technicians certified in UT are performing phased array with no separate technique qualification and no documented examination
Vision records missing for technicians on site, or dated more than twelve months before the inspection
Marketing claims "acreditado por el INN" when the INN scope covers only some methods or only one address; INN accreditation is granted against a specific annexed scope and site

Wire-rope inspection reports for hoisting installations do not record the parameters DS 132 Article 188 names, namely flat wear, number of broken wires, useful diameter and oxidation, so they do not establish the service limit
Extraction-rope determinations carried out at intervals longer than six months, or balance-rope determinations longer than twelve months, contrary to DS 132 Article 188
SICEP file allowed to lapse or left at a lower category, so the firm is filtered out at prequalification irrespective of its technical scope
No traceable link between the acceptance criteria quoted on the report and the code edition the client's specification actually calls up
sources: INN, Organismos de Inspección accreditation page and accreditation FAQ (accessed August 2026), giving NCh-ISO 17020-2012 as the applicable standard, the SDAC application route at sdac.inn.cl, forms F407-21-01v02 and FD-D06-04v01, guidance DA-D06, criteria document DA-D22 v07, fee regulation INN-R410 v08, accreditation regulation INN-R401, the five-year renewable accreditation term with surveillance during the term, IAAC MLA founding membership and founding membership of Global ACI, successor to the merged ILAC and IAF; INN catalogue record for NCh-ISO9712:2018, "Ensayos no destructivos - Calificación y certificación del personal que realiza ensayos no destructivos", published 30 August 2018, shown as No Vigente; INN list of approved standards showing NCh3918:2026 and NCh3919:2026 on acoustic emission; Chile Decreto Supremo N° 132 (Ministerio de Minería), Reglamento de Seguridad Minera, published 7 February 2004, Articles 185, 188, 191 and 378, text read directly; Chile Decreto Supremo N° 10 (Ministerio de Salud, Subsecretaría de Salud Pública), Reglamento de calderas, autoclaves y equipos que utilizan vapor de agua, published 19 October 2013, superseding DS N° 48; INN accreditation certificate OI232 for NDT held by an accredited inspection body; SICEP public pages and Asociación de Industriales de Antofagasta material (accessed August 2026).

name: Instituto Nacional de Calidad (INACAL) Accreditation and the OSINERGMIN Registro de Empresas Inspectoras
authority: Instituto Nacional de Calidad (INACAL), Dirección de Acreditación, as the national accreditation body; Organismo Supervisor de la Inversión en Energía y Minería (OSINERGMIN) as the energy and mining regulator; Ministerio de Energía y Minas (MINEM) as the rule-maker
appliesTo: NDT and inspection contractors serving Peruvian mining, hydrocarbons and fuel distribution. It binds any firm inspecting buried fuel tanks and piping, any firm certifying LPG stationary tanks or their repairs and alterations, and any firm bidding into Antamina, Cerro Verde, Las Bambas, Southern Peru, Petroperú or Pluspetrol contracts where accredited inspection is specified.
summary: Peru is the clearest regional case of accreditation made compulsory by regulation rather than chosen for marketing. INACAL's Dirección de Acreditación accredits inspection bodies against NTP-ISO/IEC 17020, using application form DA-002 filed through INACAL's management platform, with the fee calculated on the number of procedures in scope. OSINERGMIN then layers a sector registry on top. Under Decreto Supremo N° 001-2022-EM, periodic hermeticity inspection of buried tanks and piping storing liquid fuels and OPDH may only be performed by inspection bodies accredited by INACAL and entered in OSINERGMIN's Registro de Empresas Inspectoras, with the inscription procedure approved by Resolución de Consejo Directivo N° 151-2024-OS/CD. Without both, the certificate the site needs has no standing.
personnelCertification: Employer-based certification is accepted, largely because Peru offers no verified alternative. INACAL accredits certification bodies for persons under NTP-ISO/IEC 17024, but no Peruvian body certifying NDT personnel to ISO 9712 could be verified in INACAL's accredited directory. Peruvian technicians therefore hold employer certification written against ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or ISO 9712 certificates issued abroad. An outsourced Level III can sign the written practice, approve procedures and certify Level I and II staff. Note the separate statutory track: tank inspection certification must come from an engineer holding a current API 510 authorisation or from an accredited inspection body, and an ASNT Level III certificate does not substitute for that.
requiredDocuments: Formulario DA-002, solicitud de acreditación para organismos de inspección, with annexes, filed through INACAL's DASGAC platform, plus proof of payment calculated on the number of procedures
Management system manual and procedures conforming to NTP-ISO/IEC 17020, with the type A, B or C declaration and the impartiality risk analysis
Práctica escrita to ASNT SNT-TC-1A signed by the Level III, plus each technician's certification file, examination records and current vision records
Inscription file for OSINERGMIN's Registro de Empresas Inspectoras under RCD N° 151-2024-OS/CD, citing the INACAL accreditation
Certificado de Inspección de Hermeticidad del STE and the accompanying Informe de Índice de Riesgo for buried tank systems

Certificado de Conformidad for LPG stationary tanks issued by an INACAL-accredited certification body, or the manufacturer's ASME Section VIII data report U-1 or U-1A signed by an authorised inspector
Evidence that any LPG tank repair or alteration was carried out to API 510 or to NB-23, the National Board Inspection Code, endorsed by an accredited inspection body
Equipment calibration certificates traceable to INACAL's national metrology service
Authorisation from the Instituto Peruano de Energía Nuclear (IPEN) for industrial radiography sources and operators
auditProcess: File form DA-002 with annexes and the fee through INACAL's DASGAC platform, defining the scope by inspection activity and normative document
INACAL reviews the documentation against the general, specific and complementary accreditation criteria for NTP-ISO/IEC 17020
An evaluation team is appointed and carries out documentary review, on-site evaluation and witnessing of inspections for each activity claimed
Close non-conformities within INACAL's timescale with objective evidence
INACAL decision and issue of the accreditation certificate with the approved scope
For regulated fuel work, apply separately to OSINERGMIN for inscription in the Registro de Empresas Inspectoras under RCD N° 151-2024-OS/CD
Periodic INACAL supervision during the accreditation term, and reaccreditation before expiry
industries: Copper, zinc, gold and polymetallic mining
Oil and gas production and refining
Fuel retail, LPG distribution and direct consumers
renewal: INACAL does not publish the accreditation term or the supervision interval on its public accreditation pages, so confirm both in the current accreditation criteria before committing to a client; do not quote a number from another country's practice. What is fixed sits on the regulated side. For buried tank systems, the first hermeticity certificate is required before the system enters service, and thereafter the periodicity is set by the Índice de Riesgo assessment carried out for that specific installation. The inspection report must be submitted to OSINERGMIN within thirty calendar days of the test, and the hermeticity test itself must detect a leak rate of at least 0.1 gallons per hour (0.3785 litres per hour).
commonFindings: The firm holds INACAL accreditation but is not entered in OSINERGMIN's Registro de Empresas Inspectoras, so the hermeticity certificates it issues are rejected on supervision
Accredited scope does not name the specific normative document the client is relying on, so the certificate falls outside scope even though the method itself is covered
Risk-index report and hermeticity report not filed with OSINERGMIN within thirty calendar days of the test
LPG stationary tank accepted on the nameplate alone, with no Certificado de Conformidad from an INACAL-accredited certification body and no U-1 or U-1A data report
Tank repairs signed off without evidence the work followed API 510 or NB-23, and without an accredited inspection body's endorsement
The employer's written practice names methods the Level III is not himself certified in, leaving Level II certifications in those methods without a valid basis
Technician files show training hours but no documented supervised experience, which is what SNT-TC-1A actually requires
Radiography performed without a current IPEN authorisation for the source, the operator, or the transport of the source
sources: Ley N° 30224, Ley que crea el Sistema Nacional para la Calidad y el Instituto Nacional de Calidad, published 11 July 2014, with INACAL operational from 1 June 2015 having absorbed INDECOPI's Servicio Nacional de Acreditación, Servicio Nacional de Metrología and the Comisión de Normalización; INACAL accreditation pages including "¿Cómo obtener la Acreditación?" listing form DA-002 for inspection bodies and the DASGAC platform, and the Organismos de Inspección page citing NTP-ISO/IEC 17020, accessed August 2026; OSINERGMIN "Inspección Periódica de Hermeticidad" page citing Decreto Supremo N° 001-2022-EM, which supersedes DS N° 064-2009-EM, and Resolución de Consejo Directivo N° 151-2024-OS/CD, accessed August 2026; the text of the hermeticity norm read directly, including the definitions of Entidad Acreditada and Certificado de Inspección de Hermeticidad, the 0.1 gallons per hour leak index and the thirty-day filing period; OSINERGMIN supervision guidance for LPG direct consumers and distribution networks, version 1.0, May 2022, read directly, citing DS N° 065-2008-EM Article 19, DS N° 001-2007-EM Article 9, NTP 321.123 clauses 5.1.1 to 5.1.15, ASME Section VIII Division 1, API 510 and NB-23; MINEM DS N° 024-2016-EM, Reglamento de Seguridad y Salud Ocupacional en Minería, as modified by DS N° 023-2017-EM and DS N° 034-2023-EM. No NTP adoption of ISO 9712 was found, so none is cited.

name: Organismo Nacional de Acreditación de Colombia (ONAC) — Inspection Body Accreditation for Non-Destructive Testing
authority: Organismo Nacional de Acreditación de Colombia (ONAC) as the national accreditation body; Ministerio de Minas y Energía and the Agencia Nacional de Hidrocarburos (ANH) for the regulated hydrocarbon inspection scopes
appliesTo: NDT and inspection contractors in Colombian oil and gas: drill pipe and tubing inspection at pipe yards, tank and pipeline integrity work, and flare-efficiency and leak-detection inspection at production facilities. It binds firms selling into the Ecopetrol group, Frontera, Parex, Geopark and the drilling contractors, and any firm that puts an accreditation mark on an inspection report.
summary: ONAC is the Colombian state's accreditation body and its inspection body scheme, coded OIN, is where NDT sits. Scopes are granted against ISO/IEC 17020:2012 under inspection field code 22, "Equipos y elementos a través de ensayos no destructivos — END", and the annexed scope names the exact activity, the execution criteria and the acceptance and rejection criteria down to the clause and table, plus the inspection body type A, B or C. Two hydrocarbon inspection scopes have been made effectively compulsory by regulation: flare efficiency measurement and natural gas leak detection and quantification at production facilities, under Ministerio de Minas y Energía Resolución 40066 de 2022 as modified by Resolución 40317 de 2023, and ANH Resolución 10981 de 2023.
personnelCertification: Colombia is the regional exception: it has a domestic third-party route. ONAC accredits certification bodies for persons under ISO/IEC 17024, and ACOSEND has held that accreditation to certify NDT inspectors at Levels I and II against ISO 9712:2012 in MT, PT, RT, UT and VT; verify current status in ONAC's Directorio Oficial de Acreditados before relying on it. Level III is not covered domestically, so Level III comes from ASNT or a foreign ISO 9712 body. Employer certification under SNT-TC-1A remains common in operator supply chains, but inside an ONAC-accredited inspection body personnel competence must be demonstrated against ISO/IEC 17020 clause 6.1, not merely against the employer's written practice.
requiredDocuments: Solicitud de acreditación with the proposed scope drafted the way ONAC's annex is drafted: inspection field code, inspection activity, execution criteria, acceptance and rejection criteria, and body type

Internal inspection procedures cited by exact name and version number, in the style of "Ultrasonido — Medición de Espesores con Scan B en Tuberías de perforación (Drill Pipe - Heavy Weight) y tubería de producción (Tubing) V.8"

Controlled copies of every normative document named in the scope, at the edition named: DS-1 Drill Stem Inspection Vol. 3 5th ed. 2020, ASME BPVC.V-2023 Article 23 SE-797, API Spec 5CT 11th ed. December 2023, API RP 5C1 8th ed. 2020, API Std 653
Impartiality analysis and the declared type A, B or C under ISO/IEC 17020:2012
Personnel competence records covering certification, authorisation, training, witnessed performance and ongoing monitoring per ISO/IEC 17020 clause 6.1
Equipment inventory with calibration and verification records for each method in the scope
Inspection reports and certificates in the format ONAC assessed, with the accreditation symbol applied per ONAC's rules of use
Fee calculation from ONAC's Modelo Integral de Tarifas (MIT)
For the hydrocarbon scopes, the ANH technical guidance annexes and documented method for flare efficiency evaluation and leak quantification
auditProcess: Submit the application and scope to ONAC; ONAC applies its application-review procedure and confirms scheme, scope and fee from the MIT model
Documentary evaluation against ISO/IEC 17020:2012 and the applicable ONAC accreditation rules in the RAC series
On-site evaluation plus witnessing of inspections for every activity, method and normative document in the requested scope
Non-conformity treatment with evidence of corrective action within the timescale ONAC sets

Decision by ONAC's decision-making body and publication of the certificate and annexed scope in the Directorio Oficial de Acreditados; the accreditation cycle starts from the date of publication in the DOA
Surveillance evaluations at months 9, 21, 33 and 45 after approval of the renewal, with re-evaluation at month 55
methodsInScope: Optical gas imaging and leak quantification
industries: Oil and gas drilling and production
renewal: ONAC does not run one fixed validity across every scheme; the certificate itself carries the expiry date, and it is the surveillance rhythm that is published. Under the accreditation service rules RAC-3.0-01, version 12 dated 8 January 2025, from the first renewal onwards ONAC schedules surveillance evaluations in months 9, 21, 33 and 45 after approval of the renewal, with re-evaluation in month 55, and the new cycle begins from publication of the certificate in the DOA. A live example: certificate 24-OIN-053 carries a grant date of 28 July 2025 and an expiry of 27 July 2028.
commonFindings: Scope creep: the firm inspects a tubular size or applies a normative document that is not in the annexed scope, so the report cannot legitimately carry the accreditation mark
The internal procedure version named in the ONAC annex has been superseded internally without notifying ONAC of the change

Acceptance criteria applied from a different edition than the annex names; DS-1 Volume 3, 5th edition 2020, clause 3.6.5 and tables 3.6.1, 3.6.2 and 3.11.2 are specific, and an older edition's tables are a finding
A type C inspection body performing work that, as contracted, makes it supplier or repairer of the item inspected, breaking the declared impartiality arrangement
Personnel file rests solely on an SNT-TC-1A employer card, with no evidence of the competence authorisation and ongoing monitoring ISO/IEC 17020 clause 6.1 requires

Flare efficiency and leak reports issued without reference to the ANH technical guidance, or without demonstrating the 90 per cent combustion and methane destruction efficiency threshold set out in ANH Circular No. 0003 of 30 January 2025
Accreditation symbol used on reports outside the accredited scope, or on general marketing material
Surveillance dates missed because the firm counted from the certificate date rather than from the DOA publication that actually starts the cycle
