sources: ONAC accreditation certificate 24-OIN-053 for ATP Integridad y Corrosión S.A.S, NIT 900.412.013-9, ISO/IEC 17020:2012, form FR 3.5.3-03 V7 approved 2023-07-18, read in full: inspection field code 22 for NDT (ultrasonic, visual-dimensional and MFL of drill pipe, heavy weight, drill collar, casing and tubing, and visual inspection of storage tanks) as a type C body, and inspection field code 29 for flare efficiency and gas leak detection as a type A body, with dates 2025-07-28, 2026-07-10 and 2028-07-27, and citing DS-1 Drill Stem Inspection Vol. 3 5th ed. 2020, ASME BPVC.V-2023 Art 23 SE-797, API Spec 5CT 11th ed. December 2023, API RP 5C1 8th ed. 2020 and API Std 653 5th ed.; ONAC OIN and OCP scheme pages and the DOA directory (accessed August 2026), noting 26 inspection categories; ONAC Reglas del Servicio de Acreditación RAC-3.0-01 version 12, 8 January 2025, for the month 9/21/33/45 surveillance and month 55 re-evaluation schedule; Ministerio de Minas y Energía Resolución 40066 of 11 February 2022 and Resolución 40317 of 10 April 2023; ANH Resolución 10981 of 31 October 2023 and ANH Circular No. 0003 of 30 January 2025. ACOSEND's ONAC ISO/IEC 17024 accreditation for NDT Levels I and II to ISO 9712:2012 is reported by secondary sources only and should be re-verified in ONAC's DOA before it is relied on. No public Ecopetrol NDT personnel specification was verified, so none is quoted.

name: Servicio de Acreditación Ecuatoriano (SAE), formerly the Organismo de Acreditación Ecuatoriano (OAE)
authority: Servicio de Acreditación Ecuatoriano (SAE) as the national accreditation body; Agencia de Regulación y Control de Hidrocarburos (ARCH), re-established by Decreto Ejecutivo 256 of 8 May 2024 under the Ministerio de Energía y Minas, for hydrocarbon-sector qualification of inspection companies
appliesTo: NDT and inspection contractors working Ecuadorian oil and gas: the Oriente basin fields, the SOTE and OCP pipelines, the Esmeraldas and Shushufindi refineries and the fuel terminals, plus tank farms, power plants and metalwork fabrication. It binds any firm that must present itself as an accredited inspection body, or be qualified by ARCH to inspect for an operator.
summary: The body named here is real but no longer carries that name. The Organismo de Acreditación Ecuatoriano (OAE), created under the Ley del Sistema Ecuatoriano de la Calidad, was renamed and now operates as the Servicio de Acreditación Ecuatoriano (SAE); older Ecuadorian legal text and legacy contracts still say OAE, which is a frequent source of confusion at tender stage. SAE accredits inspection bodies against NTE INEN-ISO/IEC 17020:2013, the Ecuadorian adoption. Applications run through SAE's SISAC and ACREDITA SAE platforms. Accreditation is granted for five years, maintained by two surveillance evaluations at eighteen-month intervals inside the cycle, with reaccreditation applied for before expiry. In the hydrocarbon sector operators additionally require ARCH qualification, so accreditation alone does not open the gate.
personnelCertification: Employer-based certification is accepted and is the norm. Ecuador has no verified accredited domestic body certifying NDT personnel to ISO 9712, so technicians hold employer certification written against ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or ISO 9712 certificates issued abroad. An outsourced Level III can sign the written practice, approve NDT procedures and certify Level I and II staff. The constraint sits on the other side of the transaction: inside a SAE-accredited inspection body, personnel competence must be demonstrated to the assessor against NTE INEN-ISO/IEC 17020:2013, meaning training, formal authorisation, witnessed performance and ongoing monitoring records. An SNT-TC-1A card on its own is not sufficient evidence at a SAE witnessing evaluation.
requiredDocuments: Solicitud de acreditación filed through SISAC with all annexes, plus payment of the file-opening fee
Management system documentation against NTE INEN-ISO/IEC 17020:2013, including the type A, B or C declaration and the impartiality analysis
Alcance de acreditación drafted in SAE's format, naming each inspection activity and the normative documents it is performed and judged against
Práctica escrita and personnel certification files by method and level, with authorisation records and ongoing competence monitoring evidence
NDT procedures approved by the Level III and traceable to the codes the client cites, typically ASME, API and AWS
Equipment inventory with calibration and verification records for each method in scope
ARCH qualification file for hydrocarbon-sector work, kept current independently of the SAE cycle
Authorisation from the national radiation control authority for industrial radiography sources, operators and source transport
Internal audit, management review, non-conformity and corrective-action records covering the full scope claimed
auditProcess: Confirm eligibility: legal personality, a functioning quality management system, competent personnel, adequate infrastructure and demonstrated knowledge of SAE's requirements
File the accreditation application through SISAC with annexes and pay the file-opening fee
SAE appoints the evaluation team and issues the estimated cost of the service
Evaluation in three parts: documentary review, on-site verification, and witnessing of the inspection body's own inspectors performing real inspections
Close non-conformities within the timescales SAE sets
SAE decision and grant of accreditation for a five-year cycle
Two surveillance evaluations at eighteen-month intervals during the cycle, and reaccreditation applied for before the cycle expires
industries: Oil and gas production and transport
renewal: SAE accreditation runs for five years and is maintained by two surveillance evaluations at eighteen-month intervals within the cycle; reaccreditation must be applied for before the cycle expires. Scope extension is available at any point on demonstration of conformity, and accreditation can be withdrawn where non-compliance affects technical competence or the quality of results. ARCH qualification runs on its own cycle set by the agency and must be tracked as a separate diary item; firms routinely lose work by keeping one current and letting the other lapse.
commonFindings: Documents, contracts and certificates still cite "OAE", so the entity named does not match SAE's current register and the client's procurement system rejects it
The witnessing stage fails because the inspector observed on site is not the one whose competence file was submitted
Scope written in generic terms such as "ensayos no destructivos" rather than by activity and normative document, so SAE cannot grant it as drafted
Surveillance evaluation missed because the firm tracked the five-year expiry but not the eighteen-month surveillance points inside the cycle
Personnel competence evidenced only by an SNT-TC-1A card, with no authorisation record, no witnessed performance and no ongoing monitoring as ISO/IEC 17020 requires
ARCH qualification lapsed while SAE accreditation stayed live, and the contractor was rejected at the operator's gate
Procedures approved by a Level III whose own certification in that method had already expired
Impartiality analysis silent on group companies that also supply, fabricate or repair the items being inspected
sources: SAE, "Cómo acreditarse: organismos de inspección" (accessed August 2026), giving the ISO/IEC 17020 basis, the SISAC application route, the three-part evaluation of documentary review, on-site verification and witnessing, the five-year accreditation period, two surveillance evaluations at eighteen-month intervals, reaccreditation before expiry, scope extension and withdrawal grounds; SAE news item on training in NTE INEN ISO/IEC 17020:2013 for accrediting inspection bodies, and SAE course for Andean Community technical experts on ISO/IEC 17020; SAE published scope document SAE-INS-17-002 and SAE-accredited inspection body scopes covering hydrocarbon-sector metallurgical and non-destructive inspection; Decreto Ejecutivo 1036 of 6 May 2020 creating ARCERNNR by merging the electricity, hydrocarbons and mining regulators, and Decreto Ejecutivo 256 of 8 May 2024 splitting it back into ARCH, ARCOM and ARCONEL under the Ministerio de Energía y Minas, with a 90-day implementation window, as reported by Primicias; SAE institutional pages confirming creation in 2007 under the Ley del Sistema Ecuatoriano de la Calidad and the OAE-to-SAE naming.

name: COVENIN Venezuelan Standards and the Servicio Desconcentrado de Normalización, Calidad, Metrología y Reglamentos Técnicos (SENCAMER)
authority: SENCAMER, the national standardisation, quality, metrology and technical regulation service, which is the current issuer of COVENIN standards and operates the accreditation subsystem under the Ley Orgánica del Sistema Venezolano para la Calidad
appliesTo: NDT and inspection contractors working the Venezuelan oil, gas and petrochemical estate: Faja del Orinoco upgraders, the Paraguaná, Puerto La Cruz and El Palito refineries, gas processing plant and the PDVSA pipeline network, plus steel and aluminium at Ciudad Guayana, power generation and shipyards. It binds any firm certifying NDT personnel or claiming accredited status inside Venezuela.
summary: COVENIN is the designation carried by the Venezuelan national standard, not a live commission. The Comisión Venezolana de Normas Industriales was created in 1958, and authority to issue COVENIN standards now sits with SENCAMER. For an NDT service provider the operative document is COVENIN 1999:2021, the third revision of the requirements for qualification and certification of NDT personnel, which completely replaces COVENIN 1999:1999 and was revised by technical committee CT22 Ensayos No Destructivos under SENCAMER's guidelines, aligning Venezuelan requirements with ISO 9712. COVENIN 2967:2021 covers NDT training and qualification centres. SENCAMER also administers the NORVEN conformity mark and the accreditation of conformity assessment bodies, including inspection bodies and testing laboratories.
personnelCertification: Mixed, and the mix is commercially decisive. COVENIN 1999:2021 sets out a national qualification and certification scheme aligned with ISO 9712, which is a central rather than employer model, and COVENIN 2967:2021 governs the training and qualification centres that feed it. But a functioning SENCAMER-accredited ISO/IEC 17024 body certifying NDT personnel could not be verified, and in practice the PDVSA supply chain has long run on employer certification written against ASNT SNT-TC-1A, with ISO 9712 certificates from foreign bodies for staff who also work internationally. An outsourced Level III can sign the written practice; whether the client accepts that in place of COVENIN 1999 certification is a contract question, so settle it in the tender documents before mobilising.
requiredDocuments: Certificados de calificación y certificación per COVENIN 1999:2021, by method and level, where the contract calls up the national scheme
Práctica escrita to ASNT SNT-TC-1A signed by the Level III, with education, training, experience and examination requirements per method, where the contract runs on the employer model
Training records from a centre meeting COVENIN 2967:2021 requirements, supporting the training hours claimed
Written NDT procedures approved by the Level III and traceable to the code the client cites: ASME BPVC Section V, API 1104, AWS D1.1 or the applicable PDVSA specification
Vision examination records covering near vision and colour differentiation, dated within the last twelve months
Equipment calibration and verification records traceable to SENCAMER's metrology subsystem
Accreditation certificate and annexed scope where the firm claims SENCAMER-accredited inspection body status
Radiation-protection authorisation for gamma radiography sources, operators and source transport
Mechanical integrity records where the client's system follows PDVSA's mechanical integrity guidance for critical equipment such as storage tanks, piping, pumps and safety systems
auditProcess: Establish first which basis the contract runs on, COVENIN 1999:2021 national certification or employer certification under SNT-TC-1A, because the evidence set differs entirely
Assemble personnel files: certificates by method and level, training records from a COVENIN 2967 centre or a demonstrable equivalent, experience logs and current vision records
Have a Level III review and sign the written practice and every NDT procedure against the codes and PDVSA specifications the client names
Submit the application and proposed scope to SENCAMER where accreditation as a conformity assessment body is being sought
Documentary review and on-site evaluation by SENCAMER, including witnessing of inspections in the claimed scope
Close non-conformities and receive the accreditation decision with the annexed scope
industries: Oil and gas production and heavy crude upgrading
renewal: COVENIN 1999:2021 aligns Venezuelan personnel certification with ISO 9712, whose cycle is five years with a single renewal and recertification at ten years; treat that as the working assumption but confirm it against the text of COVENIN 1999:2021 itself, which could not be read directly from SENCAMER's catalogue server. Where the contract runs on employer certification instead, the interval is whatever the written practice states, commonly five years for Levels I and II with annual vision checks. SENCAMER accreditation cycle lengths are not published on its public pages, so do not quote one.
commonFindings: Certificates issued against COVENIN 1999:1999, which COVENIN 1999:2021 completely replaced, still in circulation and being treated as current
The written practice recites SNT-TC-1A but sets shorter training or experience hours than the recommended practice, with no documented technical justification
Training hours claimed from a centre that does not meet COVENIN 2967:2021 requirements for NDT training and qualification centres
Vision records missing, or older than twelve months, for technicians on active assignment
Procedures cite a code edition the client's specification does not call up, or cite a PDVSA specification the firm holds no controlled copy of
Level III signature appears on procedures covering a method the Level III is not himself certified in
Radiography performed without a current source authorisation, or with transport documentation that does not reconcile with the source inventory
No traceable calibration chain for thickness gauges and reference blocks used on mechanical integrity surveys
sources: SENCAMER standards catalogue record for COVENIN 1999:2021, "Requisitos para la calificación y certificación de personal en ensayos no destructivos", third revision, completely replacing COVENIN 1999:1999, revised by technical committee CT22 Ensayos No Destructivos under SENCAMER guidelines and aligned with ISO 9712; catalogue record for COVENIN 2967:2021 on NDT training and qualification centres; ISBN record 978-980-06-2366-4 for the COVENIN publication on qualification and certification of NDT personnel; Ley Orgánica del Sistema Venezolano para la Calidad, Gaceta Oficial N° 37.555 of 23 October 2002, establishing the standardisation, metrology, accreditation, certification, testing and technical regulation subsystems; SENCAMER public statements on the COVENIN corpus (3,921 standards through 54 technical committees), 34 technical regulations, the NORVEN mark and more than 40 accredited conformity assessment bodies; documented history of the standardisation function passing from COVENIN (Decreto 501, 1958) through FONDONORMA and SENORCA to SENCAMER, with SENCAMER assuming the national standardisation body role in July 2020; PDVSA IR-S-14 Integridad Mecánica, part of the PDVSA engineering risk manual, covering design, manufacture, installation, testing, inspection, monitoring and maintenance of critical equipment. SENCAMER's own servers were unreachable from this session in August 2026 and the full text of COVENIN 1999:2021 was not read, so no clause reference is given.

name: Trinidad and Tobago Bureau of Standards (TTBS) and the Occupational Safety and Health Act, Chap. 88:08
authority: Trinidad and Tobago Bureau of Standards (TTBS), including its laboratory accreditation arm TTLABS; the Occupational Safety and Health Authority and Agency; the Minister responsible, who licenses boiler examiners; the Ministry of Energy and Energy Industries for petroleum operations
appliesTo: NDT and inspection contractors serving the Point Lisas ammonia, methanol and iron estate, Atlantic LNG at Point Fortin, the Pointe-à-Pierre refinery complex, Heritage and Touchstone upstream, offshore platforms and the marine and dry-dock trade. It binds any firm examining steam boilers or air pressure containers, and any firm claiming accredited inspection status locally.
summary: Trinidad and Tobago has no NDT-specific regime, and the gap itself is the commercially important fact. TTBS's accreditation arm, TTLABS, accredits laboratories to ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO 15189 only, so there is no domestic route to ISO/IEC 17020 inspection body accreditation; firms go to JANAAC in Jamaica or to a foreign accreditation body, which is how TTBS's own Implementation Division came to hold ISO/IEC 17020:2012 accreditation. What is legally binding sits elsewhere. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, Chap. 88:08, and the Boilers Regulations and Air Pressure Containers Regulations continued in force by section 98(2), steam boilers and air pressure containers must be thoroughly examined every twelve months by a person holding a Ministerial licence who is independent of the occupier, owner or hirer.
personnelCertification: Employer-based certification is accepted for NDT, and is dominant. There is no local ISO 9712 certification body, and TTLABS does not accredit personnel certification bodies, so technicians hold employer certification written against ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the norm across the US-influenced petrochemical estate, or PCN and other ISO 9712 certificates issued in the UK. An outsourced Level III can write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and certify Level I and II staff. The statutory boiler and pressure-vessel examination is a separate and stricter matter: it requires a licence from the Minister plus personal independence from the equipment's owner, and no NDT certification substitutes for it.
requiredDocuments: Written practice to ASNT SNT-TC-1A, signed and dated by the Level III, covering every method, level and technique the company offers
Personnel certification files with training records, documented experience, examination papers and grading, and current near-vision and colour differentiation records
Written NDT procedures approved by the Level III against the code the client cites: ASME BPVC Section V, API 510, API 570, API 653 or AWS D1.1
Boiler examiner's licence issued by the Minister, unsuspended and uncancelled, for anyone examining steam boilers, economisers, superheaters or air pressure containers
Prescribed Form No. 7, report of examination of the boiler when cold, signed by the person making the examination
Prescribed Form No. 8, report of examination of the boiler under normal steam pressure, signed by the person making the examination
General Register entries or attachments, filed within twenty-one days of each statutory examination
Hydraulic test certificate specifying the maximum permissible working pressure and the tests applied, for any new or previously used boiler before it is taken into use
Equipment calibration certificates and reference block traceability records
Radiation-protection authorisation for gamma radiography sources, operators and source transport
auditProcess: Establish the statutory route first: identify which items on the client's site are steam boilers, economisers, superheaters or air pressure containers under the Act, because those require a Ministerially licensed examiner, not merely a certified NDT technician
Confirm the examiner's licence is current and that he is not in the employ of the occupier of the premises, nor of the owner or hirer of the equipment
Carry out the examination in the prescribed order: the boiler cold, with interior and exterior prepared to the examiner's satisfaction, then under normal steam pressure
Report on Forms 7 and 8, signed by the person making the examination, and enter or attach them to the General Register within twenty-one days
Where the client requires third-party accreditation, apply to JANAAC or another recognised accreditation body for ISO/IEC 17020 accreditation, since TTLABS does not offer that scheme
Maintain the twelve-month cycle, dated from completion of the examination under normal steam pressure
industries: Upstream oil and gas, onshore and offshore
renewal: The statutory intervals are fixed and verifiable. Steam boilers and all fittings and attachments: thorough examination at least once in every period of twelve months and also after any extensive repairs, with the twelve months running from completion of the examination under normal steam pressure; the competent person may extend that period by not more than one month in an emergency where shutdown would cause serious loss or damage, after which the next examination must fall within the succeeding eleven months. Air pressure containers: thoroughly cleaned, examined and hydraulically tested every twelve months. Hoists and lifts: thoroughly examined every twelve months. Boiler examiners' licences and the examination fee schedule are published in the Gazette on 1 January each year.
commonFindings: Boiler examination performed by an NDT contractor's Level II or Level III holding no Ministerial boiler examiner's licence
The examiner is on the occupier's payroll, or the owner's or hirer's, breaching the independence requirement the Boilers Regulations impose
Only the cold examination performed and the examination under normal steam pressure omitted, so the twelve-month clock never legitimately restarts
Forms 7 and 8 completed but not entered in or attached to the General Register within twenty-one days of the examination
A second-hand or relocated boiler taken back into use with no prior examination, hydraulic test and report
Air pressure containers treated as out of scope and inspected ad hoc, rather than on the twelve-month clean, examine and hydraulically test cycle
"Accredited" claimed on tender documents when the firm holds only ISO 9001 certification; TTLABS accredits laboratories, not inspection bodies, and the distinction is routinely blurred in local bids
Written practice imported unchanged from a US parent, listing methods and techniques the local branch has no certified Level III to support
sources: Occupational Safety and Health Act, 2004 (Act No. 1 of 2004), Chap. 88:08, as amended by Act No. 3 of 2006, Laws of Trinidad and Tobago revised edition, read directly: the Occupational Safety and Health (Prescribed Forms) Order (GN 187-1948) items 18 Hoists or Lifts, 19 Steam Boilers and 20 Air Pressure Containers; the Boilers Regulations (GN 2-1949) including the annual and other examinations provisions, the boiler examiner licence and independence requirement, Gazette publication of licences and the list of boiler examiners on 1 January each year, and the twenty-one day report filing period; the Special Provisions for Safety in the Case of Air Pressure Containers Regulations (GN 3-1949) including the competent person requirement; all continued in force by section 98(2). The Act, except section 98, came into operation by Proclamation LN 48/2006 on 17 February 2006, with section 98 brought into force by 17 August 2007, repealing the Factories Ordinance (Ch. 30 No. 2), the Employment of Women (Night Work) Act and the Gas Cylinders (Use, Conveyance and Storage) Act. TTBS website and TTLABS accreditation page (accessed August 2026) confirming accreditation to ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO 15189, ILAC and IAAC membership, and that the TTBS Implementation Division operates as an ISO/IEC 17020:2012 inspection body accredited by JANAAC; JANAAC website confirming ISO/IEC 17020 among its scopes alongside ISO/IEC 17025, ISO/IEC 17021-1 and ISO 15189, and its IAAC MLA and ILAC MRA signatory status; CROSQ report of TTBS Certification Division accreditation by JANAAC to ISO/IEC 17021-1:2015 on 3 October 2022. The Standards Act number and chapter establishing TTBS could not be verified from a primary source in this session and is therefore not stated.

name: Nadcap Audit Criteria for NonDestructive Testing (NDT) Auditees Accreditation Program — AC7114
jurisdiction: International — administered by PRI from Warrendale, Pennsylvania, with offices serving Europe and Asia-Pacific; driven by the US and European aerospace primes
authority: Performance Review Institute (PRI), a not-for-profit affiliate of SAE International, administering Nadcap on behalf of the Nadcap NDT Task Group and its subscribing primes
appliesTo: Any site that performs NDT on aerospace hardware: independent inspection service providers and NDT test houses, and captive NDT departments inside machining, casting, forging, fabrication and MRO shops. It binds when a subscribing prime — Boeing, GE Aviation, Pratt & Whitney, Rolls-Royce, Collins Aerospace, Safran, Honeywell, Lockheed Martin, Sikorsky, Bell, Eaton — flows Nadcap accreditation down as a purchase-order condition. Accreditation is granted per site and per method, not per company.
summary: AC7114 is the base checklist of the Nadcap NDT programme, and it audits the NDT quality system rather than any one method. It covers customer requirement flowdown and the sequencing of NDT operations, procurement control over sub-tier calibration and cleaning/etching facilities, an annual internal NDT audit, control and traceability of inspection status identifiers, inspection and traveller records, and calibration including interval extension. Section 5 audits people: the written practice, certification packages, vision records, the Responsible Level 3, outside Level 3 agencies and training course outlines. AC7114 is never used alone — every accredited method adds a slash sheet, and each prime may add a supplemental question set. The general quality system is covered by AS9100/EN9100, AC7004, or ISO/IEC 17025 for test houses.
personnelCertification: Employer-based. AC7114 audits the supplier's own written practice built to AIA/NAS 410 (EN 4179 in Europe); PRI certifies no individuals. Crucially the checklist explicitly contemplates an outsourced Level 3. Question 5.5.1 lets the employer designate either an Internal or an External Responsible Level 3 — a corporate Level 3 not stationed at the site counts as external. 5.5.2 requires every audited method to be covered by a Level 3, internal or external. 5.5.3 asks whether outside agencies provide Level 3 services and 5.5.4 requires documentation on file proving that outside Level 3 is certified to NAS 410/EN 4179. The employer, not the contractor, still signs the certifications.
requiredDocuments: Completed self-audit checklists — AC7114 plus every applicable slash sheet and supplement — uploaded to eAuditNet no less than 30 days before the scheduled audit, with the procedure and paragraph referenced for each question
NDT written practice for qualification and certification of personnel, approved by the Responsible Level 3
NDT method process procedures, plus the work instructions known in industry as technique sheets or data cards
List of Approved NDT Personnel including Level 3's, on attachment AC7114-A
NDT material and equipment list for each method on attachments AC7114/1A through AC7114/9A
Subscriber Matrix of Nadcap Subscribers that have approved the supplier for NDT — inaccuracy here is stated cause for a follow-up audit
Personnel certification packages: training records, experience, latest written and practical examinations, vision and colour-perception records
Annual internal NDT audit records, and the documented annual maintenance (technical proficiency) review for each certified individual in each method
Calibration certificates providing traceability to the unit of measure, and documented justification where a calibration interval has been extended
Proof on file of NAS 410 / EN 4179 certification for any outside-agency or corporate Level 3 used for examinations, procedure or technique approval, hardware inspection, or as Responsible Level 3
auditProcess: Register the site in eAuditNet, select the AC7114 base plus the slash sheets and subscriber supplements matching the methods and primes in scope, and request an audit date — PRI states most audits occur three to six months after scheduling is confirmed.
Run the self-audit against every selected checklist, correct internally identified nonconformances, and upload the self-audit and pre-audit document pack at least 30 days before the audit.

On-site audit, typically two to five days: in-brief attended by the Responsible Level 3 and quality manager, scope verification on the eAuditNet scope screen, system review plus one compliance job per method, with nonconformances raised daily and a closing meeting.

Respond to each NCR in eAuditNet with a five-part corrective action — root cause, immediate corrective action, action to prevent recurrence, product impact evaluation, and objective evidence. Elapsed time counts toward cumulative delinquency days, which govern merit eligibility.

PRI's NDT staff engineer compiles the audit pack; the NDT Task Group, made up of the subscribing primes, reviews it and ballots on accreditation — PRI describes this decision step as taking roughly a week once NCRs are closed.

Accreditation is granted and the certificate and Scope of Accreditation are published on the eAuditNet Qualified Manufacturers List. An NCR with potential product impact can, at the Task Group's discretion, trigger a Verification Corrective Action (VCA) audit at the supplier's expense.
renewal: Initial accreditation is 12 months. PRI states it can be extended to 18 months based on audit performance after three audits, and to 24 months after five audits, under the Supplier Merit Program. Both lengths appear on real certificates: an 18-month accreditation expiring 31 May 2023 and a 24-month accreditation expiring 31 May 2026 and 28 February 2027. Major NCRs, non-sustaining corrective actions and accumulated delinquency days cost a site its merit interval.
commonFindings: Self-audit uploaded late, performed against a superseded checklist revision, or not including one compliance job per method (AC7114 question 4)
Written practice not approved by the Responsible Level 3, or failing to identify every method and specific technique actually performed at the site
Techniques shown on an individual's certificate that do not appear as techniques in the written practice (question 5.2.3)

Near-vision examination not repeated annually, colour perception not repeated at least every five years, or the exam administered by someone not designated in writing by the Responsible Level 3 (questions 5.4.6, 5.4.7)

No documented annual maintenance review in each method for each individual certified to process and inspect hardware — the requirement applies to Level 3s too, and the record must name reviewee, reviewer, process and acceptance criteria, part identification, method and disposition
No proof on file of the outside or corporate Level 3's NAS 410 / EN 4179 certification (question 5.5.4)
Annual internal NDT audit missing, or not covering the inspection process, planning and traveller documentation, personnel certification records, procedures and equipment

Inspection status identifiers (stamps, initials, clock numbers) not controlled — no issue, recall and traceability register, or an identifier available to someone other than the individual it is assigned to
sources: AC7114 Rev L (Issued 1997-07, Revised 21-SEP-2017, superseding Rev K, to be used on audits starting on or after 31-DEC-2017) read in full for question numbering and Compliance Assessment Guidance. Current revisions confirmed from PRI-issued Nadcap NDT certificates and Scopes of Accreditation: AC7114 Rev S (audits on/after 19-May-2024) and AC7114S Rev R (on/after 10-Nov-2024) on 2025-dated certificates; AC7114 Rev R and AC7114S Rev Q on a certificate expiring 31 May 2026; AC7114 Rev P and AC7114S Rev O on a certificate expiring 31 May 2023. PRI Nadcap FAQ (accreditation length wording) and Getting Started pages, accessed 21 Aug 2026.

name: Nadcap NDT method slash sheets and subscriber supplemental checklists — the AC7114/n and AC7114/nS series
jurisdiction: International — same PRI/Nadcap NDT programme as the AC7114 base document
authority: Performance Review Institute (PRI) — Nadcap NDT Task Group; the supplemental 'S' sheets are owned by the individual subscribing primes
appliesTo: Every Nadcap NDT auditee, because the base AC7114 alone cannot be accredited. A shop adds one slash sheet for each method it wants on its Scope of Accreditation, plus the 'S' supplemental sheet for each prime that has approved it. A firm running penetrant, magnetic particle and film radiography is therefore audited against at least four criteria documents plus supplements in a single visit.
summary: The slash sheets are where Nadcap NDT gets method-specific. AC7114 states it 'is supplemented by Audit Criteria for specific NDT processes to be accredited and shall be used with the applicable Subscriber Supplemental Checklists.' Each method has a numbered slash sheet audited alongside the base; each has an 'S' twin carrying prime-specific questions keyed to subscriber codes; and each has a lettered attachment form on which the site declares its materials and equipment for that method. Scope, revision and effective date are all tracked per sheet, so a single site's certificate routinely lists documents at different revisions with different 'to be used on audits on/after' dates. Getting the slash-sheet selection wrong is the fastest way to have real work fall outside the accredited scope.
personnelCertification: The slash sheets do not create a separate certification scheme — certification stays employer-based to NAS 410/EN 4179 under the base document. What they do is define the granularity: the base checklist's certification-record table is laid out by slash sheet, with a row for AC7114/1, /2, '/3 and /7', /4, /5, /6, /8 and /9, and the auditor reviews at least one certification package for each method at each level issued since the last audit. So the Level 3 — internal or external — must hold NAS 410/EN 4179 certification in every method whose slash sheet is on the scope, and personnel certificates must name the technique, not just the method.
requiredDocuments: The applicable slash sheet completed as a self-audit for every method in scope, uploaded with the base AC7114 self-audit 30 days before the audit
The applicable subscriber supplemental sheet (AC7114S, AC7114/1S, /2S, /3S, /4S, /5S, /10S) for each prime shown on the Subscriber Matrix
Per-method material and equipment attachment forms: AC7114/1A, /2A, /3A, /4A, /5A, /6A, /7A, /8A, /9A
Method process procedure and the technique sheets or data cards for the parts to be run as compliance jobs
Records for the process control tools and reference standards used for equipment set-up in that method
Certification packages, filed so they can be produced by method and level for each slash sheet on the scope
Current Scope of Accreditation from the eAuditNet Qualified Manufacturers List, to confirm which slash sheets and revisions the site is actually accredited to
auditProcess: Select the slash sheets that match the methods actually performed and confirm them on the eAuditNet scope verification screen with the auditor — digital radiography, for example, needs AC7114/10 and is not covered by the film radiography sheet AC7114/4.

Check revision effectivity before preparing: PRI publishes each sheet with a 'to be used on audits on/after' date and issues change notifications, and an existing self-audit performed before a revision was released may not be acceptable.
Complete a self-audit per slash sheet and populate the matching AC7114/nA attachment with the site's materials and equipment for that method.
Provide one compliance job per method so the auditor can follow a real part through that method's process procedure, technique sheet, process control checks and reporting.
Answer the subscriber supplemental questions for each prime on the Subscriber Matrix; supplements are audited in the same visit and produce NCRs against the S document, not the base.
Close NCRs per document in eAuditNet; the Task Group ballots the whole pack, and the resulting certificate lists each slash sheet with its revision and the subscriber codes accredited under it.
methodsInScope: UT — AC7114/3 (with AC7114/7 in the same personnel-record grouping)
Remote image and film viewing — AC7114/9
Digital radiography DDA and computed radiography CR/PSL — AC7114/10
renewal: The slash sheets follow the base accreditation cycle — 12 months initially, extendable to 18 and then 24 months under the Supplier Merit Program — but each document is revised on its own clock. A single 2025-dated certificate shows AC7114 Rev S effective for audits on/after 19-May-2024, AC7114/2 Rev P and AC7114/3 Rev O both on/after 17-Mar-2024, and AC7114/1 Rev O marked for audits before 16-Feb-2025, meaning a newer revision took effect mid-cycle. Revision effectivity must be re-checked before every audit, not once per accreditation.
commonFindings: Scope on the Qualified Manufacturers List does not match what the shop runs — most often digital radiography or computed radiography performed while only the film radiography sheet AC7114/4 is on the scope
Self-audit prepared on a superseded slash-sheet revision after PRI had already posted and notified the new one
Subscriber Matrix inaccurate, so the supplemental checklist for a prime that has approved the site was never run — AC7114 states this is cause for a follow-up audit
Per-method material and equipment attachment (AC7114/1A through /9A) not completed or not available at the time of the audit
Technique sheets or data cards for the method not reviewed and approved by a Level 3 certified in that specific method
Process control tools or reference standards used for equipment set-up in the method not controlled, calibrated or traceable
No compliance job available for a method in scope, so the auditor cannot witness that method end to end
Subscriber supplemental questions answered by pointing at the base-checklist response rather than the prime's specific requirement
sources: AC7114 Rev L (Revised 21-SEP-2017) read in full — Section 2.2.1/2.2.2 for the attachment series AC7114-A and AC7114/1A–/9A and the Subscriber Matrix, and the certification-record tables listing AC7114/1, /2, '/3 and /7', /4, /5, /6, /8, /9. Slash-sheet titles and revisions taken from PRI-issued Scopes of Accreditation: AC7114/1 Rev N and Rev O (Penetrant), /2 Rev N and Rev P (Magnetic Particle), /3 Rev N and Rev O (Ultrasonic), /4 Rev N (Film Radiography), /5 Rev F (Eddy Current), /9 Rev B (Remote Image and Film Viewing), /10 Rev B (Digital Radiography DDA and CR/PSL), and the matching /1S, /2S, /3S, /4S, /5S, /10S supplements with subscriber codes U1 Honeywell, U2 Pratt & Whitney, U3 Rolls-Royce plc, U4 Lockheed Martin, U6 Rolls-Royce Corporation, U10 GE Aviation, U11 Boeing, U14 Safran, U16 Bell Helicopter, U17 Sikorsky, U21 Eaton, U26 Collins Aerospace (Goodrich). AC7114/11 Rev A is listed as a posted document on the Japanese Aerospace Quality Group AC list dated 03-Dec-2021. NOTE: the numbers AC7114/6, /7, /8 and /11 are confirmed to exist, but their subject titles were not verifiable from a primary source and are deliberately not stated here — AC7114/7 is grouped with AC7114/3 in the base checklist's personnel-record table, which places it in the ultrasonic family. All sources accessed 21 Aug 2026.

name: Title 14 Code of Federal Regulations Part 145 — Repair Stations, with the limited rating for nondestructive inspection, testing, and processing
jurisdiction: United States — FAA certificate; also held by repair stations located outside the US under bilateral aviation safety agreements
authority: Federal Aviation Administration, Flight Standards Service; day-to-day oversight sits with the repair station's responsible Flight Standards office
appliesTo: NDT firms whose inspection results are used to return civil aeronautical articles to service. A standalone NDT house needs its own repair station certificate carrying the §145.61(b)(9) limited rating for nondestructive inspection, testing, and processing. Alternatively the firm works as a noncertificated contractor to a repair station, in which case the repair station must qualify and surveil it under its own quality control system. Covers aircraft, engines, propellers, accessories and components.
summary: Part 145 does not describe NDT techniques; it regulates the organisation that performs them. The FAA issues a limited rating for 'Nondestructive inspection, testing, and processing' under §145.61(b)(9), and §145.61(c) requires the repair station's operations specifications to name the specification used for the specialized service — either a civil or military specification currently used by industry and approved by the FAA, or one the applicant develops and the FAA approves. Around that sit §145.151 personnel, §145.155 inspection personnel proficiency and English literacy, §145.163 an FAA-approved initial and recurrent training program with records kept at least two years, and §145.211(c) a quality control manual that must describe how inspection personnel proficiency is established and maintained and how measuring and test equipment is calibrated, including intervals.
personnelCertification: Employer-based, and the FAA says so plainly. AC 65-31B defines certification as 'written testimony of qualification that the employer typically issues' and states: 'In the United States, there is no national certifying agency; therefore, most certifications are employer-based and are not transferrable.' The AC lists acceptable standards — AIA-NAS-410, ATA Specification 105, CAN/CGSB-48.9712-95, ISO 9712, MIL-STD-410E (rescinded but acceptable), ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and prEN 4179. It defines an 'Outside Agency' as an independent body under contract for NDI services, explicitly including consultants and self-employed individuals, and paragraph 9b permits a qualified outside agency to provide NDI training, qualification and testing at the organisation's option and as provided in its written practice.
requiredDocuments: Application for a repair station certificate and rating, with the attachments required by §145.51(a)
Operations specifications containing the specification used to perform the specialized service, per §145.61(c)

Repair station manual, and the quality control manual required by §145.211(c) covering preliminary, hidden-damage and final inspection, establishing and maintaining proficiency of inspection personnel, current technical data, qualifying and surveilling noncertificated persons who perform maintenance, calibration of measuring and test equipment including intervals, and corrective action on deficiencies
FAA-approved employee training program under §145.163(a), submitted per §145.51(a)(7), with individual training records documented and retained a minimum of two years

Written NDI qualification and certification program — the written practice — describing training, examination, qualification, documentation, proficiency maintenance, and the steps to decertify, retrain or recertify (AC 65-31B paragraph 9a)

Personnel records specifying date, time and place of qualification, employing organisation, level, special qualifications or limitations, and the standard under which the individual is qualified, including a copy of any FAA repairman certificate issued to that individual (AC 65-31B paragraph 12)

Vision examination records — near vision to Snellen 20/25 or Jaeger #1 in at least one eye, corrected or uncorrected, on a periodic basis not exceeding one year; colour perception evaluated once at initial examination with any limitation approved in writing by the responsible Level III
Calibration records for NDI instruments traceable to a national metrological institute such as NIST
Contracting arrangements and evidence of qualification and surveillance for any noncertificated person performing maintenance functions, as required by §145.151(d) and the quality control manual
auditProcess: Pre-application discussion with the responsible Flight Standards office to agree the rating sought and the specification that will be named in the operations specifications for the NDI specialized service.
Formal application under §145.51 with the repair station manual, quality control manual and the employee training program required by §145.51(a)(7).
FAA review of the submitted manuals and program for compliance with §§145.207, 145.209, 145.211 and 145.163, with revision cycles until they are acceptable to the FAA.

On-site evaluation of housing, facilities, equipment, materials and data under §145.109, and demonstration that inspection personnel meet §145.155 and that the quality control system is actually being followed.
Issue of the certificate, the ratings and limitations, and the operations specifications naming the approved NDI specification.

Continued operational surveillance by the responsible Flight Standards office, with revisions to the quality control manual notified under §145.211(d) and training program revisions submitted under §145.163(d).
methodsInScope: Eddy current array and phased array where covered by the approved specification and the written practice
renewal: Under §145.55(a) a certificate or rating issued to a repair station located in the United States is effective from the date of issue until surrendered and accepted for cancellation, or suspended or revoked — there is no periodic expiry. Under §145.55(b) a certificate issued to a repair station located outside the United States expires on the last day of the 12th month after issue and the FAA may renew it for 24 months; renewal must be requested no later than 30 days before expiry and the prescribed fee paid, otherwise the full §145.51 application procedure applies. Personnel recertification runs on the AC 65-31B intervals: Level I Special not exceeding one year, Levels I and II not exceeding three years, Level III at five-year intervals, with requalification also triggered by six months of inactivity in the method or an expired vision examination.
commonFindings: The specification named in the operations specifications for the NDI specialized service does not match the specification the technicians actually work to
Quality control manual silent on how proficiency of inspection personnel is established and maintained, which §145.211(c)(1)(iv) requires explicitly
Employee training program treated as generic safety training with no method-specific initial and recurrent NDI content, or training records not retained for the full two years required by §145.163(c)
Vision examinations lapsed beyond the one-year period, or colour-perception limitations never evaluated and approved in writing by the responsible Level III
Written practice references SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410 but the recertification intervals actually applied do not match the standard the organisation says it follows
Outside agency used for training, qualification or testing without that use being provided for in the written practice, as AC 65-31B paragraph 9b requires
No documented qualification and surveillance of the noncertificated NDT contractor performing work under the repair station certificate
Calibration of NDI measuring and test equipment performed without stated intervals in the quality control manual or without traceability to a national standard
sources: 14 CFR §§145.51, 145.55, 145.59, 145.61, 145.151, 145.155, 145.163, 145.211 as published in the electronic CFR via Cornell LII, current text including Docket FAA-2016-8744 Amdt. 145-31 (81 FR 49163, 27 July 2016) for §145.61 and Amdt. 145-32 (83 FR 9176, 5 March 2018) for §145.163. FAA Advisory Circular 65-31B, 'Training, Qualification, and Certification of Nondestructive Inspection Personnel,' dated 2/24/14, initiated by AFS-300, cancelling AC 65-31A of 25 April 2003, read in full — paragraphs 3, 5d, 5u, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12. Accessed 21 Aug 2026.

name: Appendix B to 10 CFR Part 50 — Quality Assurance Criteria for Nuclear Power Plants and Fuel Reprocessing Plants
authority: U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission
appliesTo: Directly, it binds NRC licensees and applicants. Practically it reaches every NDT service provider working on safety-related structures, systems and components, because the licensee flows the criteria down by contract and remains accountable. Appendix B states the applicant may delegate the work of establishing and executing the QA program to contractors, agents or consultants but 'shall retain responsibility.' Covers design, manufacture, construction, operation, maintenance, repair, refuelling and modification.
summary: Appendix B sets eighteen quality assurance criteria for activities affecting the safety-related functions of nuclear structures, systems and components. For an inspection service provider two criteria bite hardest. Criterion IX, Control of Special Processes, requires measures assuring that special processes 'including welding, heat treating, and nondestructive testing, are controlled and accomplished by qualified personnel using qualified procedures in accordance with applicable codes, standards, specifications, criteria, and other special requirements.' Criterion X, Inspection, requires inspection by individuals other than those who performed the activity being inspected. Criterion XVII requires records identifying the inspector or data recorder, the type of observation, the results, the acceptability and the action taken on any deficiency. Criterion XVIII requires planned periodic audits by trained personnel without direct responsibility in the area audited.
personnelCertification: Appendix B is method-agnostic and names no certification scheme: Criterion IX simply requires qualified personnel and qualified procedures 'in accordance with applicable codes, standards, specifications.' The scheme therefore comes from whatever code the licensee imposes — in practice ASME Section XI with ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189, or NQA-1. That makes certification employer-based: the supplier writes and owns the written practice and signs the certificates. An outsourced Level III can author and approve the written practice and the NDE procedures and can administer examinations, but Criterion I requires that whoever performs quality assurance verification have organisational freedom and sufficient independence, and the supplier's own management retains the responsibility.
requiredDocuments: Quality assurance program description covering all eighteen criteria, with the organisational chart and delegated authorities required by Criterion I
Documented instructions, procedures and drawings for activities affecting quality, with quantitative or qualitative acceptance criteria (Criterion V)
Special process procedures for nondestructive testing, with evidence the procedures and the personnel are qualified (Criterion IX)
Inspection program showing inspection is performed by individuals other than those who performed the work, and identifying any mandatory hold points (Criterion X)
Procurement documents imposing the applicable regulatory, code and QA requirements on sub-tier suppliers (Criterion IV) and the supplier evaluation and assessment records required by Criterion VII
Calibration and control records for measuring and test equipment (Criterion XII)

Nonconformance and corrective action records, with the cause and the action to preclude repetition documented and reported to management for significant conditions adverse to quality (Criteria XV and XVI)

Inspection and test records identifying the inspector or data recorder, the type of observation, the results, the acceptability and the action taken on deficiencies, plus qualifications of personnel, procedures and equipment (Criterion XVII)
Internal audit plan, checklists, reports and reaudit records demonstrating a comprehensive system of planned and periodic audits (Criterion XVIII)
auditProcess: The licensee or its designee evaluates the supplier before award — Criterion VII requires source evaluation and selection, and control of purchased services proportionate to their importance.
The supplier submits its QA program manual and procedures for the licensee's review against the eighteen criteria and against whatever code the contract invokes.

On-site audit by the licensee, its designee, or a joint programme such as NUPIC, performed to written procedures or checklists by trained personnel not having direct responsibilities in the area audited (Criterion XVIII).

Findings are documented and reviewed by management having responsibility in the area audited; the supplier responds with cause determination and corrective action to preclude repetition (Criterion XVI).
Followup, including reaudit of deficient areas where indicated, then placement on the licensee's Approved Suppliers List for the specific scope of services.

Criterion VII requires the effectiveness of the supplier's quality control to be reassessed at intervals consistent with the importance, complexity and quantity of the service — which is what drives the recurring audit cycle.
methodsInScope: Any NDE method invoked by the applicable construction or inservice code
industries: Fuel cycle and fuel reprocessing facilities
Small modular and advanced reactor supply chain
renewal: Appendix B sets no expiry — it is a standing regulatory requirement, not a certificate. What recurs is verification. Criterion XVIII requires a comprehensive system of planned and periodic audits, and Criterion VII requires the licensee to assess the effectiveness of a supplier's quality control 'at intervals consistent with the importance, complexity, and quantity of the product or services.' For NDT service suppliers this normally lands on the joint utility audit cycle — NUPIC runs most vendors on a 33-month schedule — supplemented by annual internal audits.
commonFindings: QA manual written to the eighteen criteria in the abstract with no procedure translating Criterion IX into control of NDE special processes at the working level
Independence problem under Criterion X — the technician who performed the examination also signs the verifying inspection
Records failing Criterion XVII because the inspection record does not identify the inspector or data recorder, the type of observation, the acceptability, or the action taken on a deficiency
Sub-tier flowdown gaps under Criteria IV and VII — calibration houses, consumables suppliers or contract technicians procured without the applicable QA and 10 CFR Part 21 requirements imposed
Corrective action stopping at the immediate fix, with no documented determination of cause and action to preclude repetition as Criterion XVI requires
Internal audits performed by someone with direct responsibility in the area audited, or with no checklist, contrary to Criterion XVIII
Measuring and test equipment used out of calibration with no evaluation of the validity of previous results (Criterion XII)
Commercial-grade items and services used in safety-related work without a dedication process, so the item never qualifies as a basic component
sources: Appendix B to 10 CFR Part 50, 'Quality Assurance Criteria for Nuclear Power Plants and Fuel Reprocessing Plants,' full text from the GPO govinfo CFR annual edition, Title 10 Volume 1, revised as of 1 January 2024 — Introduction and Criteria I through XVIII, quoting Criterion IX, X, XVII and XVIII verbatim. Cross-referenced against 10 CFR Part 21, 'Reporting of Defects and Noncompliance,' same edition, whose definition of 'basic component' at paragraph (4) expressly includes 'safety-related design, analysis, inspection, testing, fabrication, replacement of parts, or consulting services... whether these services are performed by the component supplier or others.' Accessed 21 Aug 2026.

name: ASME NQA-1, Quality Assurance Requirements for Nuclear Facility Applications
jurisdiction: United States, and internationally wherever it is invoked by contract; NRC-endorsed for US nuclear facility work
authority: The American Society of Mechanical Engineers (standard owner and operator of the voluntary NQA-1 Certification programme); the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission endorses it through Regulatory Guide 1.28, and the U.S. Department of Energy imposes it on its own contractors
appliesTo: Suppliers of items or services with a safety function for nuclear facilities — including inspection, examination and testing services. It reaches NDT service providers working for operating reactors, new build, SMR and advanced reactor programmes, DOE sites, and nuclear component manufacturers. NQA-1 is imposed contractually by the customer; ASME's NQA-1 Quality Program Certificate is a separate, voluntary third-party attestation that the supplier's programme conforms.
summary: NQA-1 is the implementing standard that turns the eighteen abstract criteria of 10 CFR 50 Appendix B into auditable requirements. Part I contains the eighteen Requirements — Organization; Quality Assurance Program; Design Control; Procurement Document Control; Instructions, Procedures and Drawings; Document Control; Control of Purchased Items and Services; Identification and Control of Items; Control of Special Processes; Inspection; Test Control; Control of Measuring and Test Equipment; Handling, Storage and Shipping; Inspection, Test and Operating Status; Control of Nonconforming Items; Corrective Action; Quality Assurance Records; Audits. Part II adds supplemental subparts for specific activities, including Subpart 2.7 Software Control and Subpart 2.14 Commercial Grade Dedication. Requirement 9 covers special processes such as welding and NDE; Requirement 2 covers indoctrination, training and the qualification of inspection and test personnel. A graded approach lets the degree of application follow the quality level of the work.
personnelCertification: Employer-based. NQA-1 does not certify individuals and does not operate a central scheme; Requirement 2 makes the supplier responsible for indoctrination, training and for qualifying inspection, examination and test personnel, and for NDE it points to the ASNT documents — ASNT Recommended Practice SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189 — implemented through the supplier's own written practice. That means an outsourced Level III can write and approve the written practice and the NDE procedures, administer and grade examinations, and sign as the certifying technical authority where the written practice designates them, while the employing supplier retains the certification decision and the records. ASME's NQA-1 certificate attests to the programme, not to any individual.
requiredDocuments: Quality Assurance Program manual mapped to the eighteen Part I Requirements, with the graded approach and quality levels defined
Indoctrination and training records — attendance sheets, training logs and personnel training records — and records of qualification for inspection and test personnel under Requirement 2
NDE written practice to SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189, with the NDE procedures qualified under Requirement 9, Control of Special Processes
Inspection and test plans and acceptance criteria under Requirements 10 and 11, and the inspection, test and operating status controls of Requirement 14
Procurement documents and Approved Suppliers List evidence under Requirements 4 and 7, including sub-tier flowdown of NQA-1 and 10 CFR Part 21
Commercial grade dedication procedure and critical characteristics records where Part II Subpart 2.14 applies
Software control documentation under Part II Subpart 2.7 for any NDE acquisition, analysis or sizing software used in safety-related work
Nonconforming item and corrective action records under Requirements 15 and 16
Audit programme records — plan, checklist, report and evidence of corrective action completion — under Requirement 18
Quality assurance records under Requirement 17, held in storage meeting the standard's fire-protection provisions
auditProcess: Build the programme to Part I and the applicable Part II subparts, applying the graded approach to the quality level of the work actually sold.
Submit the QA manual for review — to the customer directly, or to ASME through CA Connect if seeking the voluntary NQA-1 Quality Program Certificate.

Implement and generate objective evidence: NQA-1 certification and customer audits both assess implementation, not just the manual, so the programme must have been running long enough to produce records.

Undergo the assessment — for ASME certification, a full audit of the quality assurance program by trained ASME auditors; for customer acceptance, an Appendix B supplier audit by the licensee or a joint programme such as NUPIC.

Close findings with cause determination and corrective action under Requirement 16, then receive the NQA-1 Quality Program Certificate or placement on the customer's Approved Suppliers List for the defined scope.
Maintain through internal audits under Requirement 18 and periodic reassessment by ASME or the customer.
industries: U.S. Department of Energy sites and national laboratories
Fuel cycle and radioactive materials processing
Nuclear inspection and testing service providers
renewal: NQA-1 compliance itself does not expire; it is maintained continuously and verified by audit. NQA-1 Part I Requirement 18 requires audits to verify compliance with the programme, and in practice suppliers run internal audits of all requirements annually and are audited by customers on a recurring cycle — NUPIC's standard vendor schedule is 33 months. The ASME NQA-1 Quality Program Certificate is renewed by reassessment; ASME publishes a price guide covering both new certificates and renewals but does not publish the renewal interval on its programme pages, so it is not stated here.
commonFindings: Programme written to Part I but silent on the Part II subparts the work actually triggers — most often Subpart 2.7 for NDE acquisition and sizing software and Subpart 2.14 for commercial grade dedication
Graded approach applied inconsistently, so safety-related work is executed under procedures written for a lower quality level
Requirement 2 records incomplete — training and indoctrination logged but no qualification records for the individuals performing inspection and examination
NDE written practice not aligned to the specific edition of SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 that the customer's procurement documents invoked
Requirement 9 special process control missing the link between the qualified procedure, the qualified personnel and the specific job performed
Requirement 7 sub-tier control weak — calibration laboratories or contract technicians engaged without evaluation, survey, or dedication
Requirement 18 audits performed by personnel with direct responsibility in the area audited, or audit packages missing the plan, checklist, report or corrective action closure
Requirement 12 measuring and test equipment found out of tolerance with no evaluation of the acceptability of items previously inspected with it
sources: ASME NQA-1-2022, 'Quality Assurance Requirements for Nuclear Facility Applications' (ASME/ANSI listing); ASME NQA-1-2024 issued 24 July 2024 is the newest edition. NRC Regulatory Guide 1.28, Revision 6, 'Quality Assurance Program Criteria (Design and Construction),' issued September 2023 and announced in the Federal Register on 11 September 2023, endorses NQA-1-2017, NQA-1-2019 and NQA-1-2022 subject to exceptions and clarifications, extends endorsement to Part II, and also endorses NEI 14-05A Revision 1 (September 2020) for accreditation in lieu of commercial grade surveys for laboratory calibration and test services. Part I Requirement list and the Part II Subpart 2.7 and 2.14 titles cross-checked against an ASME/ANS Section technical overview presentation dated 21 January 2026 and ASME's own standard page. ASME NQA-1 Certification programme description and CA Connect process from asme.org. NOTE: the specific paragraph number within Requirement 2 that addresses NDE personnel could not be confirmed from the standard itself and is deliberately omitted. Accessed 21 Aug 2026.

name: Nuclear Procurement Issues Committee joint utility supplier audits and commercial grade surveys
jurisdiction: United States, with international nuclear plant operators participating as members
authority: NUPIC — a committee of NRC licensees and international nuclear plant operators, self-governing, with audits performed by lead auditors and team members drawn from the member utilities
appliesTo: Suppliers of safety-related items and services to US nuclear plants, including NDT and inservice inspection service providers, calibration laboratories and commercial-grade item manufacturers. A supplier qualifies for a NUPIC audit if it has at least five customers who are NRC licensees or international nuclear plant operators; sponsorship by five NUPIC members automatically enrolls the supplier into the audit schedule.
summary: NUPIC is not a regulator and issues no certificate. It is a cost-sharing mechanism: rather than every utility auditing the same NDT vendor separately to 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, member utilities run one joint audit, and the resulting report is shared with the membership so each licensee can use it to place the supplier on its own Approved Suppliers List. NUPIC distinguishes a full audit, which examines compliance with 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, from a commercial grade survey, which assesses the critical characteristics of the components supplied. It publishes the checklists used and an annual audit and survey schedule, and its programme documents are numbered — NUPIC Document 6 describes the joint audit programme and Document 11 the implementation guidelines.
personnelCertification: NUPIC certifies nobody and imposes no scheme of its own; it verifies that the supplier's programme meets 10 CFR 50 Appendix B and whatever code the licensees invoke, which for NDT means employer-based certification under a written practice built to ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189, and to ASME Section XI where inservice inspection is in scope. An outsourced Level III can therefore own the written practice, qualify and examine personnel, and approve procedures — but NUPIC auditors will look for the employer's own certification signatures, the objective evidence behind each certification package, and documented justification that the contracted Level III is qualified for that role.
requiredDocuments: Quality assurance manual, which NUPIC suppliers may submit for posting on the NUPIC website at no charge so member utilities can download it
NDE written practice and the personnel certification packages behind it — training, experience, written, practical and where applicable specific examinations, plus vision records
NDE procedures and, where inservice inspection is in scope, evidence of ASME Section XI Appendix VII qualification and Appendix VIII performance demonstration
Completed NUPIC Audit Checklist, NUPIC Survey Checklist or Calibration Checklist as applicable to the scope
Commercial grade dedication and critical characteristics documentation where the supplier is being surveyed rather than audited
10 CFR Part 21 procedure covering evaluation of deviations and reporting of defects and failures to comply
Calibration records with traceability, and for calibration and testing services any ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation being relied on under the NUPIC ILAC process and NEI 14-05A
Internal audit programme records and the corrective action programme
Approved sub-tier supplier list and evidence of sub-tier evaluation and flowdown
auditProcess: Reach the eligibility threshold — at least five customers who are NRC licensees or international nuclear plant operators — and obtain sponsorship from five NUPIC members, which automatically enrolls the supplier into the standard audit schedule.
NUPIC publishes the annual audit schedule and survey schedule; the sponsoring utility facility takes responsibility for arranging the audit and bears its cost. Vendors pay no NUPIC membership fee.
Submit the quality assurance manual in advance, optionally posting it on the NUPIC site so member utilities can review it before the visit.

Host the audit — typically about five days, conducted between 8am and 5pm Monday to Friday, longer or shorter with the complexity of the organisation — run against the NUPIC Audit Checklist for a full 10 CFR 50 Appendix B audit, or the Survey Checklist where critical characteristics of supplied components are the focus.
Respond to findings with corrective action; the audit team closes them and issues the joint audit report into the NUPIC system for the membership.

Each member utility independently accepts the report and places the supplier on its own Approved Suppliers List for a defined scope of supply. The next audit falls on the standard 33-month cycle for most vendors, or 36 months for fuel suppliers.
methodsInScope: Eddy current steam generator tube inspection
industries: Nuclear component and spare parts manufacturing
Calibration and testing laboratories serving nuclear licensees
Commercial grade item suppliers and dedicating entities
renewal: Most vendors sit on NUPIC's standard 33-month audit schedule; fuel suppliers are on a 36-month cycle. Continued eligibility depends on retaining member sponsorship — an audit is arranged and paid for by the sponsoring utility facility, so a supplier that loses sponsors falls off the joint schedule and reverts to individual utility audits.
commonFindings: Written practice and certification packages inconsistent — certificates issued for methods or techniques the training and experience records do not support
10 CFR Part 21 procedure absent or not recognising that inspection, testing and consulting services are themselves basic components under the Part 21 definition
Commercial grade dedication performed without identifying critical characteristics or without the acceptance methods required, so the item never becomes a basic component
Calibration laboratory relied on without an evaluation, or with an ISO/IEC 17025 scope that does not actually cover the parameter and range being used
Sub-tier NDT contractors used on safety-related scopes without evaluation, flowdown of Appendix B and Part 21, or surveillance
Corrective action programme closing conditions adverse to quality without cause determination or extent-of-condition review
Internal audits not covering all programme elements within the stated frequency, or performed by personnel with responsibility in the audited area
Records retention and legibility failures — inspection records that do not identify the examiner, the observation, the acceptability, and the disposition of deficiencies
sources: NUPIC official website (nupic.com) — home page, FAQ and Documentation pages, accessed 21 Aug 2026 — for eligibility (five NRC licensee or international operator customers), sponsorship by five members, the standard 33-month audit schedule and the 36-month fuel supplier cycle, approximately five-day audit duration conducted 8am–5pm Monday to Friday, the distinction between a full audit against 10 CFR 50 Appendix B and a commercial grade survey of critical characteristics, no vendor membership fee with the sponsoring customer facility bearing audit cost, the NUPIC Audit Checklist, NUPIC Survey Checklist and Calibration Checklist, the QA manual submission facility, and the document set: NUPIC Document 6 Joint Audit Program Description, Document 10 Joint Commercial Grade Survey Program Description, Document 11 Joint Audit and Checklist Implementation Guidelines, Document 21 Commercial Grade Item Survey Implementation Guidelines, Document 29 Commercial Grade Calibration Services Implementation Guidelines, plus 2024, 2025 and 2026 audit and survey schedules and the ILAC page referencing NEI-14-05-A Rev 1 and the ILAC MRA signatory list updated August 2024. Cross-referenced to 10 CFR Part 21 and Appendix B to 10 CFR Part 50, govinfo CFR annual edition revised 1 January 2024.

name: ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section XI — Rules for Inservice Inspection of Nuclear Reactor Facility Components, made mandatory by 10 CFR 50.55a
jurisdiction: United States (mandatory through NRC regulation); adopted or adapted by nuclear regulators elsewhere
authority: ASME writes and maintains the Code; the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission makes it mandatory and conditions it through 10 CFR 50.55a. Compliance is verified in the field by the Authorized Nuclear Inservice Inspector
appliesTo: NDE service providers performing inservice inspection on Class 1, 2 and 3 components, supports and containments at operating light-water reactors, and the vendors supplying UT, ET and VT examination services during refuelling outages. It also binds repair and replacement activities on the pressure boundary. The licensee owns the ISI programme; the service provider must qualify its procedures, equipment and personnel into it.
summary: Section XI sets the mandatory examination, inspection and testing programme for nuclear reactor facility components in service: which welds and components get examined, by which NDE methods, on what schedule, against which flaw acceptance standards, and how repair and replacement activities are controlled. 10 CFR 50.55a(g)(4) requires inservice examination during successive 120-month inspection intervals to comply with the latest edition and addenda incorporated by reference eighteen months before the interval starts. IWA-2300 governs qualification of NDE personnel including VT-1, VT-2 and VT-3. Mandatory Appendix VII sets training and experience; Mandatory Appendix VIII sets performance demonstration for ultrasonic examination systems, integrating personnel, equipment and procedure into a single qualified entity. The Authorized Nuclear Inservice Inspector verifies completion before the plant returns to service.
personnelCertification: Two layers, and only the first is employer-based. For basic qualification, Section XI is employer-certified: IWA-2300 requires certification under a written practice to ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189 as referenced in IWA-1600, the employer is solely responsible for certifying Levels I, II and III, and outside agencies may be used to qualify NDE personnel — so an outsourced Level III can own the written practice and sign as the technical authority. The second layer is not employer-based: ultrasonic examinations covered by Mandatory Appendix VIII require a performance demonstration, in practice through the utility-owned, EPRI-operated Performance Demonstration Initiative. No written practice substitutes for a failed PDI demonstration.
requiredDocuments: Owner's inservice inspection programme plan for the current 120-month interval, identifying the Code edition and addenda of record
NDE written practice to SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189 as referenced in IWA-1600, with the personnel certification records it produces
Appendix VII training and experience records supporting each examiner's qualification level and method
Appendix VIII performance demonstration qualification records for each examiner, procedure and equipment combination, by applicable Supplement

Records of the annual hands-on training required by 10 CFR 50.55a(b)(2)(xiv) — eight hours on specimens containing cracks, or the Appendix VII VII-4240 annual practice on cracked material or prerecorded data from cracked welds — completed no earlier than six months before performing UT at the licensee's facility
NDE procedures qualified to the applicable Appendix, with essential variables controlled and demonstrated
Calibration blocks and reference standards, with the calibration and traceability records for examination equipment

Examination reports and indication records feeding the Owner's Activity Report or Summary Report described in IWA-6230, which must be submitted to the NRC within 120 calendar days of the completion of each refuelling outage

Quality assurance programme evidence — the licensee's 10 CFR 50 Appendix B programme applied to Section XI activities, using an NQA-1 edition permitted by Table IWA-1600-1 and incorporated by reference in 50.55a
auditProcess: The licensee defines the ISI programme for the 120-month interval against the Code edition and addenda incorporated by reference eighteen months before the interval began, plus the NRC conditions in 10 CFR 50.55a(b)(2).
The examination vendor's NDE procedures are reviewed and accepted into the licensee's programme, with essential variables and applicable Appendix VIII Supplements identified.

Examiners qualify: Appendix VII training and experience first, then Appendix VIII performance demonstration through the EPRI-operated PDI for the specific Supplements covering the components to be examined.
The licensee or a joint programme such as NUPIC audits the vendor's 10 CFR 50 Appendix B / NQA-1 quality programme and its certification, calibration and records systems before award.

Outage execution under the Authorized Nuclear Inservice Inspector, who verifies that required examinations were completed before the plant returns to service, with the annual hands-on training refreshed no earlier than six months before the examinations.

Results are evaluated against the Section XI acceptance standards; the Owner's Activity Report or Summary Report under IWA-6230 is submitted to the NRC within 120 calendar days of the end of the refuelling outage.
methodsInScope: ET including steam generator tube inspection
VT-1, VT-2 and VT-3 visual examination
industries: Reactor vessel and steam generator inspection specialists
Nuclear engineering and flaw evaluation consultancies
renewal: Two clocks. The programme clock: successive 120-month inspection intervals, each updated to the latest edition and addenda incorporated by reference eighteen months before the interval starts, per 10 CFR 50.55a(g)(4). The personnel clock: 10 CFR 50.55a(b)(2)(xviii)(A) overrides the Code — Level I and II NDE personnel must be recertified on a 3-year interval in lieu of the 5-year interval specified in IWA-2314(a) and IWA-2314(b), for the 2001 Edition through the latest edition incorporated by reference. Appendix VIII qualification carries its own currency requirement, with eight hours of hands-on training on cracked specimens annually, completed no earlier than six months before performing examinations at a licensee's facility.
commonFindings: Level I and II certifications written to the Code's 5-year recertification interval, missing the NRC's 3-year override in 10 CFR 50.55a(b)(2)(xviii)(A)

Appendix VIII qualification held for the wrong Supplement or the wrong configuration — single-sided access claimed on austenitic or dissimilar metal welds without a successful single-sided demonstration
Annual hands-on training on cracked specimens performed more than six months before the outage examinations, so the currency requirement is not met when the work is done
Procedure essential variables in the field differing from those demonstrated — probe, frequency, scan plan or software version not matching the qualified configuration
ISI programme still running the previous interval's Code edition after a new 120-month interval started
