Personnel qualified under an earlier standard and never transitioned to the edition of CP-189 or SNT-TC-1A referenced in IWA-1600 for the Code of record
VT-1 and VT-3 examiners qualified under generic visual training with no demonstration of proficiency by examination
Examination records inadequate to support the Owner's Activity Report, or submitted outside the 120-day window after the refuelling outage
sources: 10 CFR 50.55a, full text from the GPO govinfo CFR annual edition, Title 10 Volume 1, revised as of 1 January 2024 — paragraph (a)(1)(ii)(C) listing Section XI Division 1 editions incorporated by reference through the 2019 Edition; (b)(2)(xii) permitting NQA-1 editions specified in Table IWA-1600-1 alongside the licensee's Appendix B programme; (b)(2)(xiv) requiring 8 hours of annual hands-on training on cracked specimens or the Appendix VII VII-4240 annual practice, completed no earlier than 6 months before performing UT; (b)(2)(xv) Appendix VIII specimen set and Supplement conditions; (b)(2)(xviii)(A) requiring Level I and II NDE recertification on a 3-year interval in lieu of the 5-year interval in IWA-2314(a) and (b); (g)(4) successive 120-month inspection intervals updated to the edition incorporated 18 months before the interval starts; and the IWA-6230 Owner's Activity Report submission within 120 calendar days of each refuelling outage. ASME's own standard page for BPVC Section XI Division 1, 2025 Edition, 'Rules for Inservice Inspection of Nuclear Reactor Facility Components,' confirming the Authorized Nuclear Inservice Inspector role. IWA-2300 personnel provisions, employer sole responsibility for certification and permitted use of outside agencies, and the CP-189 reference in IWA-1600, corroborated against the World Nuclear Association CORDEL report 'Certification of NDE Personnel — Harmonization of International Code Requirements.' PDI ownership by utilities and operation by EPRI corroborated against NRC and PNNL assessment material. Accessed 21 Aug 2026.

name: IACS Unified Requirement Z17 — Procedural Requirements for Service Suppliers
authority: International Association of Classification Societies (IACS); applied and enforced by each IACS Member class society
appliesTo: Firms not employed by a classification society whose measurement, test or maintenance results a class surveyor relies on when making decisions affecting classification or statutory certification. For NDT businesses the binding categories are thickness measurement on ships and mobile offshore units (excluding non-ESP ships under 500 gross tonnage and all fishing vessels), in-water survey by diver or ROV, ultrasonic tightness testing of closing appliances, remote inspection techniques, and tightness testing of membrane gas carrier barriers.
summary: UR Z17 sets the minimum requirements every IACS member society applies before it will accept a service supplier's results. The firm — not the individual technician — is approved. It must submit a company outline, personnel and equipment records, work procedures, training programmes, report formats and a quality manual; pass a document review; pass an on-site audit; and pass a practical demonstration of the actual service. Approval is granted per service category and per station: where a company owns several servicing stations, each is assessed and approved separately. Subcontractors performing the approved service must themselves meet Section 5. Every report issued must include a copy of the Certificate of Approval.
personnelCertification: Employer-based, with a third-party overlay. Under 5.2.2 the supplier itself qualifies and trains its personnel to a recognised national, international or industry standard; operators need at least one year of tutored on-the-job training and supervisors at least two years' experience as an operator. For thickness measurement, Annex 1 gives EN 473 or ISO 9712 Level II for the supervisor and Level I for operators as examples of an acceptable standard. Annex 1 Section 15 names ASNT SNT-TC-1A explicitly alongside ISO 9712, but requires SNT-TC-1A holders to evidence that training was administered by an independent training body centrally certified to ASNT. An outsourced Level III can author and approve procedures and act as technical authority, but cannot replace the operator and supervisor certificates the audit inspects.
requiredDocuments: Outline of company — organisation and management structure, including subsidiaries to be covered by the approval
List of nominated agents, subsidiaries and subcontractors
List of operators/technicians/inspectors documenting training, experience and qualifications to recognised national, international or industry standards
Description of the equipment used for the service, plus a guide for operators of that equipment
Training programmes for operators/technicians/inspectors
Check lists and record formats for recording the results of the services referred to in Annex 1
Quality Manual and/or documented procedures covering the items listed in 5.5
Documented procedures for communication with the crew before commencing work, so equipment can be safely decommissioned
Record of customer claims and of corrective actions requested by certification bodies
Operators' documented acknowledgement of the code of conduct
auditProcess: Application to an IACS member society for a named service category listed in Annex 1
Document review of the 5.1.1 submission — quality manual, work procedures, personnel and equipment records
On-site audit under 5.3 to confirm the firm is organised and managed in accordance with the submitted documents and is capable of the service
Practical demonstration of the specific service under 5.4, with satisfactory reporting; at renewal this may be verified by documentary review of jobs already accepted by a QSCS-verified society
Issue of a Certificate of Approval under 6.1 stating the type and scope of services and any limitations or restrictions
Renewal or endorsement audit under 6.2; any alteration to the certified service operating system must be reported immediately (Section 7)
renewal: Renewal or endorsement of the Certificate of Approval at intervals not exceeding five years by verification audit (6.2), or on expiry of the supplier's manufacturer approval where that applies, whichever comes first. For firms engaged in thickness measurements the interval must not exceed three years. Individual societies may impose shorter intervals and intermediate audits; failure to undergo a required intermediate audit is listed as grounds for cancellation under 8.2.4.
commonFindings: Operator or supervisor certificates on file do not cover the method or level the relevant Annex 1 category requires
No evidence of the minimum one year of tutored on-the-job training for operators required by 5.2.2
Equipment records missing maintenance history or the results of calibration and verification (5.2.5)
Reports issued without a copy of the Certificate of Approval attached, which 5.2.11 requires
Subcontractors used on approved work with no evidence they meet the requirements of Section 5 (5.2.9)
Thickness measurement or reporting software not documented and confirmed as fit for the intended application before first use (5.2.6)
Alterations to the certified service operating system — new offices, new operators, revised procedures — not notified to the society (Section 7)
A second servicing station operating under the parent certificate without having been separately assessed and approved (5.2.7)
sources: IACS UR Z17 Rev.21, January 2025 — full 41-page text (Sections 1–9 plus Annex 1) read clause by clause from the ClassNK-hosted copy of the IACS requirement. The revision history in that text records Rev.19 and Rev.20 for uniform implementation by IACS Societies from 1 January 2026 and Rev.21 from 1 July 2026. Verified August 2026.

name: American Bureau of Shipping Service Supplier Recognition Program (formerly External Specialist Certification)
jurisdiction: United States — ABS, a US classification society; the programme operates worldwide
authority: American Bureau of Shipping (ABS); certification issued exclusively by ABS
appliesTo: Service providers seeking ABS recognition in one of three families: regulatory and statutory services aligned with IACS UR Z17; services required by ABS Rules and Guides, which explicitly include nondestructive test, nondestructive inspection and nondestructive evaluation; and miscellaneous programmes such as testing laboratories, inspection and maintenance services and asset layup. It binds the company and the named service scope, not individual technicians.
summary: ABS recognizes service suppliers so that its surveyors can accept their results. It is a company-level certification: ABS performs a technical documentation review, a facility and quality system assessment, verification of personnel qualifications, and a performance evaluation through practical demonstration, then issues a Recognition Certificate and lists the firm in the ABS Global Service Supplier Database with its scope, certificate validity and assigned ABS port office. The commercially distinctive point is that ABS recognizes NDT/NDI/NDE as an ABS Rule-required service in its own right — a separate entry point from hull gauging for an inspection company doing weld examination on ABS-classed newbuilds and repairs.
personnelCertification: Employer-based certification is accepted; ABS verifies certificates rather than issuing them, and personnel qualification verification is a formal step of the approval. ABS's own nondestructive inspection guidance sets the authority split an auditor tests against: procedures and techniques are to be established and approved by personnel certified to NDT Level 3 in the applicable method; inspection may be performed by certified Level 1, 2 or 3 personnel; interpretation and evaluation of results must be performed by Level 2 or 3. It references ISO 9712 and recognized international or national certifying programs as the qualification basis. An outsourced Level III can therefore write and sign the firm's NDT procedures and techniques.
requiredDocuments: Completed ABS Service Supplier online request form identifying every service type sought
Quality manual and documented work procedures covering each service type applied for
Personnel list with certificates, training records and documented experience for every operator and supervisor
NDT procedures and techniques signed by a Level 3 in the applicable method, for the NDT/NDI/NDE service type
Equipment list with maintenance, calibration and verification records
Report formats and check lists used to record the results of the service
Evidence of approval, recognition or accreditation held from other bodies
Records of customer complaints and of corrective actions taken
Information on other activities that could present a conflict of interest
auditProcess: Submit the online request form to ABS for the named service types
Documentation review by ABS of the quality system, procedures and personnel records
Facility audit, including assessment of the quality system and verification of personnel qualifications
Practical demonstration of the specific service, witnessed by ABS
Satisfactory performance and reporting confirmed, then issue of the Recognition Certificate and listing in the ABS Global Service Supplier Database
methodsInScope: UT (hull gauging and ultrasonic thickness measurement)
Remote inspection techniques (drones, ROVs, robotic crawlers)
industries: Equipment manufacture and pressure vessel fabrication
renewal: ABS's published service supplier material states the Recognition Certificate is valid for five years. Certain service types are marked as subject to annual audits — ABS CyberSafety services, integrated software quality management, pressure vessel manufacturers and smart functions. Where the service falls in the Regulatory and Statutory (IACS UR Z17) family, the underlying Unified Requirement caps renewal for thickness measurement firms at three years, so hull gauging approvals run on a shorter clock than the general five-year figure.
commonFindings: NDT procedures in use were never approved and signed by a Level 3 certified in that method
Interpretation and evaluation of indications performed or signed off by Level 1 personnel
Personnel certificates present but not traceable to a written practice or a recognized certifying program
Scope creep — services performed that are outside the service types written on the Recognition Certificate
Practical demonstration deferred, so the certificate scope was never fully activated for one of the applied-for services
Equipment calibration records incomplete, or no assessment of prior results when equipment was found out of tolerance
Subsidiary or branch office operating under the head office certificate without having been assessed
Conflict-of-interest information not disclosed where the firm also performs repair work on assets it inspects
sources: ABS Service Supplier programme page at ww2.eagle.org (full service type list, three service families, five-step approval process, annual-audit markers) and the ABS Service Supplier Cutsheet, © 2026 American Bureau of Shipping (five-year Recognition Certificate, programme steps, service categories, contact servicesuppliers@eagle.org) — both retrieved August 2026. Level 1/2/3 authority split taken from the ABS Guide for Nondestructive Inspection of Hull Welds, Section 1 Personnel and Section 1/7 Procedures and Techniques (2004-marked revisions in the ABS-hosted edition read); ABS has issued later editions of that Guide which were not read.

name: DNV Approval of Service Suppliers (AoSS)
jurisdiction: International — DNV AS (Norway), applied worldwide to DNV-classed assets
authority: DNV AS (DNV Maritime), Høvik, Norway; certificates issued by DNV surveyors
appliesTo: Firms whose results DNV surveyors rely on. DNV lists roughly 23 service categories; those that bind inspection companies are ultrasonic thickness measurement of ship structures, non-destructive testing for offshore projects and offshore units or components, and in-water survey of ships. Approval attaches to the legal entity for a named service and category, and covers only the subsidiary offices and the individually named personnel written into the certificate and its appendix.
summary: DNV's scheme issues an Approval of Service Suppliers certificate on form code AOSS 101, carrying an AOSS-format certificate number, a revision number, the service granted, the class programme it was granted under, and a category. Thickness measurement certificates are issued in accordance with Class Programme DNV-CP-0620 and typically carry Category I, authorising measurement on all types and sizes of ships; the certificate states it will be accepted for use with all rule sets published by DNV. Non-destructive testing on offshore projects and offshore units or components is granted under Class Programmes DNV-CP-0484 and DNV-CP-0640. Certificates list four explicit grounds for withdrawal.
personnelCertification: Employer-based ASNT certification is accepted in practice for ship thickness measurement: DNV certificates issued under DNV-CP-0620 name authorised personnel individually in an appendix under the heading "Operator ASNT Level", recording each as Level II and flagging those additionally designated Supervisor. Because the individuals appear on the class certificate, adding or losing a technician is a certificate revision, not an internal HR matter — the certificate itself states that any alteration to the certified service operation system, including changes to UTM operators, must be reported to DNV immediately. The offshore NDT class programmes test that the supplier uses appropriate procedures and holds qualified and certified personnel governed by a written practice; an outsourced Level III can own that written practice and the procedures.
requiredDocuments: Application submitted through DNV's class portal against the applicable Class Programme
Quality system documentation and documented work procedures for the service applied for
List of supervisors and operators with certificates and levels, for entry into the certificate appendix
List of subsidiary offices to be covered, for entry into the certificate appendix
Equipment list with calibration and maintenance records
NDT written practice covering training, experience, examination, certification, performance, control, verification and reporting (offshore NDT scope)
Report formats, and for UTM the reporting output DNV's Pegasus tool requires
Notification records for any alteration to the certified service operation system
auditProcess: Register and apply through DNV's class portal, selecting the applicable Class Programme
DNV reviews the submitted quality system, procedures, personnel and equipment documentation
On-site audit of the firm and its named offices
Practical demonstration of the service, witnessed by a DNV surveyor
Issue of the Approval of Service Suppliers certificate (form AOSS 101) with category, class programme reference and an appendix naming subsidiary offices and authorised personnel
Renewal audit before expiry; interim certificate revisions issued as personnel or offices change
methodsInScope: UT (ultrasonic thickness measurement of ship structures)
UT and advanced UT for offshore components
industries: Tankers, bulk carriers and gas carriers
renewal: Approval of Service Suppliers certificates for thickness measurement observed in the field run three years from issue — for example one valid 2022-04-27 to 2025-04-26 and another 2023-03-25 to 2026-03-24 — consistent with the three-year cap IACS UR Z17 places on thickness measurement firms. Certificates are re-issued at higher revision numbers between renewals when personnel or offices change. DNV lists four grounds for withdrawal on the certificate face: improperly carried out or improperly reported service, deficiencies found by the surveyor in the accepted operating system, failure to inform DNV of major changes affecting service quality, and changed or unfulfilled certificate conditions.
commonFindings: A technician performing UTM whose name is not on the certificate appendix, because a certificate revision was never requested
UTM reports not produced through DNV's mandated Pegasus reporting tool for fleet-in-service vessels
Work performed from an office not listed among the subsidiary offices on the certificate
Measurement performed outside the granted category or outside the class programme scope on the certificate
Supervisor designation on the certificate not matched by evidence of the required additional experience
Calibration and verification records for thickness gauges incomplete or missing the reference block used
Changes to the quality system or work procedures made without notifying DNV
Offshore NDT written practice does not actually cover all of training, examination, certification, verification and reporting
sources: Three DNV-issued Approval of Service Suppliers certificates read in full: certificate AOSS0000ANW (Lloyd Werft Bremerhaven, thickness measurements on ships and mobile offshore units, Class Programme DNVGL-CP-0484, valid 2022-04-27 to 2025-04-26, form AOSS 101 rev 2021-03); certificate AOSS0000GND (International Inspection LLC, Seatac USA, thickness measurements, Class Programme DNV-CP-0620, valid 2023-03-25 to 2026-03-24, with appendix listing subsidiary offices and 17 named operators by ASNT level); certificate AOSS0000M2J (Check Your Ship OÜ, thickness measurements, DNV-CP-0620, issued 2025-12-16, form AOSS 101 rev 2024-10). DNV-CP-0484 and DNV-CP-0640 confirmed as the offshore NDT class programmes via DNV's own service pages and a supplier's published DNV approval announcement. DNV's UTM page confirms Pegasus as the mandatory UTM reporting tool for fleet-in-service vessels from 1 July 2017. The full text of DNV-CP-0620, DNV-CP-0484 and DNV-CP-0640 sits behind DNV's rules portal and was not read. Verified August 2026.

name: NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, Revision 1 — Requirements for Nondestructive Testing Methods
authority: Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA); enforced in the field by the cognizant Government inspector — the Supervisor of Shipbuilding at a commercial shipyard, the Shipyard Commander at a government yard
appliesTo: Any activity performing NDT under a NAVSEA contract or on Navy ships and systems — government and commercial shipyards, regional maintenance centres, trident refit facilities, intermediate maintenance activities and their NDT subcontractors. "Activity" is defined as all sites of an organisation under the same quality assurance management using the same quality assurance plan, which is what determines how many written practices and Examiner appointments a multi-site inspection company actually needs.
summary: The document usually spoken of as "NAVSEA T9074" is not a single publication — T9074 is a series prefix. The NDT requirement is NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, Revision 1, dated 11 September 2014, Requirements for Nondestructive Testing Methods, which supersedes the 30 April 1997 original and its Advanced Change Notice 1 of 16 February 1999. It sets the minimum requirements to qualify NDT personnel, procedures and equipment, and covers radiographic, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant, ultrasonic, eddy current and visual testing in separate chapters. Its distinguishing feature for a service provider is that it converts ASNT SNT-TC-1A from a recommended practice into mandatory minimums, then layers Navy-specific controls on top.
personnelCertification: Employer-based and deliberately non-portable. Personnel are certified under the activity's own written practice, developed as required by ASNT SNT-TC-1A, which the publication invokes as mandatory minimum requirements and states shall not be considered recommendations or guidelines. The Level III is called the NDT Examiner: the activity delegates to that individual the responsibility and authority to examine and certify its NDT personnel and to approve NDT procedures and workmanship standards, so an outsourced Level III can hold the role. The catch sits in 1.6.2.1 — the Examiner's specific examination must be prepared, approved and administered by the employing activity, independent of the Examiner being tested. Transfer of NDT certifications between activities is prohibited except as authorised by NAVSEA.
requiredDocuments: The activity's written practice for NDT personnel training, examination and certification, provided to the Government inspector on request
A written NDT procedure for each method performed, carrying a certification statement signed by the cognizant Examiner
Procedure qualification data showing that known natural or artificial discontinuities near the accept/reject threshold can be reliably detected and evaluated
Records of qualification training and experience obtained before initial certification, retained as long as personnel remain certified
Results of all current examinations, correlatable to the examination administered, plus a master copy of each examination
Vision test records noting corrective aids, retained for the current and preceding certification period
Certification statements signed by the activity's NDT Examiner for Operators and Inspectors, and by an employer representative for Examiners
Annual oversight records — witnessed in-process inspections, reinspections of previously inspected product, or technical performance evaluations
auditProcess: Contract or NAVSEA Standard Item invokes T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 on the work package
Activity writes or updates its written practice to SNT-TC-1A as modified by the publication, and delegates the Level III NDT Examiner role

Examiner is examined — basic and method examinations administered by the employing activity, ASNT or another outside agency, plus a specific examination the activity prepares, approves and administers independently of him
Examiner certifies Operators and Inspectors, writes and signs the NDT procedures, and qualifies each procedure by demonstration on known discontinuities
Government inspector reviews the written practice, procedures and personnel records on request, and may require a demonstration of the procedure at any time
Annual oversight by the Examiner, with a technical performance evaluation performed before the end of the second year of the certification cycle
industries: Commercial shipyards under Supervisor of Shipbuilding oversight
Regional maintenance centres and intermediate maintenance activities
Naval machinery, piping and pressure vessel fabrication
renewal: NDT Operators and Inspectors are recertified by examination at intervals not greater than three years; Examiners at intervals not greater than five years. A certification is considered expired on the last day of the month in which recertification is due. Recertification by evidence of continuing satisfactory technical performance, or on the basis of ASNT certifications granted without examination, is not permitted. Operators and Inspectors who have not satisfied the annual oversight requirement must be re-examined by an approved practical examination administered by the activity's Examiner. Vision tests are annual, or sooner after eye surgery or other conditions affecting vision.
commonFindings: Written practice reproduces SNT-TC-1A verbatim without adopting the modifications the publication imposes, so training hours or examination content fall short of the mandatory minimums
The Examiner's specific examination was prepared or administered by the Examiner himself rather than independently by the employing activity
Recertification granted on continuing satisfactory performance, or on an ASNT certification issued without examination — both expressly prohibited
No documented annual oversight, or no technical performance evaluation before the end of the second year of the certification cycle
Vision test lapsed; the requirement is annual and expires on the last day of the month in which retesting is due
NDT procedure missing the Examiner's signed certification statement, or holding no procedure qualification demonstration data
Certifications carried across from a previous employer, which the publication prohibits without NAVSEA authorisation
Limited certifications used without the limitation being described in both the written practice and the certification records
sources: NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, Revision 1, 11 September 2014, 116 pages, Distribution Statement A (approved for public release, distribution unlimited) — Chapter 1 (Scope; 1.5 definitions; 1.6 nondestructive test personnel certification; 1.7 procedure qualification and approval) and Chapter 2 (Applicable Documents) read in full. Related documents cited within it include MIL-STD-2132, NAVSEA S9074-AR-GIB-010/278 and NAVSEA S9086-CH-STM-020 Chapter 074 Volume 2. Revision 1 is the revision attached to current Navy solicitations; no Revision 2 was found. Verified August 2026.

name: AAR Manual of Standards and Recommended Practices, Section J — Specification M-1003, Specification for Quality Assurance
jurisdiction: North America (United States, Canada and Mexico railway interchange service)
authority: Association of American Railroads (AAR), through its Quality Assurance Committee; the programme is managed and operated by AAR's wholly owned subsidiary MxV Rail using AAR Accredited Auditors
appliesTo: Facilities supplying materials, products or services for North American railway interchange service whose activity appears in Appendix A of MSRP Section J — including wheel and axle shops, tank car maintenance and modification facilities, heavy repair shops and repair tracks, and manufacturers of wheels, axles, couplers, yokes and freight cars. Certification attaches to the individual facility and to specific activity codes, not to the corporate entity.
summary: M-1003 is a quality assurance certification for the shop, not an NDT credential. It requires the facility to implement a documented quality assurance programme meeting the twenty-four elements of Chapter 2 and to be audited against them on a three-year cycle. NDT enters through Element 2.15, Process Control, which requires special processes to be performed in accordance with applicable codes, standards, specifications and governmental and contractual requirements by qualified personnel using qualified equipment and procedures; and through Element 2.22, Training, which requires special-process personnel to hold both training and applicable work experience. Where no code covers a special process, the facility must define the necessary qualifications itself.
personnelCertification: Employer-based, and unusually open. M-1003 does not name ASNT SNT-TC-1A, ANSI/ASNT CP-189 or ISO 9712. It requires that special processes be performed by qualified personnel using qualified equipment and procedures in accordance with whatever code, standard or specification actually applies to the product — which for tank cars, wheels and axles is set by AAR technical manuals and federal rules, not by M-1003 itself. Where quality requirements exceed established codes, the facility must describe the necessary qualifications of personnel, procedures and equipment in its own programme, and prove them at audit through training records held as long as the person remains qualified. An outsourced Level III can supply that qualification basis, write the procedures and certify the technicians.
requiredDocuments: Quality Assurance Manual
Completed Quality Assurance Program Evaluation (QAPE) checklist, identifying the corresponding line item of the facility's programme against each requirement in M-1003 Chapter 2
Production, inspection and test plan (Element 2.5), identifying every inspection and test point, the characteristics inspected and the acceptance criteria
Special process procedures with the personnel, equipment and procedure qualifications required by paragraph 2.15.1.10
Training records for qualified personnel, retained as long as they remain qualified or as otherwise specified
Calibration records for measuring and testing equipment, including calibration date and interval, with unique identification and calibration status labelling (Element 2.8)
Chapter 7 material nonconformance records on Forms QA-7.1, QA-7.2 and QA-7.3, retained three years
Evidence of a current subscription to AAR Circular Letters and of holding the latest revision of MSRP Section J
Internal quality audit records (Element 2.21)
auditProcess: Online application at aar.iirx.net under the Facility Certifications tab, uploading the documentation required by MSRP Section J paragraph 3.3.2
Quality Manual and completed QAPE checklist submitted to the assigned AAR Accredited Auditor approximately 60 days before the scheduled audit
Auditor reviews the manual and QAPE against M-1003 Chapter 2
On-site initial certification audit covering all twenty-four Chapter 2 elements
Findings closed through the five-step problem solving / root cause and corrective action process
Quality Assurance Committee vote, then entry in the AAR Registry of M-1003 Certified Facilities with a QA Code and the specific activity codes granted
Minimum two annual compliance audits of six to eight elements each, then a recertification audit at the end of the third year
industries: Tank car manufacture, maintenance and modification
Railcar repair shops and repair tracks
renewal: Each M-1003 certification runs three years, subject to annual compliance audits: after initial certification there is a minimum of two annual compliance audits followed by a recertification audit at the end of the third year. Initial and recertification audits cover all twenty-four Chapter 2 elements; compliance audits cover six to eight, always including the four the Quality Assurance Committee mandates for that year (2.5, 2.6, 2.11 and 2.12 for 2026; 2.5, 2.7, 2.8 and 2.21 for 2024). AAR states approximate audit costs for North American facilities of between $6,000 and $12,000 for certification and recertification audits and between $4,000 and $8,000 for compliance audits, with exact fees published in Appendix E of the AAR Office Manual. Time from completed application to initial certification varies from four to nine months.
commonFindings: QAPE checklist does not identify a specific line item of the facility's own programme against each Chapter 2 requirement
Special process personnel qualified on training alone, with no evidence of the applicable work experience Element 2.22 also requires
NDT or welding personnel, procedures and equipment not shown to be qualified as paragraph 2.15.1.10 requires
Measuring and testing equipment found out of calibration with no documented assessment of the validity of previous inspection and test results
No current subscription to AAR Circular Letters, or the facility working to a superseded revision of MSRP Section J
Chapter 7 forms QA-7.1, QA-7.2 and QA-7.3 misused, or nonconformance records not retained for three years
Activities performed on the floor that do not match exactly the activity codes listed for the facility in the AAR Registry
Corrective actions closed with retraining or reinstructing the craftsman, which the AAR audit handbook states is not corrective action
sources: AAR M-1003 Quality Assurance Audit Handbook 2026, Revision F, revised April 2026 (public version) and Revision C, revised January 2024 (public version), both published by AAR — read in full for programme management, audit criteria selection, mandatory elements, RCCA process, nonconformance reporting and fees. AAR M-1003 Frequently Asked Questions at aar.com/standards/FAQ.php (application route, four-to-nine-month timeline, fee ranges, three-year cycle, twenty-four elements, auditor and QAPE requirements). MSRP Section J Appendix A Activity Code Guide dated 27 January 2026 (activity codes and technical approval requirements). Quality Assurance Program Evaluation (QAPE) Checklist, Rev 02/01/2026 (element titles and the special process and training question set). All retrieved August 2026. The M-1003 specification text itself is a paid AAR publication and was not read in full; element titles were reconstructed from the QAPE checklist.

name: 29 CFR Part 1915 — Occupational Safety and Health Standards for Shipyard Employment
jurisdiction: United States (federal OSHA; State Plan states adopt standards at least as effective)
authority: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), US Department of Labor; State Plan agencies in states operating their own programmes
appliesTo: Employers whose workers perform ship repair, shipbuilding, shipbreaking and related employment on the navigable waters of the United States, including work aboard vessels, in drydock and in adjacent land-side areas. An NDT contractor entering a shipyard is a covered employer in its own right for its own crew, independently of the host yard's programme, and is cited independently for its own employees' exposure.
summary: Part 1915 is the safety regime an inspection crew actually works under inside a shipyard, and it is the one most likely to stop a job. Subpart B governs confined and enclosed spaces: before entry the space must be visually inspected and tested by a competent person, in the order oxygen content, then flammability, then toxicity. Subpart A section 1915.7 defines the competent person and the records that person must keep. Hot work in or adjacent to spaces that contain or last contained fuel or flammable liquids needs a Marine Chemist or Coast Guard authorized person certificate. Subpart I covers PPE and respiratory protection, Subpart P fire protection, and Subpart Z the exposure limits tank and hull work generates.
personnelCertification: There is no NDT certification scheme here at all, and that is the confusion this regime creates. Part 1915 turns on the employer's own designation of a competent person, who under 1915.7(c) must understand and carry out instructions left by Marine Chemists, Coast Guard authorized persons and Certified Industrial Hygienists; know subparts B, C, D and H; calibrate and use oxygen, combustible gas, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide indicators and interpret the results accurately; perform the required tests and inspections; judge when further testing by a Marine Chemist or Certified Industrial Hygienist is needed; and maintain the section's records. An outsourced Level III has no standing under Part 1915 unless the employer designates them and they meet 1915.7(c) in full.
requiredDocuments: Competent person records under 1915.7(d): location, time, date, location of the inspected spaces, the operations performed, test results and any instructions — posted near the space and retained at least three months after the job is completed
Marine Chemist certificate or Coast Guard authorized person certificate where hot work falls under 1915.14(a)
Written certification of confined space training under 1915.12(d)(5), giving the employee's name, the name of the certifier and the date(s)
Calibration records for oxygen, combustible gas, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide indicators
Written respiratory protection programme, medical evaluations and fit-test records (1915.154)
Hazard communication programme and safety data sheets (1915.1200)

Exposure monitoring and medical surveillance records under the applicable Subpart Z substance standards — lead (1915.1025), chromium (VI) (1915.1026), respirable crystalline silica (1915.1053), asbestos (1915.1001)
Personal fall arrest system inspection and training records (1915.159)
auditProcess: OSHA compliance officer arrives on a programmed inspection, complaint, referral or accident report
Opening conference; the employer's Part 1915 programme documents and competent person records are requested
Walkaround, including observation of entry testing, instrument calibration checks and employee interviews
Closing conference; citations issued with proposed penalties and abatement dates
Abatement certification submitted, or the citation contested within the statutory period
renewal: No certificate and no renewal. The obligations are continuous: atmospheric testing before each entry and as often as necessary to ensure conditions are maintained, training and retraining as the employer's programme requires, and retention of competent person records for at least three months after completion of the job. Marine Chemist certificates are job- and condition-specific rather than periodic. OSHA's published maximum civil penalties, stated on osha.gov/penalties as the amounts assessable after 15 January 2026, are $16,550 per serious, other-than-serious or posting violation, $16,550 per day beyond the abatement date for failure to abate, and $165,514 per willful or repeated violation.
commonFindings: Atmospheric testing performed out of order — flammability or toxicity checked before oxygen content, which 1915.12 sequences explicitly
A competent person designated on paper who cannot demonstrate calibration and correct use of the instrument actually in the space
Entry made outside the 19.5 to 22.0 percent oxygen band without meeting the narrow emergency rescue or short-duration exception, which requires continuous monitoring
Hot work performed within, on or immediately adjacent to fuel tanks without a Marine Chemist or Coast Guard authorized person certificate
Competent person records not posted near the space, or discarded before three months after the job finished
No written certification of confined space training naming the employee, the certifier and the date
Respirators issued and used without a written programme, medical evaluation or fit test
Subcontracted NDT crew relying entirely on the host yard's competent person with no designation of its own
Lead or chromium (VI) exposure from grinding and surface preparation ahead of MT or PT not assessed against the Subpart Z substance standards
sources: 29 CFR Part 1915 as published on osha.gov, retrieved August 2026 — Subpart A–P index; §1915.7 Competent person (paragraphs (c)(1)–(c)(7) and (d)); §1915.12 Precautions and the order of testing before entering confined and enclosed spaces and other dangerous atmospheres (oxygen 19.5–22.0 percent, flammable vapours below 10 percent of the lower explosive limit, toxicity and the training certification at (d)(5)); §1915.14 Hot work; §1915.1000 Air contaminants; and the complete Subpart Z section index. Penalty amounts from osha.gov/penalties. Verified fact worth noting: Part 1915 Subpart Z contains no ionizing radiation section and does not incorporate 29 CFR 1910.1096, so radiographic source control for shipyard RT rests on the firm's NRC or Agreement State radioactive materials licence rather than on Part 1915.

name: AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2025, Structural Welding Code — Steel
jurisdiction: United States, and internationally wherever adopted by contract
authority: American Welding Society (AWS), D1 Committee on Structural Welding; an ANSI-approved American National Standard. Welding inspector certification is administered by the AWS Certification Committee under AWS QC1. Enforcement is by the Engineer and Owner through the contract documents, and carries statutory force wherever a governmental body incorporates the code into law or regulation.
appliesTo: Contractors, fabricators and inspection firms working to AWS D1.1 on welded structures made from the commonly used carbon and low-alloy constructional steels — structural steel buildings, plate girders, tubular structures, stud welding, and strengthening and repair of existing structures. It binds whoever the contract documents make responsible for inspection, which in practice splits between the Contractor's Inspector and the Owner's Verification Inspector.
summary: D1.1 is a code, not a certification scheme — nobody issues a D1.1 certificate to a company. What it does is dictate who may inspect, how NDT must be procedured, and what constitutes acceptance. Clause 8 is the inspection clause and runs in seven parts: general requirements, contractor obligations, acceptance criteria, NDT procedures, radiographic testing, ultrasonic testing of groove welds, and other examination methods including radiation imaging systems and advanced ultrasonic systems. The 2025 edition rewrote how NDT personnel certification is established, added definitions splitting MT and PT indications into linear and rounded, and updated the Table 8.1 visual acceptance criteria for undercut and piping porosity.
personnelCertification: Explicitly dual-track since the 2025 edition. Subclause 8.14.6, Personnel NDT Certification, now carries subclauses: 8.14.6.2, Employer-Based Certification, allows NDT personnel to be certified in accordance with the employer's written practice by ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189; 8.14.6.3, Internationally Recognized Third-Party Certification, allows certification by ANSI/ASNT CP-9712, CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or ISO 9712. Employer-based certification is therefore squarely accepted, and an outsourced Level III can own the written practice and certify the technicians. Clause 10.29.1 goes further for tubular work: UT of T-, Y- and K-connections shall be performed to a written procedure prepared by an NDT Level III, with Level III certification obtainable through SNT-TC-1A and CP-189.
requiredDocuments: Employer's written practice for NDT personnel qualification and certification, per ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189 (8.14.6.2)
NDT personnel certification records, or current ANSI/ASNT CP-9712, CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or ISO 9712 certificates where the third-party route is used (8.14.6.3)
Written NDT procedures for each method used (Clause 8, Part D)
UT procedure for tubular T-, Y- and K-connections prepared by an NDT Level III (10.29.1)
Inspector qualification records for both the Contractor's Inspector and the Verification Inspector (Clause 8, Part A)
Radiographs together with their examination, report and disposition records (8.18)
Ultrasonic test reports (8.26) and dB accuracy certification records (8.31)
UT equipment qualification and calibration records against IIW-type or other approved reference blocks (8.23, 8.24, 8.27)
Visual inspection records evaluated against the Table 8.1 acceptance criteria
Engineer's written approval where alternate acceptance criteria are used (8.8)
auditProcess: Contract documents invoke AWS D1.1 and specify the extent, category and timing of NDT (8.15)
Contractor establishes inspector qualification under Clause 8 Part A and NDT personnel certification under 8.14.6, by the employer-based or third-party route
An NDT Level III writes and approves the NDT procedures, including the UT procedure for tubular T-, Y- and K-connections that 10.29.1 requires
Contractor's Inspector performs the inspection; the Owner's Verification Inspector checks the same work against the same clause
Results reported per the examination, report and disposition subclauses for each method and evaluated against Table 8.1 and the Clause 8 Part C acceptance criteria
Engineer approves any alternate acceptance criteria under 8.8 before they are applied
methodsInScope: Advanced ultrasonic systems including phased array (8.34)
renewal: The code is reissued on roughly a five-year cycle: D1.1/D1.1M:2025 is the 25th edition, approved by ANSI on 19 March 2025 and revising D1.1/D1.1M:2020; the currently published designation is D1.1/D1.1M:2025-AMD1. Personnel credentials renew on their own clocks. Under AWS QC1, welding inspector certification is valid for three years; renewals are limited to two consecutive three-year periods, and before the end of the ninth year from initial certification the inspector must recertify — by examination, by a Committee-approved endorsement, or by experience and continuing education. A CAWI is not eligible for renewal and may hold that certification for up to three years only. Visual acuity examinations must be performed no more than one year before the examination date or the expiry date for renewals and recertifications.
commonFindings: No written practice on file where NDT personnel are certified under the employer-based route of 8.14.6.2
UT operators certified to a general NDT scheme with no evidence of the supplementary examination on the code's own UT provisions
The Level III who signed the UT procedure for tubular T-, Y- and K-connections is not certified in that method, contrary to 10.29.1
MT and PT indications recorded and dispositioned without applying the linear and rounded definitions introduced in 8.10.1
Visual acceptance judged against the previous edition's Table 8.1, missing the revised undercut limits for welds under 12 in. and the new piping porosity limits
Verification Inspector qualification records absent, or one individual acting as both Contractor's and Verification Inspector
Radiographs not retained or dispositioned as 8.18 requires
UT equipment qualification and dB accuracy certification records not maintained
CWI working on an expired card, or past the two-renewal limit without having completed nine-year recertification
sources: AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2025, Structural Welding Code — Steel, 25th edition, ANSI-approved 19 March 2025, revising D1.1/D1.1M:2020 — front matter, Summary of Changes and the complete Clause 8 and Clause 10 tables of contents read from the AWS-published preview at pubs.aws.org. Clause-level detail for 8.10.1, 8.14.6, 8.14.6.2, 8.14.6.3 and 10.29.1 taken verbatim from the AWS Welding Journal article "What's New in AWS D1.1 2025, Structural Welding Code — Steel" published by AWS/FABTECH. Current designation D1.1/D1.1M:2025-AMD1 confirmed on aws.org. AWS QC1:2016, Standard for AWS Certification of Welding Inspectors, read in full (clauses 8.1 visual acuity, 10.1 certification validity, 15 renewals, 16 nine-year recertification). ASNT standard editions confirmed on asnt.org: SNT-TC-1A (2024), ANSI/ASNT CP-189 (2024) and ANSI/ASNT CP-105 (2024) as employer-based, ANSI/ASNT CP-9712 (2023) as the US adoption of ISO 9712:2021 and third-party. Verified August 2026. The full body text of Clause 8 sits behind AWS's paywall and was not read line by line.

name: ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section V — Nondestructive Examination
authority: American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Boiler and Pressure Vessel Standards Committee, Subcommittee on Nondestructive Examination; enforced in practice by the referencing Code Section, the Authorized Inspector, and the state or provincial boiler and pressure vessel jurisdiction that has adopted the BPVC
appliesTo: Any NDE contractor examining pressure-retaining items built or repaired to an ASME construction code — Section I power boilers, Section IV heating boilers, Section VIII pressure vessels, Section XII transport tanks, and B31.1 or B31.3 piping — plus NBIC repair work that reaches Section V through the original code of construction. It binds the shop crew, the field crew and the outsourced NDE laboratory equally. Section V never applies on its own; a referencing Code Section invokes it.
summary: Section V certifies no company and no person. It tells an NDE provider how to run a method, and three obligations follow you into every audit. First, a written procedure for each method and technique, demonstrated capable of producing meaningful results to the satisfaction of the Authorized Inspector — Article 1, T-150. Second, examination equipment calibrated and that calibration recorded and available to the Inspector. Third, certification records for NDE personnel whose required contents are fixed by Article 1, T-190. Personnel qualification itself sits at Article 1, T-120, which routes out to the employer's written practice and to whichever editions of ASNT SNT-TC-1A, ANSI/ASNT CP-189 or ACCP the referencing Code Section accepts. Article numbers and records, not company certificates, are what a supplier audit asks you to produce.
personnelCertification: Employer-based, not central. Section V leaves certification to the employer's written practice, built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, ANSI/ASNT CP-189 or ACCP in the edition the referencing Code Section accepts. Radiographic and ultrasonic examiners must be qualified and certified to that written practice or to a central certification programme; magnetic particle, liquid penetrant and visual examiners may be certified by the Certificate Holder on the basis of proficiency in the techniques employed plus an annual eye examination. The joint National Board and ASME Guide states that the Level III examiner may be an employee of the Certificate Holder or of a subcontractor, and that where he is subcontracted, documented evidence must be on file accepting the subcontractor's Level III examiner as the Certificate Holder's Level III examiner. An outsourced Level III is expressly contemplated by the audit guidance.
requiredDocuments: NDE written practice for the qualification and certification of NDE personnel
Written NDE procedure for each method and technique, with the record of the demonstration witnessed by the Authorized Inspector (Article 1, T-150)
Level III approval signature on each NDE procedure and each revision
NDE personnel certification records containing the items required by Article 1, T-190
Annual near-vision and colour-contrast differentiation eye examination records for examiners
Calibration records for examination and measuring equipment, including densitometer and step-wedge comparison film
Documented acceptance of a subcontracted Level III examiner as the Certificate Holder's Level III examiner
Examination reports, radiographic film or digital images, and interpretation sheets available to the Inspector
Current edition of Section V and of the referencing Code Section held on site
auditProcess: Identify the referencing Code Section — Section I, IV, VIII, XII, B31.1, B31.3 or NBIC Part 3 — because it fixes which Section V Articles apply and which personnel-qualification editions are Code-accepted
Draft the written practice and the method procedures; the Level III reviews and approves them
Demonstrate each procedure capable of producing meaningful results to the satisfaction of the Authorized Inspector, and record the demonstration
Qualify, examine and certify personnel against the written practice; assemble certification records to the contents T-190 requires

Present the programme inside its host review — the ASME/National Board joint review, the client's supplier audit, or the Authorized Inspector's routine surveillance; there is no standalone Section V certificate to apply for
Correct nonconformities and have the Authorized Inspector re-verify before examination results are accepted for Code work
renewal: No certificate and no expiry — Section V is a code, not an accreditation. ASME publishes BPVC editions on a two-year cycle; the 2025 edition follows 2023 and 2021. Written practices and procedures must be re-reviewed against the edition the referencing Code Section and the adopting jurisdiction have accepted, since the Code-accepted editions of SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 and ACCP change between BPVC editions. Personnel recertification intervals are set by the employer's own written practice, not by Section V.
commonFindings: NDE procedure written to an older edition than the one the referencing Code Section adopts
No record of the procedure demonstration the Authorized Inspector is entitled to witness under Article 1, T-150
Personnel certification records missing one or more of the contents required by Article 1, T-190
Subcontracted Level III used with no documented acceptance on file naming him as the Certificate Holder's Level III examiner
Annual eye examinations lapsed for magnetic particle, penetrant and visual examiners
Densitometer and step-wedge comparison film not calibrated as Section V requires
Written practice retains 'should' language where the quality system makes the requirement 'shall'
Level III approval signature missing from a revised procedure that is already in production use
sources: ASME BPVC Section V product page, asme.org, 2025 edition current (BPVC editions listed as 2025, 2023, 2021). The National Board & ASME Guide (nationalboard.org / asme.org), sections 2.11, 3.10 and 6.2.10 — verified for Article 1 T-120 (personnel qualification, cited alongside SNT-TC-1A and AWS QC1), T-150 (procedures demonstrated capable of producing meaningful results to the satisfaction of the Inspector) and T-190 (contents of NDE personnel certification records); for the rule that RT and UT examiners must be certified to the Employer's written practice or a central certification programme; for MT/PT/VT certification on proficiency plus annual eye examination against SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 or ACCP in the current Code-accepted edition; and for the subcontracted Level III acceptance requirement quoted above. Article numbering cross-checked against the API 653 Publications Effectivity Sheet for March–November 2025 exams (Section V Articles 1, 2, 6, 7 and 23/SE-797, ASME BPVC 2023 edition) and the API 570 Body of Knowledge for February/June/October 2026 exams (Articles 1, 2, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 23/SE-797). ASNT SNT-TC-1A 2024 edition with addendum effective May 2025 per ASNT. Accessed 21 August 2026. Specific T-paragraph numbers beyond T-120, T-150 and T-190 were not independently verifiable and are not stated.

name: National Board Inspection Code, NB-23 (NBIC), and the National Board "R" Certificate of Authorization
jurisdiction: United States and Canada — National Board member jurisdictions that have adopted the NBIC
authority: The National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors, 1055 Crupper Avenue, Columbus, Ohio; reviews conducted jointly with the National Board member jurisdiction and the applicant's Authorized Inspection Agency
appliesTo: Organizations that repair or alter boilers, pressure vessels and other pressure-retaining items, whether in a shop, at a temporary location or at a field site, and the NDE laboratories they subcontract to. It also reaches valve repair organizations under the VR certificate and nuclear repair work under the NR certificate. An NDT firm normally encounters it as the subcontracted NDE laboratory whose written practice, procedures and personnel records sit inside the R Certificate Holder's quality management system.
summary: NBIC has four parts — Installation, Inspection, Repairs and Alterations, and Pressure Relief Devices. Part 3 governs repairs and alterations regardless of the original code of construction, and provides alternative methods for examination, testing and heat treatment when the original code's requirements cannot be met. To perform code repairs a firm needs an R Certificate of Authorization: a quality management system meeting NBIC Part 3, Section 1.5; an inspection agreement in force with an Authorized Inspection Agency; and a successful on-site review. For an NDE provider, the practical requirement is that your written practice, method procedures, personnel certification records and calibration records must be available inside the certificate holder's system, because the certificate holder is responsible for all work including subcontracted work.
personnelCertification: Employer-based. NDE procedures and personnel are qualified in accordance with ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or the certificate holder makes arrangements with an outside NDE laboratory to provide the same. Subcontracted NDE is explicitly acceptable and is one of the specialised activities the review guidance expects to see subcontracted; welding is not treated the same way. The R Certificate Holder remains responsible for all work performed, including the subcontractor's. The one role that cannot be outsourced to the shop is the inspection itself: repairs and alterations must be verified by a National Board Commissioned Inspector employed by an Authorized Inspection Agency, commissioned centrally by the National Board under NB-263, RCI-1, Rules for Commissioned Inspectors.
requiredDocuments: NB-12, Application for New Issuance of the National Board "R" Certificate of Authorization
Quality Management System manual addressing every element of NBIC Part 3, Section 1.5
Executed inspection agreement with an Authorized Inspection Agency; the first page is submitted with NB-12
All parts of the latest mandatory edition of the NBIC, plus the code of construction edition and addendum and the referenced standards for materials, welding and nondestructive examination
Welding procedure specifications, procedure qualification records and welder performance qualification records
NDE written practice, method procedures and personnel certification records — in-house or from the subcontracted NDE laboratory
Calibration records for measuring and test equipment
NB-66, R-1 Report of Repair, and NB-229, R-2 Report of Alteration, with the National Board registration record
Qualification Review Report (QRR) from the previous review
auditProcess: Contract an Authorized Inspection Agency; the National Board will not schedule a review without an inspection agreement in force
Write the Quality Management System manual to NBIC Part 3, Section 1.5 and implement it; submit NB-12 with the first page of the AIA contract

Review team assembled — at minimum a representative of the National Board member jurisdiction where the organization is located, or the National Board standing in for it, plus a representative of the AIA in accordance with NB-263, RCI-1
On-site review of the QMS and verification of implementation, demonstrating to the mandatory edition of the NBIC using current work, a demonstration mock-up, or a combination of both
Review team prepares a Qualification Review Report recommending that the certificate be issued, renewed or withheld
Certificate of Authorization and the "R" symbol stamp issued; the holder may then register R-1 and R-2 reports with the National Board
renewal: The Certificate of Authorization expires three years after the date of issuance or renewal. Renewal must be applied for at least six months before expiry, submitted online through the Certificate Administrator account on the National Board Business Center, and a triennial review is conducted. NBIC editions are published every two years; an edition is permissive on its date of issue and becomes mandatory six months later, so an organization may be reviewed against an edition it has not yet been obliged to adopt. The National Board publishes the R certificate fee as $1,150 USD for the three-year term, with a one-time $150 steel stamp loan charge on new issuance; jurisdiction and AIA time for the review is billed separately.
commonFindings: Quality manual still written around "Quality System" and not reconciled with the 2025 edition, which renamed it Quality Management System throughout
Inspection agreement with the AIA lapsed, or not covering the field or temporary-location scope actually being worked
Latest mandatory NBIC edition not held on site, or the code of construction edition and addendum for the item being repaired missing
NDE subcontracted without the subcontractor's written practice, procedures and personnel certification records held in the R Certificate Holder's files
Demonstration mock-up does not exercise the scope printed on the certificate — for example a field scope certified but only shop work demonstrated
R-1 and R-2 forms completed but not registered with the National Board where the original Manufacturer's Data Report was registered there
Renewal application filed inside the six-month window, forcing a gap in certification
Temporary Location used beyond the authorized period or outside the scope listed on the certificate
sources: National Board "R" Certificate of Authorization page, nationalboard.org, accessed 21 August 2026 — verified for the NB-12 application route, the AIA inspection agreement prerequisite, the on-site quality system review, the three-year term, the $1,150 USD certificate fee and the $150 one-time steel stamp loan charge. NB-415, Revision 8, Accreditation of Repair Organizations (nationalboard.org) — verified for the NB-12 and Business Center renewal route, the six-month renewal window, review team composition under NB-263 RCI-1, the demonstration by current work or mock-up, the Qualification Review Report, the three-year expiry, the NBIC Part 3 Section 1.5 QMS requirement, the two-year NBIC edition cycle with mandatory status six months after issue, the Shop/Temporary Location/Field Site definitions, registration of NB-66 (R-1) and NB-229 (R-2), and NBIC Part 3 Supplement 11 for engineered repairs and alterations. National Board "NBIC 2025 Edition Changes" page — verified for the four-part structure, the Quality System to Quality Management System rename, and the new Part 3 supplement on Engineered Repairs and Alterations. The National Board & ASME Guide for the NDE quality-system review questions and the treatment of subcontracted NDE.

name: API Standard 510, Pressure Vessel Inspection Code: In-service Inspection, Rating, Repair, and Alteration — Owner-User Inspection Programme
jurisdiction: United States — adopted internationally and by some US state jurisdictions
authority: American Petroleum Institute. API's Individual Certification Programs (ICP) office certifies the Authorized Pressure Vessel Inspector; the inspection programme itself is owned and enforced by the owner-user, and by the boiler and pressure vessel jurisdiction where the state has adopted API 510
appliesTo: NDT firms and contract inspection agencies serving refinery, chemical and gas-processing owner-users. The programme belongs to the owner-user, but the examiner hours, the NDE procedures, the Level III and frequently the Authorized Inspector are bought in. It reaches any firm supplying thickness measurement, weld examination, on-stream inspection or turnaround inspection on in-service pressure vessels, and any firm signing inspection reports that feed the owner-user's mechanical integrity file.
summary: API 510 is not a certificate a service company holds; it is the owner-user's programme, and it defines the roles your people fill. It separates the API Authorized Pressure Vessel Inspector, who holds API's central certification and evaluates results against the code, from the examiner, who performs the nondestructive examination and does not evaluate against API 510 unless specifically trained and authorised to do so by the owner-user. Selling into this regime means selling examiner hours plus the paperwork that makes them admissible: an accepted written practice, Level III-approved procedures, current examiner certifications and calibrated equipment. Inspection types are external visual, internal or on-stream, and thickness measurement, each running on its own interval cap, and each producing records the owner-user must be able to defend.
personnelCertification: Split, and the split is the commercial point. The Authorized Pressure Vessel Inspector must hold API 510 certification — a central, third-party certification examined by API and delivered through Prometric. No employer can issue it and no outsourced Level III can substitute for it. The NDE examiner side is entirely employer-based: examiners are certified under an employer's written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, ANSI/ASNT CP-189 or ACCP, so an outsourced Level III can write and approve the method procedures, administer and grade examinations and recommend certification, with the employer's designated certifying authority signing. API additionally operates ultrasonic examiner qualification programmes — QUTE, QUSE, QUSE-PA and QUPA — that some owner-users specify on top of ASNT certification for corrosion mapping and weld phased array.
requiredDocuments: Owner-user inspection programme document naming the Authorized Inspector and defining what the examiner is authorised to evaluate
Current API 510 certificate for each Authorized Pressure Vessel Inspector, with the recertification due date
NDE written practice, and the Level III approval on each method procedure
Examiner certification records and current annual eye examinations
Thickness measurement location and condition monitoring location drawings, and the full reading history against those identifiers
Corrosion rate and remaining-life calculations supporting the next inspection date
Inspection report signed by the Authorized Inspector, kept distinct from the examiner's data report
Repair and alteration records, including welding procedure specifications, procedure qualification records and the Authorized Inspector's acceptance
Equipment calibration records and certification of ultrasonic calibration blocks
auditProcess: Owner-user issues the inspection programme and defines the scope of contracted work
Contractor's written practice, NDE procedures and personnel records are reviewed and accepted by the owner-user's Authorized Inspector before mobilisation
Pre-job qualification on site: examiner certificates, eye examinations and equipment calibration verified
Examination performed to procedure — the examiner records data, the Authorized Inspector evaluates it against API 510
Inspection report issued, remaining life and next inspection date calculated, and any repair or alteration approved by the Authorized Inspector
Contractor records tested in the owner-user's or a third party's audit, usually inside a PSM mechanical-integrity or supplier audit, because API does not audit inspection companies
renewal: There is no company certificate to renew. The individual API 510 certificate runs for a three-year term. Recertification requires that the inspector has spent a minimum of 20% of his time over the most recent three-year certification period performing or supervising inspection activities, and has completed 24 CPD hours within each three-year cycle; an online open-book quiz of 25 questions with a four-hour limit is required every six years. API's published fees for the 510, 570 and 653 programmes are $875 USD for members and $1,125 for non-members for initial certification, $745 and $855 for recertification, and $350 to reschedule an exam. The 2026 API 510 exam windows are 2–23 January and 8–29 May 2026.
commonFindings: Examiner taking thickness readings and also signing the evaluation against API 510 without written authorisation from the owner-user
Inspector certificate expired, or CPD hours not documented for the three-year cycle
Thickness data reported with no corrosion rate and no remaining-life calculation, so the next inspection date has no basis
NDE procedure that does not cover the technique actually used — a generic manual UT procedure used for encoded corrosion mapping is the common case
Repeated identical thickness readings year on year with no explanation of how the data was taken
Level III approval on a procedure with no evidence that the Level III's own certification is current
Contractor's written practice never formally accepted by the owner-user before work started
External visual, internal or on-stream, and thickness measurement intervals tracked in separate systems, so the shortest governing cap is missed
sources: API 510 certification page, api.org, accessed 21 August 2026 — verified for the education and experience eligibility ladder (BS or 3+ years military technical service plus 1 year; 2-year degree or 2 years military plus 2 years; high school diploma plus 3 years; no formal education plus 5+ years, each with a supervision component), the 7.5-hour exam day, 170 questions of which 140 are scored, split 110 closed-book and 60 open-book, the three-year recertification cycle, the 20% time requirement, 24 CPD hours per three-year cycle and the 25-question web quiz every six years. API ICP Schedules & Fees page — verified for $875/$1,125 initial, $745/$855 recertification, $350 reschedule, and the 2026 exam windows. API ICP Policies page — verified that the term of certification is three years and the open-book quiz is required every six years for 510, 570, 653, 936 and 1169. API Standard 510 announcement page — confirms the 11th edition, which added a detailed section for the analysis of inspection results; the October 2022 publication date comes from reseller listings, not from API's own page. Inspection-interval caps commonly cited for the 11th edition (internal or on-stream at the lesser of half the remaining corrosion life or ten years; external visual at the lesser of five years or the internal/on-stream interval) were cross-checked against two independent secondary summaries and NOT against the code text — confirm against API 510 before publishing them as figures.

name: API Standard 570, Piping Inspection Code: In-service Inspection, Rating, Repair, and Alteration of Piping Systems — Owner-User Piping Inspection Programme
jurisdiction: United States — adopted internationally and used by owner-users worldwide
authority: American Petroleum Institute. API's Individual Certification Programs office certifies the Authorized Piping Inspector; the piping inspection programme is owned and enforced by the owner-user, and audited by the owner-user or by OSHA under process safety management
appliesTo: Contractors inspecting in-service metallic and fibreglass-reinforced plastic process piping and its associated pressure-relieving devices. It excludes specialty equipment — instrumentation, exchanger tubes and control valves. Piping retired from service and abandoned in place falls outside the code; piping that is temporarily out of service but mothballed stays inside it. Any firm supplying thickness readings, corrosion-under-insulation surveys, injection-point inspection or weld examination on process piping is working to this code.
summary: API 570 is built around circuits, not vessels, and that changes what a service provider must deliver. Piping is classified by consequence of failure, condition monitoring locations are the unit of record, and the code singles out injection points, dead legs, small-bore piping, corrosion under insulation and soil-to-air interfaces as the places programmes fail. The code is explicitly written for outsourcing: it states it is intended for use by organizations that maintain or have access to an authorized inspection agency, a repair organization, and technically qualified piping engineers, inspectors and examiners, all as defined in its definitions section. The Authorized Piping Inspector must hold API 570 certification. The examiner performing the NDE need not, and normally does not.
personnelCertification: The same split as API 510, with one distinctive feature. The Authorized Piping Inspector holds API's central, third-party API 570 certification, which no employer can issue. The examiner is certified by his employer under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, ANSI/ASNT CP-189 or ACCP, so an outsourced Level III can own the written practice, approve the procedures and certify the technicians. The distinctive feature is that the API 570 body of knowledge itself teaches the inspector ASME Section V Articles 1, 2, 6, 7, 9, 10 and Article 23 SE-797 — the inspector is expected to audit your procedures, not merely receive your results. API's QUTE, QUSE, QUSE-PA and QUPA ultrasonic examiner qualifications are increasingly specified for piping corrosion mapping and weld phased array.
requiredDocuments: Owner-user piping inspection programme with the piping circuit list and each circuit's class designation
Current API 570 certificate for each Authorized Piping Inspector
Isometric drawings with condition monitoring locations and thickness measurement locations permanently identified
Injection point, dead leg, small-bore piping and corrosion-under-insulation inspection registers
NDE written practice, Level III-approved method procedures and examiner certification records
Thickness data history with both short-term and long-term corrosion rates calculated
Inspection reports signed by the Authorized Piping Inspector
Repair, alteration and rerating records including welding procedure specifications, procedure qualification records and pressure test records
Insulation removal and reinstatement records supporting corrosion-under-insulation inspection
auditProcess: Piping circuits defined and each circuit assigned a class by consequence of failure; the class drives the maximum interval and the density of condition monitoring locations
Contract scope written against the circuit list; the contractor's written practice, procedures and examiner records accepted by the owner-user before mobilisation
Isometrics and CML/TML identification verified on site — the most common single source of data that cannot afterwards be trended
Examination performed to procedure, with readings recorded against the permanent CML identifier rather than the line number
Authorized Piping Inspector evaluates the data, computes short-term and long-term corrosion rates and sets the next interval
Findings on injection points, dead legs, corrosion under insulation and soil-to-air interfaces reported separately, because these are the areas the code singles out and the areas audits target
industries: Terminals and pipelines within plant boundaries
renewal: No company certificate. The individual API 570 certificate runs three years, on the same ICP rules as API 510: at least 20% of time over the certification period performing or supervising inspection, 24 CPD hours per three-year cycle, and a 25-question open-book web quiz every six years. Published fees are $875 USD member and $1,125 non-member for initial certification, $745 and $855 for recertification, and $350 to reschedule. The 2026 API 570 exam windows are 6–27 February and 5–26 June 2026. The code itself is on API's own revision cycle; the 5th edition is current.
commonFindings: Readings recorded against a line number rather than a permanent condition monitoring location identifier, so no corrosion rate can be trended
Injection points and dead legs not maintained on a separate register with their own shorter intervals
Corrosion-under-insulation inspection reported with no record of where insulation was actually removed
Class 1 piping inspected on a Class 2 interval because the circuit was never reclassified after a service change
Ultrasonic procedure written for plate used on small-bore piping with no technique addressing curvature and wall thickness
Examiner certified in ultrasonics generally with no documented qualification for the encoded or mapping technique actually used
Only one corrosion rate calculated, so the governing rate between short-term and long-term is not identified
Inspector certificate current but the programme still written to a superseded edition of API 570
sources: API 570 Body of Knowledge for the February, June and October 2026 exams, api.org — verified for the reference publication list (API 570; API RP 571, 574, 576, 577 and 578; ASME Section V, Section IX, B16.5, B31.3 and PCC-2), for the ASME Section V Articles in scope (Article 1 general requirements including owner/user and subcontractor responsibilities, calibration, the definitions of inspection and examination and record keeping; Article 2 radiographic; Article 6 liquid penetrant with mandatory appendices II and III; Article 7 magnetic particle, yoke and prod only; Article 9 visual; Article 10 leak testing with mandatory appendix I; Article 23 SE-797 ultrasonic thickness), and for the ASME PCC-2 articles examined. API 570 4th edition publisher's preview, api.org — verified for the scope statement, the exclusion of instrumentation, exchanger tubes and control valves, the treatment of abandoned versus mothballed piping, and the statement that the code is intended for organizations that maintain or have access to an authorized inspection agency, a repair organization, and technically qualified piping engineers, inspectors and examiners as defined in Section 3. API Standard 570 announcement page confirms the 5th edition; the February 2024 date comes from reseller listings. API ICP Schedules & Fees for fees and 2026 exam windows. The class-based maximum thickness-measurement and external-visual intervals were not verified against the 5th edition text and are therefore described here without figures.

name: API Standard 653, Tank Inspection, Repair, Alteration, and Reconstruction — Aboveground Storage Tank Inspection Programme
jurisdiction: United States — adopted internationally and referenced in several US state aboveground storage tank programmes
authority: American Petroleum Institute is the certifying agency for the Authorized Inspector under the code's normative Authorized Inspector Certification annex; the inspection programme is owned by the tank owner-operator and, where the state has adopted API 653, overseen by the state environmental or fire-safety authority
appliesTo: Tank inspection and NDT firms working steel storage tanks built to API 650 and its predecessor API 12C, and by extension any steel tank the owner-operator elects to maintain to this standard. Scope runs from the foundation, bottom, shell, structure and roof to attached appurtenances and nozzles up to the face of the first flange, first threaded joint or first welding-end connection. Floor-scanning contractors, shell UT crews and reconstruction inspectors are all inside it.
summary: API 653 is the one code in this set that names an independent contract organization as an acceptable authorized inspection agency, so a tank inspection company can itself be the AIA for an owner-operator — a materially different commercial position from API 510 or 570.
